title: Challenges, Stable Operations and Future-Oriented Development: Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis Reviews 2024
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 13. janvāris, 2025 Challenges, Stable Operations and Future-Oriented Development: Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis Reviews 2024 The Liepāja SEZ Authority has summarised its results for 2024. Businesses implemented four significant new investment projects with a combined value exceeding approximately EUR 128 million. An important declaration was signed on establishing the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. The centre is directly linked to at least seven development projects involving renewable resources, their processing and the manufacture of new products using the latest scientific research and technologies. Cargo turnover at the Port of Liepāja slightly exceeded 7 million tonnes in 2024. Chairman of the Liepāja SEZ Board Uldis Sesks: “The year 2024 showed that we have learned to overcome various obstacles and develop new ideas together with entrepreneurs, turning them into reality. We plan for tomorrow and work today, but for almost 30 years our priority has remained unchanged: jobs, and well-paid jobs. They increase the city’s budget and prosperity, creating opportunities for a better life and investment in healthcare, education, culture, sport and public utilities, as well as support for people receiving assistance from social services.” Investment projects completed in 2024 demonstrate the quality of the Liepāja SEZ business environment: the Syfud fish processing facility (approximately EUR 80 million invested, Lithuania), a water terminal in Liepāja (approximately EUR 30 million, Cyprus), the Golden Fields Factory LV protein production plant (approximately EUR 16 million, United Arab Emirates), and Norplast Piemare’s large-scale fibreglass structure production facility in the port (approximately EUR 2.5 million, Norway). At the same time, manufacturing and port companies continue to operate steadily, develop and build new factories and terminals. Importantly, construction began in 2024 at the Liepāja Industrial Park on the site of the former steelworks. In addition, several strategic investors joined the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), Liepāja City Council, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Riga Technical University (RTU) in signing an important declaration on the establishment of the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis: “In a sense, 2024 was a turning point. We deliberately moved from ideas to action, planning business development with the future in mind: an offshore wind energy support base, a hydrogen production plant, a sustainable aviation fuel plant and the assembly of hydrogen-powered aircraft, while continuing to support the operations and development of existing manufacturing and port businesses.” The transport and logistics sector has undergone substantial changes for some time, directly affecting cargo turnover at the port. Operating conditions remain uncertain, but stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja have adapted. In 2024, they handled slightly more than 7 million tonnes of cargo, a volume comparable to 2023. Ro-ro cargo, timber and energy-related cargo increased, while agricultural products declined. Āris Ozoliņš, head of the Association of Port of Liepāja Tenants and a board member of the Latvian Stevedoring Companies Association, noted that businesses faced no shortage of challenges in 2024. As head of LSEZ SIA “Terrabalt”, he emphasised that the greatest challenge this year is launching the reconstruction of the ferry berth. “This is not only about developing ferry transport, but about preserving it. Berth No. 46 was built 60 years ago and is physically and functionally outdated. Its reconstruction could increase cargo turnover by as much as one million tonnes per year.” At the very end of 2024, the first new production facility within the Liepāja SEZ port area was commissioned; it was the 26th facility built in the past seven years. The new LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare plant manufactures large fibreglass structures and is located at Berth No. 64 of the Port of Liepāja, 37 Atslēdznieku Street, Liepāja. The facility covers 1,935 m², and approximately EUR 2.5 million was invested in the project. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Auction Announced for Property at Eksporta Street 3 in the Liepāja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 06. oktobris, 2026 Auction Announced for Property at Eksporta Street 3 in the Liepāja Industrial Park As development of the Liepāja Industrial Park continues on the site of the former Liepājas metalurgs steelworks, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Authority has announced an auction for the property at 3 Eksporta Street, located within the industrial park. This is the next step towards involving businesses in the revitalisation and transformation of the industrial area, offering the opportunity to acquire existing production buildings together with the land. The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority is organising an ascending-bid electronic auction for a newly formed property at 3 Eksporta Street, Liepāja. Auction property: Address: 3 Eksporta Street, Liepāja Land: total area 51,521 m² The plot contains buildings, including warehouses of various sizes, a production workshop, a workshop building and other structures. Starting price: EUR 680,000.00 Bid increment: EUR 6,800.00 Security deposit: EUR 68,000.00 Auction conditions to consider: The building(s) must be renovated or reconstructed, and the site improved, within 60 (sixty) months of signing the purchase agreement; The buildings must meet the minimum energy efficiency requirements stipulated by the laws and regulations of the Republic of Latvia; At least EUR 733,076.85 (seven hundred thirty-three thousand seventy-six euros and 85 cents) must be invested in the auction property. The auction opens on 6 October 2026 at 13:00 and closes on 5 November 2026 at 13:00. Bidders may register between 6 October 2026 at 13:00 and 26 October 2026 at 23:59 on the electronic auction website: https://izsoles.ta.gov.lv. The auction takes place electronically at: https://izsoles.ta.gov.lv. The Liepāja SEZ Authority first consolidated all properties on the site of the former Liepājas metalurgs plant, worked with the municipality to develop a local spatial plan, and constructed the first streets with the necessary utilities. Selling properties through auctions is the next step in involving entrepreneurs in regenerating and transforming the industrial site. It offers them the opportunity to acquire existing production buildings with land and renovate or reconstruct them to meet the requirements of a modern green-economy business environment. The Liepāja Industrial Park is located in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. It is intended for modern manufacturing, science and research, logistics centres and energy-intensive projects. The development area of approximately 120 hectares is divided into plots with building opportunities and access to utilities. The Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas metalurgs site between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets in Liepāja. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected Natura 2000 site. Under the approved development strategy, the aim is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 new jobs. Sustainability is embedded in the industrial park’s guiding principles, with a clear focus on education, innovation and the circular economy. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: A New Procurement Procedure Will Be Announced for the Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. maijs, 2026 A New Procurement Procedure Will Be Announced for the Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja Following changes to the amount of EU Structural Funds financing available, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has decided to cancel the previously announced procurement procedure for the reconstruction of Berth No. 46. It will prepare updated technical specifications and launch a new procurement procedure this week, first consulting interested tenderers and subsequently inviting them to submit bids. The Liepāja Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Authority continues to implement the project “Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja” (the Project). Its aim is to reconstruct the berth to ensure the safe handling of ferries at the port, including ferries used for military mobility. The original solution, in accordance with the construction design prepared by CHR Design Solutions Ltd, envisaged reconstructing the berth and installing shore-side electricity supply and polluted-water collection facilities for vessels. On 9 October 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded a grant agreement with the European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) for the project “Ensuring Safe Mooring of Ro-Ro Ferries at the Port of Liepāja”, worth EUR 6,927,015. To implement the project in full, an additional EUR 10,662,546 in EU Cohesion Fund financing was planned. In January 2026, discussions with CINEA established that Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) financing could not be combined with financing from other EU funds. Therefore, on 22 April 2026, the Liepāja SEZ Board decided to terminate the grant agreement, eliminating any risk of double financing associated with implementation of the Project. On 24 April 2026, the Liepāja SEZ Authority submitted a Project application under the 2021–2027 EU Cohesion Policy Programme, Priority 3.3 “Strengthening Military Mobility — Railways and Ports”, Specific Objective 3.3.1, Measure 3.3.1.2 “Development of Dual-Use Public Infrastructure in Major Ports”. As a result, public funding available for the Project will not exceed EUR 10,662,546. In view of the potential reduction in available public financing to EUR 10.66 million, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has optimised the scope of the reconstruction of Berth No. 46 while ensuring that the berth can accommodate two military ferries and meet the applicable requirements for military mobility infrastructure projects, including the criteria for adapting civilian infrastructure for military use. According to the Project application, reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja will include: Reconstruction of the berth, including the necessary dredging and reinforcement of the basin bed on its northern side; Reconstruction of the berth superstructure; Construction of three mooring platforms; Construction of the transport infrastructure required for berth operations; Construction of the electrical supply, stormwater drainage and firefighting systems required for berth operations, without installing shore-side electricity supply or polluted-water collection equipment for vessels; Construction of cargo ramps, consisting of one fixed and one hydraulic ramp. Based on calculations by the Liepāja SEZ Authority, the provisional total cost of the Project is EUR 18,000,000.00, of which EUR 7,337,454.00 will be co-financed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority. title: First Auction Announced for the Sale of an Industrial Building in Liepāja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. jūlijs, 2025 First Auction Announced for the Sale of an Industrial Building in Liepāja Industrial Park As development of the Liepāja Industrial Park continues on the site of the former Liepājas metalurgs plant, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Authority has announced its first property auction. This is the next step in involving businesses in renewing and transforming the industrial area, offering the opportunity to purchase production buildings. The auction will run from 29 July to 28 August 2025. “We initially consolidated all properties on the former Liepājas metalurgs site, developed a local spatial plan and began constructing streets and utility networks. The area is gradually being reintegrated into the city, making it accessible to the public and attractive to investors. It already contains various industrial buildings, for which we will seek new owners through auctions, owners who will renovate and rebuild them to suit a modern green-economy business environment,” says Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis. Auction property: Address: 98A Brīvības Street, Liepāja Land: total area 5,132 m² Existing building: steam workshop, total area 2,239 m² Starting price: EUR 142,000 Bid increment: EUR 1,420 As Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš said when construction began at the Liepāja Industrial Park: “By demolishing the old gatehouse, which once controlled entry to the Liepājas metalurgs site, we are symbolically turning a new page in Liepāja’s industrial history. I hope that, in the years to come, this area will become one of the strongest green industrial parks in Latvia.” The Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed on the site of the former Liepājas metalurgs plant, for which a local spatial plan has been prepared. The development covers approximately 120 hectares and includes the construction of eight new streets, which are planned to be opened to public access. Phase 1 of the project “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure” is being implemented using EUR 10 million in funding from the Recovery and Resilience Facility, in accordance with the prepared design. Following the procurement results, A-Land will carry out two construction projects and CTB Ltd one. The project involves constructing three sections of streets with utilities (water supply, domestic wastewater drainage, stormwater drainage and district heating networks). At the same time, AS Sadales tīkls is installing the electricity distribution networks. The Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas metalurgs site between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets in Liepāja. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected Natura 2000 site. Under the approved development strategy, the aim is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 new jobs. title: Procurement Announced for Design Documentation and Author Supervision for the Access Road at 6 Roņu Street
text: 21. augusts, 2024 Procurement Announced for Design Documentation and Author Supervision for the Access Road at 6 Roņu Street The Liepāja SEZ Authority continues to develop infrastructure needed by fishermen at the Port of Liepāja and has announced procurement for preparation of an explanatory design report and author supervision for the project “Construction of an Access Road at 6 Roņu Street, Liepāja” — an access road to the fish-landing area at Berths No. 92A and 92B. The project envisages developing infrastructure for fishermen by constructing an access road from Roņu Street to the fish-landing area at Berths No. 92A and 92B, including road lighting, stormwater drainage networks and landscaping of the surrounding area. The design and author supervision work will be carried out and financed under the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund, within the 2023–2027 Action Plan of the Fisheries Development Programme 2021–2027, through the measure “Implementation of Community-Led Local Development Strategies”, Action 4.1 M4/R1, eligible activity “Strengthening the Development of Port Infrastructure”. Information on submitting a tender is available on the Liepāja SEZ Authority website: https://liepaja-sez.lv/lv/iepirkumi-un-izsoles/paskaidrojuma-raksta-izstrade-un-autoruzraudziba-objektam-piebraucama-cela-izbuve. Under an open call for project applications within the Fisheries Development Programme 2021–2027, with the strategic objective of providing a modern port for fisheries, the Liepāja SEZ Authority prepared and submitted three project applications concerning Berths No. 92A and 92B and construction of an access road from Roņu Street to the fish-landing area at these berths. Fishing is one of the traditional industries at the Port of Liepāja. EU regulatory documents and Latvian government support recognise coastal fishing as an industry to be preserved, with public funding allocated for this purpose. During the previous EU programming period, from 2017 to 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority implemented Phases 1, 2 and 3 of the Rural Support Service project “Improving Infrastructure Needed by Fishermen at the Port of Liepāja”. Total financing amounted to EUR 3.87 million. Phase 1 — reconstruction of the Old Harbour waterfront between Uliha Street and Celtnieku Street: Replacement of the road surface; Construction of new underground utility networks and reconstruction of existing ones; Landscaping and improvement of the surrounding area. Construction started in July 2017 and was completed at the end of 2017. Cost: EUR 1.1 million. Phase 3 — “Construction of a Vehicle Parking Area in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone at 12 Muitas Street, Liepāja”: Demolition of two old warehouses; Construction of parking facilities for trucks and passenger vehicles; Landscaping of the area. The project was implemented in 2019 at a cost of EUR 246,100. Phase 2 — “Improving Infrastructure Needed by Fishermen at the Port of Liepāja”: On the Old Liepāja side, reconstruction of Berths No. 83, 85, 86 and 87, and improvement of a 360-metre section of street; On the New Liepāja side, renovation of Berths No. 71 and 72, and improvement of a 240-metre section of street; Reconstruction of an 800-metre section of Atslēdznieku Street. Fish-landing areas were improved at all berths, together with transport access for fishermen. Construction was completed in early 2023 at a total cost of EUR 2.6 million. Was this information useful? title: Liepāja Marina Concludes an Active Sailing Season
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 04. novembris, 2024 Liepāja Marina Concludes an Active Sailing Season The active yachting season traditionally ends on 1 November. This year Liepāja Marina welcomed 243 yachts, 15 more than last year. The number of yachts served increased in every month except July, traditionally one of the busiest months. Most visiting yachts still came from Lithuania and Poland, but yachts also arrived from faraway countries such as Chile, Australia and New Zealand. Sailing patterns in the Baltic Sea have changed in recent years due to several external factors, initially the COVID pandemic and more recently the geopolitical situation. Russia’s aggression against Ukraine has affected yacht traffic: although the war does not directly involve the Baltic Sea region, security concerns have discouraged sailors from many countries from making voyages. According to marina manager Kārlis Kints, the number of yachts served exceeded the previous year’s figure, and yachts often stay for more than one night. “That is good, because it means sailors like Liepāja. It is excellent publicity for our services and for the city.” He also noted that the end of the season is largely symbolic: any yacht that sails to Liepāja will still be welcomed. This season the marina’s berths hosted numerous sailing vessels stopping in Liepāja on their way to regattas, while training young sailors or simply enjoying sailing. During the Sea Festival, the Liepāja SEZ Authority brought together sea-going and inland-water vessels at the marina for a lively parade that has become a popular tradition among participants and spectators alike. The event “Across the City, from the Lake to the Sea” was held for the sixth time. Statistics show that sailors from Lithuania, Poland, Germany and the Scandinavian countries were once again the most frequent visitors to Liepāja. The longest journeys were made by vessels from the United States, New Zealand, Australia, Chile and the Marshall Islands. As usual, the marina was busiest in the three summer months, serving 64 yachts in June, 70 in July and 57 in August. Background: The Liepāja SEZ Authority took over management of the marina in 2015. Its reconstruction began in 2020, with new infrastructure including a new service building, improving the quality of services available to sailors. As in previous years, in 2024 Liepāja Marina was the only marina in Latvia entitled to fly the Blue Flag, the symbol of environmental and service quality. Was this information useful? title: The Blue Flag Has Been Raised at Liepāja Marina for 18 Years
text: 28. maijs, 2025 The Blue Flag Has Been Raised at Liepāja Marina for 18 Years The Blue Flag has been raised at Liepāja Marina for 18 years. It is the only marina in Latvia to have fulfilled all the criteria required to receive this internationally recognised environmental quality certification. This year the Blue Flag was raised at the marina on 26 May. Marina manager Kārlis Kints was joined in raising the flag by former Latvian Prime Minister and Member of Parliament Māris Kučinskis. As the marina manager told those attending the ceremony, sailors appreciate Liepāja because the new marina complex is convenient and located in the very centre of the city. Yachts that have visited Liepāja before are returning increasingly often. Their crews particularly value both the city’s development and the amenities offered by the marina completed in 2020. In 2023 the marina welcomed 228 yachts, while in 2024 it received 243 yachts and sailing vessels. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Dan Store Latvija Terminal Has Operated Successfully at the Port of Liepāja for 25 Years
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 12. jūnijs, 2024 Dan Store Latvija Terminal Has Operated Successfully at the Port of Liepāja for 25 Years The Dan Store terminal handles exports of agricultural produce and imports of animal feed. It offers customers flexible logistics solutions through direct rail access, modern infrastructure and equipment operated by experienced professionals. In 2023 the company recorded a turnover of EUR 6.7 million. LSEZ SIA Dan Store was among the first companies to transform from a cargo owner into a Port of Liepāja terminal with extensive warehousing shortly after the Liepāja Special Economic Zone was established. Through gradual investment in development, Dan Store has become one of the largest bulk cargo handling and storage terminals. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasises that nothing stood where the Dan Store terminal is now located. “There were ruins left behind by the military port, without infrastructure or anything we see here today. Year after year, several warehouses have been built, substantial investments made and cargo flows established. The volume is significant — more than 600,000 tonnes each year. The cargo mix changes: one year there are more agricultural products, another year more wood pellets for heating. It varies from year to year, but it is very important for the Port of Liepāja.” Ibs Henrichsen, General Manager of LSEZ SIA Dan Store, says: “Liepāja is a good place to work, where cooperation is easy. As far as I know, Dan Store has a good reputation in Latvia. Many of the people who were here when we began developing the business still work for us, right from the beginning.” The company currently employs 29 people. Although handling agricultural cargo has become more automated, with many tasks performed by computer systems, human involvement remains essential. Kaspars Skrīvers has managed the Dan Store terminal for 19 years. “We work around the clock. We have four shifts, four teams rotating every 12 hours. Staff are always present at the terminal. When cargo is not being handled, there is maintenance work to do. There is always plenty of work.” Dan Store Latvija was founded in 1999. Its largest shareholder is Copenhagen Merchants, which joined existing shareholders Bunge and Svane Shipping in 2009. The terminal imports and exports agricultural cargo, working with partners in several European countries, the United States, Argentina and Brazil. The company was originally attracted to Liepāja by its favourable geographical position, ice-free port, rail infrastructure and motivated workforce. Dan Store currently stores grain, animal feed and other agricultural cargo in six silos with a capacity of 22,000 tonnes and three warehouses with a combined capacity of 65,000 tonnes. title: The “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition Takes Place This Weekend
text: 29. janvāris, 2025 The “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition Takes Place This Weekend Liepāja manufactures a wide range of products. The “Made in Liepāja” exhibition takes place this weekend, on 31 January and 1 February, giving everyone an opportunity to see what Liepāja’s businesses produce. Alongside the exhibition, a conference will discuss business today and in the future, local innovation projects and sustainable solutions. Liepāja manufactures heavy, large-scale equipment needed at airports, in construction and industry; electronic control systems used on ships; components for the automotive industry; and even breathing apparatus for firefighters around the world. Export goods are made both in factories and in industrial parks. Liepāja has preserved its manufacturing traditions while developing new ones, and is now working to become a centre for sustainable industry using technologies developed by scientists and researchers. Liepāja is Latvia’s second-largest manufacturing city after Riga. It contributes significantly to the economy and to the country’s gross domestic product. title: New Jensen Metal Facility Is the Fifth Factory in Karosta Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 04. aprīlis, 2025 New Jensen Metal Facility Is the Fifth Factory in Karosta Industrial Park On 28 March this year, the Building Authority Commission of Liepāja City Municipality approved the new Jensen Metal production building at Karosta Industrial Park for use. The new facility was constructed next to two existing Jensen Metal plants. The company provides around 450 competitively paid jobs, contributes significantly to national GDP growth and supports the city’s economic development. The new 5,968 m² production facility will increase the company’s capacity to manufacture stainless-steel products, improve and modernise the working environment, and help it serve customers even more efficiently with high-quality products. The new plant at 11 Virssardzes Street, at the junction of Beverīnas and Lazaretes streets, complements the metalworking company’s two existing modern manufacturing and office buildings: its ferrous-metal and fittings plant at 11 Virssardzes Street, which opened in 2019, and its stainless-steel plant at 34 Ģenerāļa Baloža Street, opened in 2022. LSEZ Jensen Metal SIA was the first company willing to build production facilities in Karosta Industrial Park. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis says: “The investments made in Karosta Industrial Park to improve the site and build utility infrastructure have paid off. We can see that Karosta, once used by the military and left with degraded land, has become home to modern manufacturers providing well-paid jobs, supporting the development of this part of the city. Now we must take the next step and develop the former Liepājas metalurgs plant site in the same way if we want to attract world-class manufacturers using innovative technologies. We have launched a development project covering utilities, lighting, streets, pedestrian routes, cycle paths and a green recreation area. What was achieved in Karosta must also be achieved at the former Liepājas metalurgs site.” The idea of creating Karosta Industrial Park dates back to 1999. The aim was to generate new jobs, increase tax revenues for the city and state, and provide additional funding for education, culture, sport and other projects. Building new factories in Karosta was not feasible and investors were not attracted to the site until 2015, when the municipality, together with the Liepāja SEZ Authority, prepared approximately 20 hectares of land for business use. After the bankruptcy of Liepājas metalurgs, solutions were sought to address unemployment. In 2014, European Regional Development Fund financing was secured for the project “Development of Business Areas and the Necessary Public Infrastructure in Liepāja”. It included regenerating degraded land and building utility networks and public street infrastructure, including lighting, pedestrian paths and cycle paths. Was this information useful? title: New SyFud Plant in Liepāja Will Significantly Increase Latvia’s Fish Processing Export Capacity
text: 01. novembris, 2024 New SyFud Plant in Liepāja Will Significantly Increase Latvia’s Fish Processing Export Capacity The opening of the new SyFud plant in Liepāja will substantially increase and diversify Latvia’s fish processing production and export capacity. The fish-processing factory opened on 31 October, following total investments of approximately EUR 80 million in infrastructure and technologies. Over time, its annual production value could reach EUR 250 million. SIA Syfud, operating under the Port Lite brand, acquired the site of the former Liepāja fish-canning factory in 2020 and began a major investment project implemented in several phases. Three production buildings have now been constructed and equipped with new, modern machinery ensuring a safe, environmentally responsible and efficient fish-processing operation. “Latvia, and Liepāja in particular, has longstanding and robust fish-processing traditions. We are proud to work in both this sector and this city, but it also brings great responsibility. Our aim in planning the Liepāja factory was to produce new, modern fish products demanded in European and other Western markets. We will not compete with traditional Latvian fish processors; instead, we specialise in new products, contributing to Liepāja, the industry and Latvia’s economy as a whole,” says company owner Sigits Ambrazevičs. Minister of Agriculture Armands Krauze says: “The new fish-processing plant in Liepāja is the result of successful implementation of Latvia’s fisheries development policy, which makes it possible to channel substantial, targeted EU support towards investment and development in Latvia. It is equally important that EU-supported investment reaches the regions, helping the industry grow more evenly across the country. Liepāja has always been one of Latvia’s fish-processing centres, and I am pleased that, thanks to entrepreneurs and EU funding, fish processing and fishing continue to thrive here. EU support and projects like this provide a good example for both established and aspiring entrepreneurs who wish to modernise or start businesses that can contribute not only to fisheries but to the entire economy and employment.” Syfud produces two main categories of goods: crab sticks and other surimi products, and salmon products. At full capacity, the factory will be able to produce 1,000 tonnes of surimi and 1,000 tonnes of salmon products each month, reaching turnover of up to EUR 250 million annually. Output will be increased gradually: crab-stick production began in 2021, and the installed lines are expected to reach full capacity within three years. The overwhelming majority of Syfud products are intended for export, with approximately 10% potentially remaining in the Baltic market. The main export destinations are Germany, France, Italy, Spain and other EU countries; discussions are also under way with partners in the United States. To maintain consistently high quality and meet customer demand, the factory uses state-of-the-art equipment from Marel, Reich and Multivac, employs experienced, highly qualified specialists and will source production raw materials from Norway and the United States. “The efficient balance between product quality and cost enables Syfud to rank among Europe’s top three smoked-salmon producers. This means a new, large and highly competitive player is entering the processed-salmon market, bringing additional capacity and value to Latvia’s fish-processing industry,” says S. Ambrazevičs. The Syfud factory currently employs 150 people. The workforce is expected to grow to 200 by the end of the year and to around 800 by the end of 2027, when the plant is expected to reach full production capacity. “The new Syfud fish-processing plant is an ambitious project that revives Liepāja’s fish-processing traditions and creates hundreds of new jobs. Through large-scale investment and cutting-edge production technologies, it strengthens our city as a regional centre for the economy and innovation and improves Latvia’s competitiveness on world markets,” says Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis says: “Syfud is the 25th factory built in the Liepāja SEZ over the past seven years and one of two operating in food production. Each new factory demonstrates the quality of Liepāja’s business environment and creates jobs that make a significant contribution to the city budget, helping establish Liepāja as an important centre not only for the regional economy but also for education, culture and sport.” The factory’s salmon range includes smoked, salted and frozen salmon and trout products supplied in various packages, including vacuum packs and modified-atmosphere packaging (MAP). Salmon is sourced from organic and wild fisheries as well. Its surimi range includes sticks, pieces, shrimp-style products, and other fresh and frozen products in vacuum or alternative packaging. “We will have almost everything you can imagine that retailers and food-service businesses might need,” adds S. Ambrazevičs. More than EUR 75 million excluding VAT has been invested in building and equipping the new factory. The project was co-financed through the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund measure “Processing of Fishery and Aquaculture Products”, administered by the Rural Support Service, as well as financing from Rietumu Banka. “To build a factory on this scale, investments — including EU funding in this case — are only one prerequisite. Behind it all are people with an idea, an understanding of how a modern company should operate and the determination to compete in European and global markets. Fisheries is a sector whose products can proudly carry Latvia’s name around the world. I wish the company continued growth,” says Indulis Āboliņš, Acting Director of the Rural Support Service. Jeļena Buraja, Chair of the Management Board of Rietumu Banka, emphasises: “Financing local businesses is a cornerstone of our bank’s strategy, and manufacturing has a special place in it. I am convinced manufacturers must receive support, because they create added value and jobs, expand export potential and generate tax revenue. Such companies are crucial to the development of the economy and the whole country; they foster growth in Latvia’s regions and improve people’s welfare. I wish the new factory success and hope that very soon the people of Liepāja, and all of us in Latvia, will be proud of its achievements.” SIA Syfud is a Latvian-registered company with Lithuanian capital. Its sole owner and ultimate beneficial owner is Sigits Ambrazevičs, a well-known Lithuanian entrepreneur with more than 25 years of experience in seafood processing and trade. title: How to Create Greater Added Value from Renewable Wind Energy
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 25. aprīlis, 2025 How to Create Greater Added Value from Renewable Wind Energy With lively discussions about offshore wind industry development in the region and ways to use renewable energy to generate greater added value for the national economy, the Baltic region’s leading wind energy conference, “Wind Works’ 2025”, concluded in Riga on 24 April. Participants again highlighted Liepāja as the most strategically advantageous location for an offshore wind support base on the eastern Baltic Sea coast. They also discussed wind energy as a key economic driver: beyond addressing climate change, the sector creates jobs, develops technology, stimulates industrial growth and strengthens security. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis presented the advantages of the Port of Liepāja and its industrial sites to industry professionals and investors, discussed progress on renewable energy projects and chaired the panel “The Role of Ports in Renewable Energy Production and the Economy”. Participants included Ministry of Economics Parliamentary Secretary Jurģis Miezainis, European Trade Commissioner Chris Barton, Van Oord Project Development Director Roger Klaskwin and Rønne Port CEO Jeppe La Cour. Opening the discussion, European Trade Commissioner Chris Barton stressed the need for strategic, bold decisions on developing the Baltic Sea region and its port infrastructure, so that ports can efficiently support the construction and subsequent servicing of wind farms. In both the short and long term, an offshore wind support base brings substantial economic benefits to the city and region by encouraging a wide range of manufacturing and service businesses and creating well-paid jobs. The Port of Liepāja was identified as the strategically most important potential offshore wind support base on the eastern Baltic Sea coast. After extensive research, the Dutch company Van Oord selected Liepāja. Construction planning is currently under way and cooperation agreements have been signed with two other major European companies, Euroports and Smulders. Van Oord Project Development Director Roger Klaskwin outlined the conditions needed to establish such a base and emphasised that location is the decisive factor behind the selection of Liepāja. Rønne Port CEO Jeppe La Cour shared how the port on the Danish island of Bornholm evolved from a fishing port into a leading Baltic Sea offshore wind support port serving wind farm construction. He identified important strategic similarities between Rønne and Liepāja that could allow Liepāja to achieve comparable growth in the near future. Participants also considered when an offshore wind support base should be built. It is a chicken-and-egg problem: a wind farm needs a port with suitable infrastructure, but infrastructure requires investment before the wind farm is built. Strategic and responsible decisions by the state are therefore needed, alongside discussion of the extent to which the state should influence ports’ development. Parliamentary Secretary Jurģis Miezainis agreed with other speakers that the most favourable location is paramount. Several investors have selected Liepāja SEZ sites for renewable energy projects and have begun research and preparations. An offshore wind support base, green hydrogen and sustainable aviation fuel production, a CO₂ terminal, and a factory producing hydrogen-powered aircraft are among the complementary and indirectly linked projects. The Liepāja SEZ Authority, together with the municipality, investors, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) and Riga Technical University (RTU), has established the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre to help make Liepāja a climate-neutral city that is friendly to people and the environment. title: Karosta After the Occupation: The Perspective of Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 10. maijs, 2024 Karosta After the Occupation: The Perspective of Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis On Friday, 17 May at 15:00, students and other interested visitors are invited to hear Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis speak about Karosta after the Soviet occupation. The event takes place at the Liepāja Occupation Museum, 7/9 K. Ukstiņa Street, as part of the exhibition “The Legacy of Soviet Occupation in Karosta”. The exhibition “The Legacy of Soviet Occupation in Karosta” will be on display at the Liepāja Occupation Museum until 29 September, accompanied by a series of talks about Karosta. Historian Juris Raķis spoke about Karosta before Soviet occupation on 25 April. Karosta is part of Liepāja but was originally built as an autonomous city within a city, serving as a military base. Liepāja regained Karosta in the mid-1990s, when neither the state nor the city knew how to restore the degraded territory left by Soviet troops. Following the establishment of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone in 1997, the former military base became integrated into Liepāja again. The challenge was to incorporate it into civilian life while preserving its cultural heritage and finding new opportunities for development. Although two world wars caused extensive damage to Karosta, this cannot be compared with the consequences of Soviet occupation, which remain visible today. Even so, Karosta in the 1990s and Karosta today are almost unrecognisable as the same place. For around 30 years it has no longer been a closed military site, but an attractive district of Liepāja with its own enduring character. Uldis Hmieļevskis will reflect on what these decades have meant for Karosta. About Karosta Karosta’s origins can be traced to 1890, when Russia decided to build a new naval base near Liepāja. In less than 17 years, a practically new, autonomous city emerged. At the time it was one of the most modern complexes of its kind in Europe. Russia displayed the achievement at several exhibitions, and the project received high recognition at the 1900 Paris International Exposition. What is now called Karosta initially consisted of two relatively separate areas. Karosta itself was a naval city and fleet base, with an outer harbour, hydraulic structures, a canal, bridge, ship-repair yard, barracks, cathedral and officers’ residences, under the Naval Ministry. The Libau coastal fortress — its forts, fortress canal (now known as Melnupīte) and other defences, including structures in central and southern Liepāja — was administered by the War Ministry. After the fortress was abolished in 1908 and the naval base lost its status as the main base, the two areas gradually merged into what we know today as Karosta. Until 1994, Karosta was a closed military base serving the Soviet Navy. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: New Protein Production Plant Opens in Karosta Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. jūnijs, 2024 New Protein Production Plant Opens in Karosta Industrial Park On 19 June, the Golden Field Factory LV protein production facility in Karosta Industrial Park was officially opened. The plant marks the return of agricultural product processing to Liepāja and the arrival of the first investments from the United Arab Emirates and the United States. The new plant provides more than 50 jobs and represents an investment of EUR 16 million. It plans to process locally sourced and imported peas and beans into protein and starch for use in the food industry. All output is intended for export. “This is already the fourth factory in Karosta Industrial Park and the twenty-fourth built in Liepāja over the last seven years, but it is certainly a special one. First, it will process agricultural products — beans and peas — into high-value-added protein. Second, it is the first facility to successfully preserve and integrate historic Karosta buildings,” says Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis. The building at 11 Zemgales Street was commissioned by the Liepāja municipal Building Authority on 29 November 2022 as the office and production building of SIA EB Liepāja in Karosta Industrial Park, with a total floor area of 4,802.4 m². SIA EB Liepāja later leased the building to Golden Field Factory LV SIA. Design work began in March 2020 and construction in August 2021. This is the fourth factory in Karosta Industrial Park, but the first to restore and incorporate historic Karosta architecture. Architect Gundars Vīksna integrated the historic buildings into the new plant’s design, implemented by contractor SIA UPTK. “When developing the idea of Karosta Industrial Park, the municipality and the Liepāja SEZ Authority agreed that Zemgales Street’s historic appearance should be preserved, and this was later incorporated into the development requirements. As a result, one of the buildings on Zemgales Street underwent a complete revival, while part of another building’s facade was preserved and linked to the spacious production premises. The surrounding area was also landscaped and parking was constructed.” Background: The idea for Karosta Industrial Park emerged in 1999 to encourage job creation, increase tax revenue for the city and state, and provide additional resources for education, culture, sport and other projects. Building new factories in Karosta was not feasible or attractive to investors until 2015, when the municipality and Liepāja SEZ Authority prepared almost 20 hectares of land for business development. title: Cleaning Up Karosta Canal: Improving the Baltic Sea Ecosystem and Liepāja’s Environment
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 03. oktobris, 2021 Cleaning Up Karosta Canal: Improving the Baltic Sea Ecosystem and Liepāja’s Environment On 1 December 2021, Liepāja hosted the opening seminar for the Port of Liepāja’s Karosta Canal remediation project, “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja”. The seminar, “Cleaning Up Karosta Canal: A Contribution to the Ecological Health of the Baltic Sea and Liepāja’s Environment”, highlighted the canal’s importance to Liepāja’s cultural and historical development. The cleanup will improve environmental quality and biodiversity in the canal, the Baltic Sea ecosystem and water quality, as well as local environmental conditions and residents’ health. The project implemented by the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority follows remediation work carried out in 2018. Its aim is to reduce the adverse effects of historically contaminated sediments in Karosta Canal on the environment, human health and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea. Activities at the former military base severely affected environmental quality in Karosta Canal, making it one of Latvia’s most polluted sites. Contaminants include petroleum products (including benzene, xylene and hydrocarbons) and heavy metals (mercury, arsenic, lead, zinc, copper, selenium and cadmium), concentrated in accumulated mud and sand. Untreated municipal wastewater was also discharged into the canal before treatment facilities were built. Contamination exceeds permitted limits, degrading the ecosystem and leaving very limited flora and fauna. Although pollutants appear to be trapped in sediments, they can affect perch living near the canal. Fish may migrate to Lake Liepāja, where perch have been found to contain markedly higher concentrations of mercury. Pollution can therefore spread beyond its original location through the food chain, affecting other levels of the ecosystem, including people. Nevertheless, improvements have been observed in recent years. Long-term studies indicate that petroleum product concentrations in sediments have decreased almost eightfold since 1993, partly because bacteria naturally break down certain petroleum compounds. A 2018 assessment by the Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre of pollution loads entering the Baltic Sea found that preliminary wastewater-treatment measures had been completed. It concluded that Karosta Canal remediation would improve the Baltic Sea’s ecology and water quality, potentially enabling the canal to be removed from the Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission (HELCOM) list of pollution “hot spots”. To improve the environment of Karosta Canal and the Baltic Sea, the remediation project will remove 202,247 m³ of sediments that do not meet regulatory standards and contain 400 tonnes of contaminants. The project is funded under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total project costs are EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000 from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. Additional information: Between 1994 and 2010, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and government institutions funded dozens of geo-environmental studies in preparation for the canal cleanup. A decision to implement phase one was not taken until 2012. With EU Cohesion Fund support, the project “Cleanup of Historically Contaminated Sites in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja — Phase I” was completed by 31 December 2015. Large quantities of man-made debris, including scrap metal, concrete and timber, were removed and disposed of from 78 hectares of the canal. Approximately 60,000 m³ of polluted sediments were also dredged from the most contaminated 10-hectare section and deposited in a purpose-built disposal facility at the canal’s eastern end. Liepāja SEZ Authority begins phase two of the Karosta Canal cleanup — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zp1Yv1qPYi0 Additional sources: Analysis of pollution-load assessments, “Determination of nutrient loads from pollution sources entering the Baltic Sea in order to identify effective reduction measures and sources with the greatest pollution-reduction potential”. title: Technical and Economic Assessment of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site Completed
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 11. novembris, 2024 Technical and Economic Assessment of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site Completed From 1 August to 31 October 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority implemented an initiative under the Bilateral Cooperation Fund of the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. The initiative, “Technical and Economic Assessment of Development Options for the Historically Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja”, was a logical continuation of earlier remediation efforts. Despite numerous studies and remediation projects addressing Karosta Canal, no previous investigation had assessed the further development of the contaminated sediment disposal site, including ways to prevent the spread of stored pollutants, alternative development options and potential management scenarios. The initiative developed alternatives for the disposal site and identified the most promising management scenarios. The Liepāja SEZ Authority worked with Norwegian partners — the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) and the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI). Both have extensive experience in remediation of historic marine pollution and in creating and managing contaminated sediment disposal sites. Based on their preliminary assessment, the Norwegian partners NGI and NIVA recommend removing the remaining most heavily contaminated areas of the Karosta Canal bed. The final remediation phase would remove an additional 100,000 m³ of historically contaminated sediments and up to 196 tonnes of hazardous chemicals from the canal environment. Among the alternatives assessed for reducing greenhouse gas emissions and hazardous substance releases from sediments at the disposal site, the most effective was to add a further 60 cm thick isolating layer over the contaminated material. Karosta Canal and its historic seabed contamination constitute a uniquely degraded site affecting the Baltic Sea environment, not only in Latvia but across the wider Baltic Sea region. Since 1994, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority has systematically worked to restore the canal’s environment. Major remediation projects in 2015 and 2023 removed more than 200,000 m³ of polluted sediments from the canal and placed them in the designated historically contaminated sediment disposal site. This is a specially enclosed section of Karosta Canal designed to safely contain the deposited sediments. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Latvian Harbour Masters Discuss Current Maritime Industry Issues
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 11. aprīlis, 2025 Latvian Harbour Masters Discuss Current Maritime Industry Issues On 10 April, Latvian harbour masters and the management of the Maritime Administration met in Liepāja for a working meeting attended by representatives of the Latvian Naval Forces. Main topics included maintaining shipping channels, handling new types of cargo in cooperation with port businesses, and development projects to diversify port operations based on sustainable industries and renewable resources. They also discussed projects planned by Latvia’s three major ports — Riga, Ventspils and Liepāja — to improve maritime safety and modernise vessel traffic management and navigation systems. The ports of Liepāja and Ventspils plan to announce a joint procurement procedure soon to upgrade their vessel traffic and hydrographic systems. The port authorities of Salacgrīva, Skulte and Pāvilosta are also planning development projects. The harbour masters also reviewed and discussed the results of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) audit, the advantages and disadvantages of virtual buoys, registration requirements for yachts and recreational craft, and the need to update port regulations. title: Liepāja: An Offshore Wind Energy Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 14. aprīlis, 2022 Liepāja: An Offshore Wind Energy Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea As the geopolitical landscape, market conditions and people’s habits change rapidly, the need for carefully considered, innovative and environmentally friendly solutions is increasing. One current priority is the plan to build several offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea from 2027. This is supported by international agreements, the Baltic Sea maritime spatial plan identifying suitable locations, and the need to strengthen energy independence. A discussion entitled “Latvian Ports as the Foundation of Energy Independence” brought together representatives of Latvia’s major ports, the Latvian Wind Energy Association, Latvenergo management, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, and major port stevedoring companies. Transport Minister Jānis Vitenbergs said: “Offshore wind farms and energy independence are priorities for Latvia, and well-developed port infrastructure is essential. Today’s discussion showed which issues are urgent and require prompt, practical solutions to move wind farm projects and supporting infrastructure forward. We saw today that Liepāja has done significant preparatory work and developed an impressive proposal.” Building offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea requires a support base in a port. The Port of Liepāja is among the most suitable locations for this infrastructure. The city’s and Liepāja SEZ’s long-term development plans, including Strategic Objective No. 2 on developing the outer harbour, provide a foundation for taking action quickly and saving time before facilities are due to become operational in 2027. Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis said: “Currently, no port on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea has the required infrastructure: at least 15–20 hectares of land with two 200-metre high-load-bearing berths. We believe that projects in Latvia should use Latvian port infrastructure. Liepāja has the available land within the harbour and favourable geotechnical conditions to provide the required load capacity. We have therefore developed an outer harbour concept with 39 hectares of infrastructure in the first phase. The technical solution, investment needs, implementation roadmap and schedule have been prepared. The project would take four years, fitting the region’s offshore wind farm construction plans and even allowing some additional time.” The project aims to establish a major regional installation port for offshore wind farm construction, while also providing land for related manufacturing and an operations and maintenance (O&M) base. The technical design draws on best practices from leading offshore wind service ports in Denmark, the Netherlands and Germany. Implementation is planned in three stages according to market demand, covering a total area of 88.5 hectares. Wind energy manufacturers are already showing strong interest in opportunities offered by Liepāja SEZ. Plans for new Baltic Sea wind farms have stretched the capacity of existing factories, prompting a search for locations for new plants serving both offshore and onshore wind projects. Port infrastructure and logistics are vital to all these projects. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: Time Capsule Laid in Foundations of New Scania Latvia Service Centre in Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 28. novembris, 2025 Time Capsule Laid in Foundations of New Scania Latvia Service Centre in Liepāja Scania Latvia marked the start of construction of its new truck service and sales centre in Liepāja by ceremonially laying a time capsule in the foundations. The project is important both for the company’s future development and for the region’s transport infrastructure and business environment. The new Scania Latvia centre will be a major asset for the Liepāja region, becoming one of Kurzeme’s key transport service facilities. It will improve access to services for professional carriers, encourage regional economic activity and local business development, and support modern, safe and sustainable transport infrastructure. The new facility will replace Scania’s existing Liepāja service centre, located only a few minutes away from the planned site at 1B Grīzupes Street. The approximately 1,300 m² building will have three repair and maintenance lines capable of servicing up to ten trucks simultaneously. It will also include a modern vehicle wash and comfortable premises for service and sales specialists. The total investment is EUR 4.6 million. The centre will provide high-quality service for diesel-powered, gas-powered and battery-electric trucks, along with their bodies and trailers. The project responds to the growing regional need for high-quality, fast and technologically advanced transport maintenance services. As freight volumes and logistics activity in the Baltic region increase, demand for efficient service solutions continues to grow. Scania Latvia Managing Director Aigars Pušinskis emphasised: “The new Scania service centre in Liepāja is a strategic milestone in our company’s development. It will significantly improve the availability of transport services in Kurzeme and, I believe, across the Baltic region. Our existing centre had reached its capacity, so building a new one was a logical step. Together with our team of specialists, the upgraded centre will enable us to deliver even higher service quality.” Construction is being carried out by Mapri Būve. Board Member Holger Kald said: “There are three symbolic stages in construction: laying the time capsule, the topping-out ceremony, and opening the building. We plan for the new Scania Latvia centre to be ready by autumn next year. Winters in Liepāja are often mild enough to allow work to continue uninterrupted. Projects like this are extremely important for the regions: they create jobs, strengthen the business environment and stimulate investment beyond the capital.” Raivo Špaks, Head of Business Development at Liepāja SEZ, added: “Manufacturing and port businesses in Liepāja SEZ rely on road freight transport. The regular Stena Line ferry connection between the Port of Liepāja and Travemünde, near Lübeck in Germany, is also important. It continues to develop, functioning as an extension of the German motorway network, with goods turnover valued at around EUR 4 billion annually. Construction of Scania Latvia’s new truck service and sales centre is clear evidence of economic activity in Liepāja and the region. Where there is demand, supply follows.” Energy efficiency and environmentally friendly solutions are central to the project. Renewable-energy heat pumps are planned for heating, while solar panels on the roof will reduce electricity costs over time. Smart lighting systems will be installed inside and outside the building, adjusting to daylight levels and the movement of people. These solutions will allow the new centre to operate more efficiently and reduce its environmental impact, while providing a modern workplace for employees and top-quality customer service. About Scania Latvia: Scania is a global leader in transport solutions. Working with partners and customers, the company is driving the transition to a sustainable transport system. Scania is part of TRATON GROUP. Further information: www.scania.com Scania Latvia was founded on 2 March 1993. It sells new and used Scania trucks, provides warranty and post-warranty repairs and maintenance for Scania vehicles and combinations at service centres in Riga, Valmiera, Daugavpils and Liepāja, sells spare parts and accessories, offers vehicle financing and insurance in cooperation with Scania Finans, and provides driver training. About Mapri Būve SIA Mapri Būve is a fast-growing construction company operating since 2014 and specialising in residential, commercial and industrial buildings. As part of Estonia’s Mapri Ehitus group, it benefits from regional cooperation, shared expertise and opportunities to work on projects across the Baltic states. Mapri Būve employs 74 people in Latvia. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: “Liepāja Is One Step Ahead,” Says Economy Minister Viktors Valainis During Visit
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 17. maijs, 2024 “Liepāja Is One Step Ahead,” Says Economy Minister Viktors Valainis During Visit On 17 May, Economy Minister Viktors Valainis visited Liepāja on a one-day working trip. Discussions with city and Liepāja SEZ leaders covered energy-sector development, manufacturing, well-paid skilled jobs, investment in freight transport and exports, housing, and other important economic issues. “Liepāja is already one step ahead and is moving purposefully towards Latvia’s economic development goals: doubling the economy within ten years, pursuing a new approach to energy, developing offshore wind farms and hydrogen production, and increasing productivity and high-value-added manufacturing,” Minister Viktors Valainis said. During the visit, the minister toured manufacturing businesses, industrial parks, a water export terminal and energy development projects. He emphasised that energy-sector projects could accelerate Latvia’s economic growth through modern technology. Liepāja has a clear vision for developing an offshore wind support base and moving gradually towards hydrogen production and hydrogen-powered aircraft. The minister also praised Liepāja SEZ’s governance for attracting investment, building new factories and creating skilled jobs. “At a time when port and transit business governance reforms are again being discussed, Liepāja shows that its model works. Businesses, the municipality and the state sit together to plan how to develop the economic zone and attract investment. Other ports could aspire to this model. I am pleased with what I saw today: businesses aiming to double production and development projects worth tens of millions of euros already under way. We will do everything we can to support entrepreneurs.” Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: Liepāja Positions Itself as an Offshore Wind Energy Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea
text: 01. decembris, 2023 Liepāja Positions Itself as an Offshore Wind Energy Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis attended the Offshore Energy Exhibition & Conference in Amsterdam from 27 to 29 November, visited the ports of Rotterdam and Amsterdam, and met senior representatives of leading energy and logistics companies in the European Union. Following the working visit to the Netherlands, Hmieļevskis said the trip had reinforced his understanding of the EU’s ambitious goal of developing 150 GW of new capacity by 2050. “It is a major challenge: manufacturing capacity and port capacity will both need to triple. For Liepāja and Latvia, this creates an opportunity to build new factories producing foundations, towers, blades and perhaps even generators. Existing businesses will have opportunities to manufacture various components and parts. Liepāja Maritime College could train seafarers specifically for wind farm construction and maintenance, allowing them to work in their profession closer to home instead of spending months on long voyages.” The Baltic Sea is the North Sea 2.0 — an informal term used by the offshore wind industry in the Netherlands to describe the Baltic Sea’s potential in achieving the European Union’s energy independence and climate neutrality goals. The Netherlands has extensive energy-sector experience, dating from offshore oil and gas platforms in the North Sea to today’s offshore wind farms. The Liepāja SEZ Manager said that visiting the ports of Amsterdam and Rotterdam and participating in the wind energy exhibition and conference had resulted in valuable discussions, new contacts and talks about development projects. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is expected to participate in several major projects in the port and industrial areas. “The offshore wind industry is substantial, and Latvia must seize the opportunities it offers: creating jobs and expertise, supplying existing businesses with green energy, and developing new industries that will be in demand in the future,” said Liepāja SEZ Manager Uldis Hmieļevskis. title: Liepāja Takes a Step Towards Sustainable Aviation Fuel: LSEZ “NorSAF” Launches Environmental Impact Assessment
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 05. decembris, 2025 Liepāja Takes a Step Towards Sustainable Aviation Fuel: LSEZ “NorSAF” Launches Environmental Impact Assessment The oil and chemical product storage and handling terminal NorSAF has signed an agreement to carry out an environmental impact assessment. The assessment will examine the potential effects of the plant’s operations and technology on people and the environment. Technology for the planned NorSAF plant will be supplied by an internationally recognised engineering company that has provided technology to NASA and the US armed forces for many years. “The environmental impact assessment is an important step demonstrating our commitment to implementing the project in accordance with all environmental protection standards, working closely with government authorities and leading environmental experts and ensuring transparency throughout construction and development. We also intend to use some of the world’s most innovative, proven, safe and sustainable production technologies. They will help Latvia become a centre for sustainable energy production and exports for the Baltic region, Europe and the wider world,” said Jānis Kisiels, a board member of LSEZ SIA NorSAF. In accordance with the requirements of the State Environmental Service, the assessment examines how the company’s operations may affect different areas of the environment and whether they could cause air, wastewater or subsurface pollution affecting human health, environmental quality, and surrounding flora and fauna. The company must consider several alternatives and choose the most suitable solution to prevent or minimise adverse effects. Representatives of SIA Estonian, Latvian & Lithuanian Environment (ELLE), which is carrying out the assessment, explained that specialists from many fields are involved in preparing the report. They assess possible impacts on public health and safety, natural assets, landscapes, cultural heritage and socioeconomic conditions, among other areas. The views of the municipality, Nature Conservation Agency, Health Inspectorate, National Cultural Heritage Board and other competent authorities are also evaluated and taken into account. “Our many years of experience and expertise in assessing environmental factors will allow us to provide a comprehensive and detailed evaluation of an activity that represents a new and innovative industry both in Latvia and internationally. We will carry out the necessary studies and work with NorSAF to find optimal solutions and define conditions for operating the plant while maintaining a high level of protection for neighbouring residents and the environment,” explained ELLE board member Aiga Kāla. As previously reported, the NorSAF plant will use PureSAF technology developed by Swedish Biofuels AB. The US engineering company KBR holds the exclusive licence. For more than 60 years, KBR has supplied advanced technology and implemented projects worth billions for NASA space missions, developed solutions for the US armed forces, and built major energy-sector plants around the world. “We take responsibility for the environment and the wellbeing of local residents seriously. We demonstrate this by complying with strict Latvian and international safety standards, choosing highly innovative technologies and working with leading experts who share our values. Our technology partner KBR not only supplies solutions for some of the world’s largest high-capacity industrial complexes, with investments worth billions of US dollars, but also supports research into astronaut health, occupational illnesses and other topics to reduce risks during future crewed space missions,” emphasised Jānis Kisiels. The new plant in Liepāja is expected to produce 100,000 tonnes of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) annually, including approximately 40,000 tonnes of eSAF — synthetic sustainable aviation fuel produced using green hydrogen. The fuel will be supplied to aviation companies in the Baltic states and Northern Europe and exported to other European markets. Production is planned to begin in 2030, when NorSAF is expected to become Northern Europe’s largest SAF and eSAF plant. The estimated project cost is EUR 500–600 million. Approximately 400 jobs for highly qualified professionals — managers, engineers, logistics specialists and others — are expected to be created both directly and indirectly. title: Liepāja Well Positioned to Continue Attracting Significant Foreign Investment
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 08. oktobris, 2024 Liepāja Well Positioned to Continue Attracting Significant Foreign Investment On 4 October, more than 40 employees of Latvian embassies abroad who work to strengthen economic cooperation visited Liepāja for a study and working visit. Diplomats toured several foreign-owned factories operating in Liepāja SEZ and learned about the city’s economic development plans for the next three to five years. At the end of the visit they praised what they had seen, describing Liepāja as one of Latvia’s success stories with strong prospects for expanding export markets and attracting further significant foreign investment. The diplomats visited the new fish-processing plant of SIA Syfud, built on the site of the historic fish-canning factory. Total investment has approached EUR 80 million, with capital from neighbouring Lithuania. They also visited Golden Fields Factory LV, a newly launched protein production facility in Karosta Industrial Park, representing approximately EUR 16 million in investment from the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Mārcis Maksims, Deputy Head of Mission and Counsellor at the Latvian Embassy in the UAE, said the company was a good example of an investment project successfully implemented in a relatively short time, potentially encouraging further UAE investment in Latvia and Liepāja. When Liepāja SEZ was established, cooperation with the Latvian Embassy in Denmark helped attract the first Danish investors. They built manufacturing facilities and a cargo terminal in the port. Danish-owned manufacturers now play a prominent role in Liepāja SEZ and continue to expand. Jānis Kalva, Deputy Head of Mission at the Latvian Embassy in Denmark, said: “The Danes already have extensive experience here. When one or two Danish investors arrive and share positive experiences, Liepāja becomes a centre attracting more of them. We see increasing Danish interest and existing investors expanding. We follow Liepāja’s priorities in climate and green energy, areas where Denmark has been a pioneer — including wind energy and adapting ports for the wind and climate economy. Liepāja has major plans in these areas, and investors are looking for opportunities. There is clear potential for cooperation.” Norwegian investment arrived in Liepāja relatively recently, but several projects connected with the European Green Deal, renewable resources and business innovation are already at different stages of development. Latvia’s Ambassador to Norway, Mārtiņš Klīve, said: “Liepāja has a very compelling story. The plans, work completed and results we heard about today make it easier to promote Liepāja and Latvia to Norwegian investors. The preparation has been done: sites have been improved, infrastructure is in place, and there are real opportunities to offer. We will also work to bring Norwegian investors to Liepāja.” In recent years, joint efforts have focused on implementing several sustainable development projects and attracting investment from the Netherlands. Gatis Šneiders, Deputy Head of Mission at the Latvian Embassy in the Netherlands, noted: “The most significant areas of mutual economic interest are linked to renewable energy, particularly wind power, hydrogen production and use, and aviation. Fokker Next Gen N.V., for example, is one of the companies planning activities specifically in Liepāja.” Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026.
