title: Multimedia Exhibition on the Port of Liepāja Takes Shape in Liepāja Lighthouse
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 05. augusts, 2026 Multimedia Exhibition on the Port of Liepāja Takes Shape in Liepāja Lighthouse Liepāja Lighthouse will soon welcome visitors in a new form, becoming a unique cultural and tourist attraction. Modern technology will tell the story of the Port of Liepāja and allow visitors to explore its development from the earliest days to the present. A multi-layered multimedia exhibition is currently being developed in the lighthouse. Across five floors, projections, sound, lighting and animated historical stories will combine to trace the development of the Port of Liepāja from its beginnings to today. The project “Creating a Digital Performance on the History of the Port of Liepāja in Liepāja Lighthouse” aims to open one of the port’s navigational facilities to the public, showcasing its cultural and historical significance and creating an innovative visitor experience in which heritage and digital technology come together. “This is a unique and challenging project in Latvia. All multimedia elements will be synchronised and operate as a single show across five floors,” says Jānis Zučiks, Project Manager at ProVision Baltic. “Given the lighthouse’s cultural heritage status, it was challenging to install all the equipment without damaging the building and to ensure that the technology operates year-round in Latvia’s changeable weather.” Technologically, this is one of the most complex projects of its kind in Latvia. Up to 250-degree projections will be created inside the lighthouse using 14 projectors, accompanied by music specially composed by Andris Vilcāns, sound and lighting effects operating simultaneously across five floors as one multimedia experience. Building on years of research by Liepāja Museum, the creative team has developed five animated multimedia stories. Immersive projections and multi-channel sound will reveal the development of the port and city, their international role in trade and transport, and stories of the courage, enterprise and perseverance of Liepāja’s people. The performances are produced by video artist Māris Kalve and specialists from Kalvestudija. “The central idea and guiding theme of the Liepāja Lighthouse exhibition is the human will confronting the forces of nature. The lighthouse symbolises the will to live and to exist,” emphasises Māris Kalve, the concept’s creator, director, screenwriter and video artist. “The overarching purpose of the five stories is to remind visitors of the ever-present and absolutely essential value of humanity.” Through the multimedia performances, the lighthouse becomes a symbol of overcoming challenges. As visitors climb its vertical structure, they will travel through different eras, discovering the emergence of the port, shipping and fishing traditions, the development of the city and the lives of its people. “There are many lighthouses around the world that people can climb to enjoy breathtaking views. But only one will let visitors see not only the landscape, but time itself. That is Liepāja Lighthouse,” says exhibition director and screenwriter Pauls Ķesteris. “Ascending through the lighthouse, visitors move through centuries, exploring the creation of the port and city, human destinies, maritime and fishing traditions, historical upheavals and visions for the future.” Liepāja Lighthouse is an integral part of the port’s navigation system and continues to guide sailors and fishermen. The lighthouse belongs to the Maritime Administration of Latvia and has been placed under the management of the Liepāja SEZ Authority. Once the project is complete, the multimedia performance about the port’s history will be managed by Liepāja Museum, which will organise guided visits accompanied by a guide or lighthouse employee. The lighthouse will become a significant new cultural, tourist and heritage destination, telling the story of the port’s past and present while looking to its future. The project is implemented by Liepāja City Municipality at a total cost of EUR 387,144.34, with co-financing from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund, the state and Liepāja City Municipality. title: Partners of the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre Agree on Future Priorities
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 05. decembris, 2024 Partners of the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre Agree on Future Priorities On 4 December 2024, partners of the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre gathered for their first joint working meeting to agree on practical cooperation and communication measures and develop an action plan for the near future. The objective is to strengthen energy independence and economic development in Liepāja, Latvia and the Baltic Sea region while meeting EU climate-neutrality and sustainability goals. The meeting took place at Riga Technical University (RTU), an important partner in scientific research, innovative technologies and education programmes preparing specialists for green energy and smart manufacturing. On 12 November 2024, the partners signed a joint statement on strategically important private investment projects in green energy and smart manufacturing in Liepāja. The signatories agreed to establish the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre within the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. The centre aims to become a major Baltic regional player in green energy and innovative technologies. Its members include Van Oord, Euroports, Smulders, CIS Liepāja, GI Termināls and Fokker Next Gen Latvia, together with the Liepāja SEZ Authority, Liepāja City Council, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) and Riga Technical University. Planned projects: An offshore wind support base and heavy cargo terminal at the Port of Liepāja, providing infrastructure for building wind farms in the Baltic Sea and locating factories for large structures near the berths. Implemented by Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders. A hydrogen production plant and terminal, producing hydrogen from renewable energy sources. Implemented by CIS Liepāja. A sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant, producing fuel to help aviation transition towards more environmentally friendly energy sources. Implemented by GI Termināls. Hydrogen-powered aircraft manufacturing, producing passenger aircraft at Liepāja Airport and contributing to the decarbonisation of aviation. Implemented by Fokker Next Gen Latvia. A CO₂ export terminal for storing and transporting captured carbon dioxide emitted by industry and the energy sector. Implemented by GI Termināls. The joint statement aims to place these development projects at the top of the government agenda, securing state support through simplified procedures and approvals, access to financing instruments and infrastructure investment. The projects will promote Latvia’s economic sustainability, create new high-tech industries and contribute to GDP growth and industrial development. About the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority: The Liepāja SEZ Authority provides a high-quality, attractive business environment and encourages development of the SEZ under unified management and clear conditions. It seeks to attract investors in smart, sustainable, high-value-added industries, particularly manufacturing, green energy and technology, creating skilled jobs with competitive pay. title: Streets in Liepāja Industrial Park Receive Official Names
text: 22. augusts, 2025 Streets in Liepāja Industrial Park Receive Official Names At its meeting on 21 August, Liepāja City Council approved eight new street names for planned roads on the site of the former Liepājas metalurgs factory, now being developed as Liepāja Industrial Park. Based on residents’ suggestions and voting results, the names are Trīs skursteņu iela, Martena iela, Eksporta iela, Dzelzsgriezēja iela, Inženieru iela, Čuguna iela, Naglu iela and Dūmu iela. Residents actively participated in the naming process. They were first invited to suggest names for streets in the future industrial park at the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s stand during the “Made in Liepāja” exhibition, where a total of 385 suggestions were received. After reviewing the proposals, 14 names that best reflected the site’s identity, did not duplicate existing street names and symbolised the future park’s industrial, cultural, historical and development potential were shortlisted for a public vote. The vote attracted 301 ballots, from which eight names were selected for City Council approval. The State Language Centre also gave a positive opinion on the proposed street names. Among other recommendations, it suggested changing “Skursteņu iela” to “Trīs skursteņu iela” to better reflect the urban landscape and historical context. Assigning official street names is a prerequisite for entering the roads into the official address register. Several new streets are currently being built in Liepāja Industrial Park, including pedestrian and cycle paths, underground utilities, lighting and landscaping. Work on the new Eksporta and Inženieru streets is nearing completion, with commissioning planned soon. Work continues on Naglu and Dzelzsgriezēja streets, where the base asphalt layer has been laid. All work under the first phase of the project is scheduled for completion by the end of 2025. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Liepāja Industrial Park Named Among World’s Top 10 Industrial and Logistics Investment Projects
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 21. septembris, 2026 Liepāja Industrial Park Named Among World’s Top 10 Industrial and Logistics Investment Projects The latest edition of Real FDI’s regular publication, which highlights attractive investment projects across regions and sectors, presents its top 10 for 2026. In today’s competitive environment, the most attractive locations offer more than land: they provide modern infrastructure, energy security, logistics links and an ecosystem suited to advanced manufacturing. Liepāja Industrial Park has been recognised as one of the most promising European projects in the top 10. The projects selected by Real FDI reflect the diversity and scale of these opportunities, ranging from major freeports and established industrial districts to brownfield regeneration initiatives and airport-linked logistics centres. According to the publication, they demonstrate how connectivity, infrastructure, available land and increasingly sophisticated industrial ecosystems are shaping the next generation of investment destinations. “Countries no longer compete only to attract investment, but also in their ability to provide the industrial infrastructure that investors need.” Real FDI magazine highlighted ten of the world’s most promising industrial and logistics investment projects. They span several countries and development models, from large industrial hubs in Germany and Spain to emerging logistics centres in Iceland, Romania, Latvia, the United Kingdom and Mexico. Liepāja Industrial Park received special recognition for making sustainability part of its very DNA, with clear principles of education, innovation and the circular economy. The former Liepājas metalurgs factory site is gradually being reintegrated into the city, opening it to the public and making it attractive to investors. The park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas metalurgs site, between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets. It borders Lake Liepāja, a protected Natura 2000 area. The approved development strategy envisages more than EUR 275 million in private investment and at least 1,500 new jobs. title: Defence Minister Explores Liepāja’s Industrial and Port Capabilities
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 13. augusts, 2026 Defence Minister Explores Liepāja’s Industrial and Port Capabilities “Liepāja has strong potential for developing its defence industry,” said Defence Minister Raivis Melnis following a one-day working visit to the city. Several companies already operating in Liepāja Special Economic Zone manufacture products used by defence organisations worldwide. For example, LSEZ SIA Interspiro Production makes breathing equipment for divers and firefighters and supplies defence units in various countries. Liepāja plays a strategic role in national defence by combining civilian and military capabilities, developing a NATO support base, accommodating 300 conscripts and using and expanding its existing industrial production capacity. During his visit, the minister met with Liepāja and Liepāja SEZ leaders, explored the port’s and industrial sector’s capabilities, discussed opportunities to expand cooperation and attended the ceremonial change of command of the Latvian Naval Forces. title: Wind-Assisted Cargo Ship Arrives at the Port of Liepāja
text: 25. jūnijs, 2025 Wind-Assisted Cargo Ship Arrives at the Port of Liepāja On 25 June, a remarkable ship arrived at the Port of Liepāja: it generates part of the energy needed for propulsion from wind power. The vertical structures at its bow are wind-assisted propulsion turbines that help reduce engine-generated CO₂ emissions and save fuel. The 88-metre-long Waalvliet was built only in September of the previous year. Its wind energy technology is based on aeronautical engineering and has demonstrated resilience in challenging marine conditions. Flying the Dutch flag, Waalvliet brought a cargo of soybeans to Liepāja after departing from the Port of Rotterdam. title: Total Cargo Turnover at the Port of Liepāja Reached 3.6 Million Tonnes in the First Six Months
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 12. decembris, 2023 Total Cargo Turnover at the Port of Liepāja Reached 3.6 Million Tonnes in the First Six Months Wood-chip cargo turnover at the Port of Liepāja continues to grow, increasing by 7.7%, while ro-ro cargo volumes have remained stable. Businesses are also actively preparing for the new grain season, with the first grain shipments arriving as early as July. Total cargo turnover at the port during the first six months amounted to 3.6 million tonnes. The operations of Liepāja and other Latvian ports are affected by the geopolitical situation and changes in logistics routes and cargo types. The transport and logistics sector is actively working to attract new cargo and increase volumes, developing alternative logistics corridors, including for niche products and higher-value-added cargo such as containers and ro-ro traffic. New investment is also being sought and attracted to develop manufacturing in port areas. According to data compiled by the Ministry of Transport, overall cargo volumes declined in the first half of 2023. At the same time, several cargo segments at Latvian ports recorded growth, as did domestic rail freight. Port and rail cargo turnover continues to be affected by the current geopolitical situation and the decision adopted at the start of the year introducing sanctions on Russian petroleum products. Due to the geopolitical situation, total cargo handled at Latvian ports in the first half of 2023 fell by 14.2%, or 3.4 million tonnes, compared with the same period of the previous year. The main factor was the continuing decline in demand for coal shipments, while sanctions also reduced petroleum-product turnover. Meanwhile, grain turnover rose by 7.4% at the major ports, and overall cargo turnover at Latvia’s smaller ports—Skulte, Salacgrīva, Mērsrags and Roja—increased by 17.4%. At the Port of Riga, grain cargo turnover rose by 20% in the first half of the year, while coal and petroleum-product shipments declined. A total of 9.6 million tonnes of cargo was handled during the period. The Port of Ventspils handled 5.7 million tonnes of cargo during the period. Overall turnover was affected by lower volumes of coal, petroleum products and ro-ro cargo. Despite the general decline, ore shipments more than quadrupled, timber cargo turnover grew by 3.6%, and construction-material turnover increased tenfold. Like ports, rail freight is affected by the geopolitical situation. Total rail cargo turnover in the first six months of the year fell by 36.7% compared with the corresponding period last year. The decline was driven mainly by reduced shipments of coal, mineral fertilisers, timber and petroleum products, whereas grain turnover rose by 18.3%. Domestic rail freight showed growth, increasing by 10% overall in the first half of the year. The rise in the ferrous-metals cargo segment was as high as 67%. Was this information useful? title: Renewable Energy Complex with Terminal Planned at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. aprīlis, 2024 Renewable Energy Complex with Terminal Planned at the Port of Liepāja To add value to electricity produced from renewable energy resources, companies from Norway, Sweden and Latvia have established the SIA “CIS Liepāja” project management team. Its aim is to undertake the necessary studies and develop a renewable energy complex with a terminal, including a hydrogen production plant, at the Port of Liepāja. The Liepāja SEZ Authority has concluded a two-year reservation agreement with SIA “CIS Liepāja”. The project’s lead partner, Clean Industrial Solutions Holding AS, has made investment in innovative and sustainable solutions, alongside the promotion of the circular economy, its main objective. The planned renewable energy complex and terminal at the Port of Liepāja is consistent with the European Green Deal and its aim of transforming the economy and energy sector to achieve climate neutrality by 2050. Tors Arne Pedersen, head of Clean Industrial Solutions AS, emphasises that total planned investment in the production facility and terminal in the port area could reach approximately EUR 1 billion. The planned plant would have a capacity of 1,000 MW, enabling production of about 150,000 tonnes of hydrogen. The SIA “CIS Liepāja” project envisages construction of the renewable energy complex “Power-to-X Terminal at the Port of Liepāja” in the outer harbour by 2030. Tors Arne Pedersen, head of Clean Industrial Solutions AS, says: “Changing climatic conditions influenced by CO₂ emissions mean that we must change not only people’s habits but also develop smart and sustainable businesses, introducing innovative solutions to implement the living set of initiatives embodied in the European Green Deal. This also requires changes in the energy sector, replacing fossil fuels with renewable resources. That will allow us to create a better life for future generations.” “The future hydrogen market is enormous. For Latvia as a whole, and Liepāja in particular, this is an excellent opportunity to become the home of the first large hydrogen production facility in the European Union,” says Tors Arne Pedersen. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis says: “CIS Liepāja is a project intended to help supply CO₂-neutral energy to the EU internal market. We are delighted that one of the first modern hydrogen plants is planned for the territory of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. It fits perfectly with Fokker Next Gen N.V.’s plans to establish an assembly plant for next-generation hydrogen-powered aircraft at Liepāja Airport. These are not the only projects we are implementing together with entrepreneurs to transform port operations and industry in line with the European Green Deal.” Construction of the renewable energy complex and terminal at the Port of Liepāja is expected to create at least 80–100 jobs for highly qualified specialists, promoting the development of innovative technologies and education programmes based on scientific research. The project will create new supply chains and expand export opportunities, increasing international visibility and strengthening the competitiveness of the city and its port. title: Civil Protection and Disaster Management Exercise Held at the Port of Liepāja
text: 29. oktobris, 2024 Civil Protection and Disaster Management Exercise Held at the Port of Liepāja On 29 October, a local practical civil protection and disaster management exercise took place at berth No. 28 of the Port of Liepāja, operated by LSEZ SIA “GI Terminal”. The exercise aimed to test and improve the arrangements and measures set out in the company’s civil protection plan and the external civil protection plan. The exercise scenario involved a substance leak during the refuelling of a ship at the port berth. The exercise involved officials and employees from LSEZ SIA “GI Terminal”, the State Fire and Rescue Service, Liepāja Municipal Police, the State Environmental Service, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority and AS “Latvijas dzelzceļš”. title: New Grain Season Begins at the Port of Liepāja
text: 16. augusts, 2023 New Grain Season Begins at the Port of Liepāja In July 2023, operators at the Port of Liepāja handled 458,222.47 tonnes of various cargoes and actively prepared for the new grain season, which traditionally begins on 1 August and continues until 1 August of the following year. During the 2022/2023 grain season, the port handled 3,156.7 thousand tonnes of agricultural cargo. According to operators, each grain season is different, depending on harvest yields and market conditions. Although it remains difficult to predict the new grain season—following prolonged drought in the first half of summer and severe rainstorms, wind and hail that caused significant damage in early August—companies at the port have started receiving grain from the new harvest. The LSEZ SIA “Dan Store” grain terminal received its first barley shipment on 14 July, followed a little later by wheat and rapeseed. Evita Dambe, Cooperation and Logistics Manager at the LSEZ SIA “Dan Store” terminal, says: “Work at our terminal is currently very busy: every day we receive more than 100 trucks carrying the new grain harvest. In recent days, we have seen the quality of delivered wheat decline, with some meeting only feed-grade standards, as expected after the bad weather. It is clear that the total harvest will also be smaller, but everyone is cautious about forecasts because more than 50% of the fields remain unharvested. In any case, we expect the new season to bring challenges. I have worked at the Dan Store terminal for 17 years and can confidently say that I gain new experience every year.” The LSEZ SIA “Dan Store” terminal reports that the previous season was average, with no major increases or decreases, and that maintaining service quality was essential. Since the terminal reserves approximately 75% of its capacity for domestic suppliers, its operations depend largely on the conditions faced by Latvian grain growers and the size of the harvest. Agricultural products are the largest cargo group at the Port of Liepāja, accounting for 41% of all cargo in 2022. In the first seven months of 2023, they represented 44%, or 1,801.1 thousand tonnes, an increase of 2.1% compared with the corresponding seven months of 2022. Changes in market conditions and the geopolitical situation increased the share of grain relative to other agricultural cargo in 2023. Altogether, operators at the Port of Liepāja handle more than 30 types of agricultural cargo. In early August, the question of exporting Ukrainian grain became particularly relevant, with Latvian ports proposed as an alternative export route while the Black Sea route was closed. The Port of Liepāja handles an average of 3 million tonnes of agricultural cargo annually and has some spare capacity. However, to increase that volume, logistics between Ukraine and the Baltic states would need to be simplified at EU level by establishing a green corridor covering customs, sanitary inspections and other requirements, explains Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. title: Port of Liepāja Actively Handles Grain Harvested by Latvian Farmers in September
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 14. oktobris, 2025 Port of Liepāja Actively Handles Grain Harvested by Latvian Farmers in September In September this year, the Port of Liepāja actively handled grain harvested by Latvian farmers. Agricultural products accounted for more than half of all cargo handled (329.6 thousand tonnes), including soy imports from Argentina. In total, 635.8 thousand tonnes of cargo were handled at the port in September, 27.97% more than in September 2024. As an active part of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone, the port continues to attract local cargo and plays an important logistical role in exporting manufactured products and facilitating trade. Dry bulk shipments included construction materials (75.9 thousand tonnes), wood chips (20.6 thousand tonnes) and wood pellets (17.2 thousand tonnes). General cargo was dominated by ro-ro shipments (139 thousand tonnes), supported by the regular ferry service between Liepāja and Travemünde in Germany. In September, the port received and served 99 ships, while passenger traffic amounted to 8,232 people. Since 2018, the Port of Liepāja has maintained stable annual cargo turnover of 7–7.5 million tonnes and adapted to changes in the transport sector by supplementing traditional cargo operations with manufacturing and higher-value-added products. September also saw the successful completion of the assembly of two port cargo-unloading units, which were shipped to Canada on a specialised vessel. During the first nine months of this year, total cargo turnover amounted to 5.1 million tonnes, 139.9 thousand tonnes or 2.7% less than during the corresponding period last year. The grain season started later than usual due to rain, while demand for energy-related cargo such as wood chips remains relatively low. During the period, the port handled 86,615 ro-ro units, served 871 vessels and welcomed 81,798 passengers. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Port of Liepāja Maintains Stable Cargo Turnover
text: 19. septembris, 2023 Port of Liepāja Maintains Stable Cargo Turnover In the first eight months of 2023, the Port of Liepāja handled 4.6 million tonnes of various cargoes. Dry bulk remained the largest cargo group at 68% of the total, including grain and grain products at 44%, or 2.01 million tonnes. The port continued to maintain stable ro-ro cargo turnover with positive growth. This reflects demand and trade volumes, as well as coordinated cooperation between businesses and the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority to develop new logistics routes, attract new and locally sourced cargo, and invest jointly in infrastructure development. According to figures compiled by the Ministry of Transport, total cargo volumes at Latvia’s major ports declined by 16.8% in the first eight months of 2023 compared with the same period of the previous year. At the same time, several cargo segments grew, including grain, container and construction-material shipments. Cargo turnover at smaller ports also maintained a positive trend, increasing by 12%. In response to the overall decline in cargo turnover compared with the previous year, ports are actively seeking solutions by establishing new logistics corridors and developing alternative supply chains. This supports growth in individual cargo segments and, in the longer term, increases total throughput. New investment is also being sought and attracted to develop manufacturing in port areas. title: Port of Liepāja Continues Receiving Grain Grown by Latvian Farmers
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 02. septembris, 2026 Port of Liepāja Continues Receiving Grain Grown by Latvian Farmers The largest dry bulk terminal at the Port of Liepāja, “Liepaja Bulk Terminal”, has concluded agreements with leading Latvian grain exporters, including “Baltic Agro”, “Latraps” and “Linas Agro”, to receive grain grown by Latvian farmers from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. The terminal is currently loading Latvian-grown wheat onto the Panamax-class vessel “Tuo Fu 8”, which will take on more than 60,000 tonnes of grain at the port. Its destination is Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates. The second-largest grain terminal, “DanStore”, is also operating under its existing contracts. According to the terminal’s management, spare storage capacity is currently available because deliveries of the new harvest are progressing relatively slowly. Unlike in previous years, long queues of trucks have not formed outside the terminal at this time. The company suggests that some Latvian grain growers may be waiting for more favourable sales conditions and higher prices. Grain currently costs between EUR 250 and EUR 260 per tonne, one of the highest levels in recent years. In the coming days, “DanStore” expects a vessel that will load approximately 27,000 tonnes of Latvian grain supplied by “Baltic Agro”. The cargo is destined for Nigeria. Latvian grain reaches the Port of Liepāja not only by road but also by rail. On 2 September, the LBT terminal received a train of 26 wagons carrying 1,820 tonnes of grain from “Baltic Agro”, and another 26-wagon train from the “Latraps” cooperative is expected. Historically, and particularly since resuming operations in the 1990s, the Port of Liepāja has systematically developed agricultural cargo handling, focusing on grain terminals and locally sourced cargo. Exports of grain grown in Latvia to world markets are an important component of the port’s cargo flows. Several agricultural cargo terminals currently operate at the Port of Liepāja, with combined handling capacity of approximately 5 million tonnes per year. Their total warehouse capacity allows approximately 730,000 tonnes of grain to be stored at one time. Grain terminals at the Port of Liepāja cooperate with Latvian and foreign companies that purchase, store and supply grain to global food supply chains. All cargo operations, including handling grain in transit, are carried out in accordance with the regulatory requirements of the European Union and the European Commission. title: “Aerones” Successfully Completes Offshore Robot Tests at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 14. jūnijs, 2024 “Aerones” Successfully Completes Offshore Robot Tests at the Port of Liepāja With the support of the Liepāja SEZ Authority and the Port Harbourmaster’s Office, the Latvian company Aerones successfully conducted tests on 12 and 13 June of a specialised robotic device designed to inspect the grounding systems of wind turbines offshore, before taking the technology to work in the North Sea. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis noted that this is an excellent example of how the wind energy industry creates opportunities for Latvian scientists, manufacturers and service providers to develop new technologies and services and create jobs both during wind farm construction and maintenance. Aerones is a young, fast-growing company that uses robots to maintain wind turbines around the world. Its lead engineer, Egils Gēcis, explained that the technology, software and robots themselves were all developed in Latvia by a team of local engineers. Growing demand for the maintenance of solar and wind farms has enabled the company to expand rapidly and continually recruit new employees. Aerones operates in 25 countries with 45 teams, each equipped with several robots. Until now, Aerones has worked on land, but the company has decided to test its capabilities offshore, servicing wind turbines at sea. Smart equipment that replaces people in highly hazardous work was tested at the Port of Liepāja. The port’s spacious berth provided a suitable setting to test the new robot and its technology. Aerones lead engineer Egils Gēcis emphasised that the number of turbines worldwide is increasing and it is not easy to find people to service them. “That is where robots come in. The device here at the berth is one of the many ‘helpers’ our company has developed for this purpose. The Liepāja SEZ Authority and port management gave us an opportunity to test our equipment and assess its suitability for working on water. We have an anchoring system: the anchors need to be placed with the help of a vessel, and ropes can be passed through them to control the robot. We tested it all day today, and everything went very well. Next we are heading to Scotland.” Maintaining turbines on land and at sea is not simple: they must be inspected, cleaned and periodically repaired. People normally do this work, but it is very dangerous, so the company develops and uses robots instead. “What makes this unique is that we do all of this with remotely controlled robots. It is faster, more efficient and does not put people at risk,” said Egils Gēcis. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Diversity of Cargo Types Ensures Stable Operations at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 16. maijs, 2024 Diversity of Cargo Types Ensures Stable Operations at the Port of Liepāja Stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja handled 2.54 million tonnes of cargo in the first four months of 2024, comparable to the same period in 2023. The port’s stability rests on its diversity of cargo types and traditional emphasis on locally sourced cargo. During these four months, 479 ships were served, 24,691 passengers travelled through the port, 31,945 powered and unpowered ro-ro units were transported by ferry, and 1,967 container units were handled. Locally sourced goods account for more than 50% of cargo at the Port of Liepāja. Grain and grain products, timber, wood chips, cement and ferry cargo supplied by local manufacturers are joined in spring by peat extracted in Latvia’s Kurzeme region. The port stevedoring company Mols L has successfully cooperated for four years with SIA BaltBio, whose main business is peat extraction and transport. Peat is exported from the Port of Liepāja to several European countries, including Germany and Denmark. On average, four or five vessels, each carrying just under 3,000 tonnes, are loaded every spring. According to SIA BaltBio board member Matīss Kozlovs, that is enough peat for European countries to grow tomatoes and cucumbers. “It is advantageous for our company to export peat from the port closest to the extraction site, and Mols L works quickly and efficiently.” Mols L has operated steadily in the port’s Winter Harbour for more than 30 years, handling mainly various locally sourced cargoes. Dry bulk cargo remains the largest group at the Port of Liepāja, accounting for 67% of all shipments. General cargo is the second largest group, representing 30%, or 759.2 thousand tonnes, during the first four months of the year. The largest portion of general cargo comes from the Liepāja–Travemünde ferry route. This year the route transported 608,545.25 tonnes, or 31,945 units, an increase of 15.63%. Āris Ozoliņš, Chairman of the Board of Liepāja SEZ company Terrabalt, puts it simply: “We have to work! We have diversified our risks and cargo flows. The cargo is there.” Liquid bulk is the smallest cargo group, accounting for just 3% of all shipments, or 81.2 thousand tonnes. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Port of Liepāja Services Become More Accessible
text: 04. septembris, 2026 Port of Liepāja Services Become More Accessible The Liepāja SEZ Authority, in cooperation with the Freeport of Riga Authority and the Freeport of Ventspils Authority, has completed the largest digitalisation cooperation project undertaken by Latvian ports to date. The newly developed Port and Multimodal Logistics Services Platform brings together information about vessel calls, berths, port services, permits, passes, contracts and payments in one place. It also allows users to track vessel movements in real time and use digital maps containing port infrastructure data. For Port of Liepāja customers and services, this means: faster exchange of information and data; fewer manual tasks and less repeated data entry; more convenient communication and coordination of processes; The platform is integrated with VAS “Latvijas dzelzceļš”, SKLOIS and other national and port information systems, laying the foundation for a unified digital ecosystem for Latvian ports. The project was implemented from December 2024 to August 2026. Funding of EUR 3.24 million was provided by the European Union Recovery and Resilience Facility. The project involved the Freeport of Ventspils Authority, VSIA “Latvijas Jūras administrācija”, VAS “Latvijas dzelzceļš”, the Ministry of Transport, the Coast Guard Service, the State Border Guard and SIA “Koksnes plūsmas datu centrs”. title: Port of Liepāja Stevedoring Companies Maintain Stable Cargo Turnover in the First Nine Months of the Year
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 10. oktobris, 2024 Port of Liepāja Stevedoring Companies Maintain Stable Cargo Turnover in the First Nine Months of the Year In the first nine months of 2024, stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja handled 5,247,263.28 tonnes of various cargoes, maintaining stable cargo flows and a positive balance (+1.12%). The key factors behind this stability are cargo diversity, the ability to adapt to changing circumstances and cooperation with the Liepāja SEZ Authority to attract new cargo. During the nine-month period, the Port of Liepāja served 1,000 vessels and 85,051 passengers. Dry bulk cargo amounted to 3.36 million tonnes in the first nine months of 2024, representing 64% of total throughput. From January to September, 2.27 million tonnes of grain and grain products were handled. Exports of grain grown in Latvia have remained active for the third consecutive month. Local grain growers emphasise the importance of the Port of Liepāja for grain exports, citing flexible cooperation arrangements and extensive available storage capacity. Exports of fuel wood chips and construction materials also remained stable in the dry bulk segment. The largest dry bulk terminals, LSEZ SIA “Liepaja Bulk Terminal” and LSEZ SIA “Ekers Stividors LP”, handled 1.7 million and 1.1 million tonnes respectively during the nine-month period. General cargo reached 1.69 million tonnes over the period, a steady increase of 16.5% compared with the first nine months of 2023. Ro-ro cargo remained the largest category, followed by timber. Liquid bulk cargo accounted for just 4% of total throughput at the Port of Liepāja in the first nine months of the year, or 196.9 thousand tonnes. In September, the Port of Liepāja handled 496,792.59 tonnes of cargo, including 294.6 thousand tonnes of dry bulk, 185.6 thousand tonnes of general cargo and 16.6 thousand tonnes of liquid bulk. title: Port of Liepāja Stevedoring Companies Handled 520.3 Thousand Tonnes of Cargo in January
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 13. februāris, 2025 Port of Liepāja Stevedoring Companies Handled 520.3 Thousand Tonnes of Cargo in January In January 2025, stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja maintained stable operations, handling a total of 520.3 thousand tonnes of various types of cargo. Volumes increased for timber, ro-ro cargo and construction materials, while agricultural cargo declined. Of all cargo handled in January 2025, dry bulk accounted for 63%, general cargo for 32% and liquid bulk for 5%. Ro-ro cargo traffic continued to grow on the Liepāja–Travemünde ferry route, which operates six sailings per week. The number of ro-ro units carried in January increased by 10%. Timber and roundwood throughput also rose, by 23.8% and 12.2% respectively. The decline in agricultural cargo was linked to unfavourable weather conditions and imposed import duties. Juris Matvejevs, head of LSEZ SIA “Liepaja Bulk Terminal”, explained that the anticipated decline in agricultural cargo throughput was expected and understandable. At the same time, active efforts are under way to attract new cargo categories, including from Central Asia. Cargo turnover is affected by seasonal and weather conditions as well as market demand. Moreover, an increase in working capital, rather than simply the number of tonnes handled, is a better indicator of successful and stable operations. The transit and port sectors are undergoing significant changes. For example, in January, “Norplast Piemare” began full-scale production at its newly built factory in the port area, manufacturing large fibreglass components. The company can point to a particularly small shipment weighing only 19.7 tonnes: its contribution to overall cargo tonnage was negligible, but its economic value was substantial. In 2025, the Liepāja SEZ Authority, together with port companies and strategic investors, will continue working to establish a mutually beneficial relationship between transport, logistics and manufacturing, supporting the development of new, strategically important industries that are safe for people and the environment. title: Port of Liepāja Terminals Begin Receiving Grain
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 23. jūlijs, 2024 Port of Liepāja Terminals Begin Receiving Grain On 22 July, the LSEZ SIA “Dan Store” terminal received the first wheat harvested in Latvia, signalling the start of the new grain season. Five dry bulk terminals operate actively at the Port of Liepāja, with a combined warehouse capacity of approximately 400,000 m³. Evita Dambe, Cooperation and Logistics Manager at the LSEZ SIA “Dan Store” terminal, confirmed that the first wheat shipment arrived at the terminal this morning, meaning that farmers had begun harvesting and delivering grain to the port. Grain deliveries continued throughout the day. The largest dry bulk terminal, LSEZ SIA “Liepaja Bulk Terminals”, continues to prepare for the new grain season by upgrading and improving its infrastructure, while receiving barley at warehouses on Brīvības Street in the Liepāja SEZ territory. The company’s manager, Juris Matvejevs, noted that everything is happening slightly earlier this year, but that it is still too soon to predict the quality and size of the harvest. He also said that grain would be accumulated in warehouses during August, with the busiest export period starting in September once quality and prices have been determined and contracts signed. Traditionally, 1 August is regarded as the start of the new grain season. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: Liepāja SEZ Company Attracts Strategic Investor and Changes Its Name
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 12. februāris, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Company Attracts Strategic Investor and Changes Its Name To implement a project to build a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant and CO₂ terminal, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone company GI Termināls has attracted a strategic investor and changed its name. The company will now be known as NORSAF, and its controlling shareholder is AVIA Solutions Group, registered in Ireland. Under European Union requirements, aircraft are to begin using sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), produced from renewable resources, from 2025. The EU regulation provides that SAF should account for 63% of aviation fuel use by 2050, while approximately 15% of aircraft could transition to hydrogen or fully electric propulsion, potentially for short-haul flights. Jānis Kisiels, a board member of LSEZ SIA NORSAF, emphasised that producing sustainable aviation fuel and building its supply chains currently poses a major challenge for the aviation industry. “From 2030, demand will increase every five years, requiring large-scale production and supply. We plan to produce both SAF and eSAF, some of which will contain components of non-biological origin. We have agreed with the US company KBR to purchase the technology. KBR is one of the leading engineering and design companies in the United States and worldwide in hydrocarbon processing and sustainable fuel production. It will provide patented engineering solutions and equipment for a new SAF plant with a planned capacity of up to 100,000 tonnes per year.” Jānis Kisiels also explained that the selected technology will enable a complete production cycle. Renewable electricity generated from wind and solar power will be used in electrolysis to produce green hydrogen, which will then be combined with captured CO₂ as a feedstock for SAF and eSAF. Importantly, existing infrastructure is suitable for storing and distributing sustainable aviation fuel, which can safely be used in modern aircraft. In 2024, the company signed a land lease reservation agreement with the Liepāja SEZ Authority, stating its intention to produce SAF from renewable energy and recycled raw materials. This is one of the future development projects brought together within the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said that Liepāja has succeeded in bringing together several large, capital-intensive projects that can operate in synergy within the green industry sector. “These include developing a wind farm support base at the Port of Liepāja, producing hydrogen, storing liquefied CO₂ as a feedstock for SAF, and assembling Fokker Next Gen hydrogen aircraft. These projects are under development and align with the European Green Deal. They are needed for the future, and it is important that we are already working to implement them. Project start dates range from 2027 to 2030, which is actually very close. SAF production is the next step after wind farms, hydrogen production and CO₂ capture.” Was this information useful? title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Invites Visitors to the “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 30. janvāris, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Authority Invites Visitors to the “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition From 31 January to 1 February, the “Made in Liepāja” exhibition will take place at the Liepāja Olympic Centre. More than 180 companies will present the city’s diverse business environment at their stands. The exhibition will also include a conference where experts will discuss the economic development challenges facing Latvia and Liepāja. Admission is free. School and university students are especially encouraged to attend and explore future job opportunities in Liepāja. At 11:00, Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš and Minister of Economics Viktors Valainis will open the “Made in Liepāja” exhibition and conference, followed by presentations in the Rose Hall: • At 11:10, University of Latvia professor and chair of the Latvian Strategy and Economic Solutions Institute (LaSER) Daunis Auers will discuss development scenarios for Latvia and regional economies; • At 11:40, entrepreneur and architect Uldis Pīlēns will share his experience and an inspirational story. From 13:00 to 15:15, panel discussions in the Tango Hall will explore Liepāja’s economy and future opportunities: “The Status Quo of Liepāja’s Economy — From Post-Soviet Decline to the Largest Regional Manufacturing Centre” and “What Will Liepāja’s Economy Look Like in 2040?”. Two seminars will follow: “Digitalisation in Business: Experiences and Opportunities” at 14:30 and “Innovative Thinking in Business”, a workshop for entrepreneurs led by innovation and idea management lecturer Dr Elīna Miķelsone, at 15:15. At the Liepāja SEZ Authority stand, visitors will be able to learn about the city’s industrial parks, companies operating there and the challenges of developing Liepāja’s industries of the future. The first streets in Liepāja Industrial Park, on the site of the former Liepājas Metalurgs factory, will be constructed this year. Visitors will be invited to contribute ideas and suggestions for naming the new streets. The Liepāja SEZ Authority particularly encourages young people to visit the exhibition and help shape the business environment. Together with the Education Department and the city’s general education schools, it is organising a competition inviting young people to propose ideas for the development of Liepāja’s economy. Participants must choose one of the proposed topics, prepare a presentation of their ideas using information gained at the exhibition (as a document, presentation or video), and email it to komunikacija@lsez.lv with the subject “Opinion Workshop”. Prizes will be awarded to the best entries. Competition topics: Five key things that make a company attractive to employees. What skills are needed by employees who are in demand in the labour market? Five key characteristics of Liepāja as a high-quality business environment. Where does money come from? Five risks that could negatively affect business activity. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Announces Tender for Reconstruction of Berth 46 at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 08. oktobris, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Authority Announces Tender for Reconstruction of Berth 46 at the Port of Liepāja To support the development of freight and passenger ferry routes serving the Port of Liepāja and ensure uninterrupted flows of goods, the Liepāja SEZ Authority is continuing its plans to reconstruct Berth 46. Regular ferry services are strategically important not only to Liepāja and Latvia but also to the economy and military mobility of the European Union. Last year, the berth handled 1.8 million tonnes of cargo valued at approximately EUR 4 billion. The reconstruction will allow two cargo vessels or cargo-passenger ferries, each up to 240 metres long and with a draught of up to 11 metres, to be safely served simultaneously. Work will include installing additional mooring dolphins, reconstructing berth structures and increasing water depth from 10.5 to 12.0 metres. To accommodate newer RO-RO/RO-PAX ferries, the berth will also require shore-side power supply systems and local wastewater reception facilities. Completion of the reconstruction of Berth 46 is planned by 31 December 2027. Berth 46 is situated in the Freeport area of the Port of Liepāja, in the central section of the eastern shoreline. It is 51.5 metres wide, 204.5 metres long on the northern side and 181.0 metres long on the southern side. The berth was built between 1972 and 1975 to accommodate and service Soviet naval vessels and submarines. Today, it serves the regular Liepāja–Travemünde ferry route and is subjected to considerable stress as powerful ship engines are used during berthing and departure. Reconstruction is necessary because persistent construction defects and general deterioration, despite repair work, have irreversibly affected the berth’s technical condition and operational safety. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Announces Auction for Infrastructure Serving the Oil-Contaminated Wastewater Treatment Complex
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 07. marts, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Authority Announces Auction for Infrastructure Serving the Oil-Contaminated Wastewater Treatment Complex To improve service quality and ensure efficient management, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has announced an auction for the lease of infrastructure owned by the Authority that supports the operations of the oil-contaminated wastewater treatment complex. The aim is to identify the bidder offering the most economically advantageous proposal, who will receive and treat waste delivered by vessels calling at the Port of Liepāja under sanitary fee arrangements, in accordance with MARPOL Annex I and applicable legal requirements throughout the lease period. Applications to participate in the auction may be submitted until 11 April 2025. The wastewater treatment facilities at the Port of Liepāja were commissioned in 2004 to collect and treat oily wastewater from vessels entering the port while helping protect the Baltic Sea environment. Under the Port Reception Facilities Directive, the Liepāja SEZ Authority is obliged to receive ship-generated waste, including contaminated water, although the directive does not regulate the specific treatment process. The Port of Liepāja is the only port in Latvia that treats the contaminated water it receives from ships itself. The primary function of the Liepāja SEZ Authority is to support and facilitate business activity rather than conduct commercial operations. An audit of the Authority’s functions concluded that additional services would be needed to operate the treatment facilities profitably. After examining the experience of other ports and taking into account the Law on Prevention of Squandering of the Financial Resources and Property of a Public Person, the Liepāja SEZ Authority chose a more advantageous approach to treating contaminated water from vessels and decided to auction the lease and operation of the port’s treatment facilities. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Becomes a Full Member of WindEurope
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 21. marts, 2024 Liepāja SEZ Authority Becomes a Full Member of WindEurope The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority is taking part in the annual WindEurope offshore wind energy conference and exhibition in Bilbao, Spain, from 20 to 22 March, with particular involvement in the WindEurope ports working group. Liepāja has positioned itself as a leading offshore wind support base in the Baltic Sea region, as demonstrated by the 55-hectare land reservation agreement signed with Van Oord at the Port of Liepāja. On 18 March, the Liepāja SEZ Board decided to join the wind industry association WindEurope. The Authority is now a full member and will work actively alongside more than 500 European wind industry professionals. Industry professionals have gathered for the annual WindEurope event to attend educational presentations and discussions highlighting the advantages of wind energy, learn about the latest industry developments and establish new partnerships. Latvia is represented for the first time at Europe’s leading annual wind industry conference and is among more than 500 exhibitors. The event’s motto is “Our Wind, Our Value – Creating Value for Europe, Living by European Values.” The three-day conference also addresses the preservation of biodiversity and the need to accelerate the construction of electricity grids and port infrastructure, which are essential both during offshore wind farm construction and for subsequent servicing and maintenance. On 21 March, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis shared Liepāja’s chosen development direction at the Mission Latvia stand of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), explaining its strengths as a prospective leading offshore wind support base in the Baltic Sea. “First, our geographical location is highly advantageous: all planned Baltic Sea wind farms are within a 400 km radius. Second, the inner waters of the Port of Liepāja include a development area suitable for an offshore wind support base under the city and Liepāja SEZ development plans. Third, we have both educational capacity to train specialists and industrial capacity to manufacture a range of components. News of the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s plans with Van Oord has generated considerable interest, particularly among potential investors. This means we need to explain our plans, answer questions and arrange further meetings and visits to Liepāja,” emphasised Uldis Hmieļevskis. The three-day exhibition and conference brings together more than 12,000 participants, 520 companies, 14 ministers and 400 other speakers from the wind industry, politics and academia. Discussions cover the value of wind power, jobs, nature conservation, energy security, economic competitiveness, participation by local communities and other issues. Investment in new wind farms, including those in the Baltic Sea, has grown rapidly in recent years. Ports and their infrastructure are essential support bases for constructing, servicing and maintaining those wind farms. Wind farms currently generate 19% of all electricity consumed in Europe. The EU aims to increase this figure to 35% by 2030, strengthening European energy security and independence. This means almost doubling wind power capacity over the next seven years. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Completes the Design of the Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Ivo Koliņš Head of the Port Infrastructure Projects Department Tālr: (+371) 26457292 E-pasts: ivo.kolins@lsez.lv 22. augusts, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Authority Completes the Design of the Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja The objective of the project “Ensuring Safe Mooring of Ro-Ro Ferries at the Port of Liepāja” (hereinafter the Project) is to ensure safe mooring of RO-RO ferries at the Port of Liepāja, thereby strengthening TEN-T infrastructure capacity and improving access to domestic and international markets through better maritime transport connections. On 20 September 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority and CHR Design Solutions Ltd signed a contract to prepare the construction design for “Reconstruction of Berth No. 46 at the Port of Liepāja”. On 20 August 2025, the Liepāja City Building Authority confirmed that the design conditions of building permit No. BIS-BV-4.2-2025-18 (7/2025), issued on 21 January 2025, had been fulfilled, thus confirming the completion of the design. The project involves installing additional mooring dolphins, reconstructing the berth structures and increasing the water depth from 10.5 to 12.0 metres. This will ensure the safe handling of RO-RO/RO-PAX ferries up to 240.0 metres long and with a draught of up to 11.0 metres. The total cost of implementing the project is EUR 23,090,050. The project “Ensuring Safe Mooring of Ro-Ro Ferries at the Port of Liepāja” (acronym 22-LV-TG-LPXRORO) is partly funded under the CEF2027 programme (topic ID CEF-T-2022-COMPGEN-MARP-WORKS, project No. 101122785). The Connecting Europe Facility contribution covers 30% of the eligible project costs, amounting to EUR 6,927,015. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Completes the Karosta Canal Historical Pollution Remediation Project
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 30. aprīlis, 2024 Liepāja SEZ Authority Completes the Karosta Canal Historical Pollution Remediation Project On 30 April 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Authority completed the project “Remediation Works at the Historically Contaminated Site of the Karosta Canal in the Port of Liepāja”. It was funded through the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment” and aimed to reduce the negative effects of historically contaminated sediments in the Karosta Canal on the environment, human health and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said: “The remediation of the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja is an important investment in improving environmental quality not only in the port, but also in the city and region. Every cubic metre of historically polluted sediment removed from the canal reduces the risk of pollutants entering the Baltic Sea. Even after completion of the project, the Liepāja SEZ Authority will continue to monitor and, wherever possible, improve the environmental condition of the Karosta Canal. We are particularly grateful to our project partners for their important contribution in sharing international experience and improving public understanding of historical pollution remediation in the Karosta Canal.” To achieve the project objectives, the Liepāja SEZ Authority cooperated with the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) and the association “Baltijas krasti”, which contributed the following expertise: The Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) was responsible for transferring and applying Norwegian experience in remediating polluted water bodies to the clean-up of historical pollution in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja; The association “Baltijas krasti” implemented the project’s public information activities. The following activities have been carried out under the project since 1 August 2021: Remediation of the Karosta Canal, including removal of 145,000 cubic metres of historically contaminated sediment containing 298 tonnes of hazardous chemicals from the canal bed and its transfer to the canal’s contaminated-sediment disposal site; Establishment of a sustainable Karosta Canal monitoring network; Three experience-sharing events with experts from the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA), including on remediation projects in polluted marine environments, contaminated-site management and marine pollution environmental risk assessment; Three public information campaigns about the possible effects of pollution on human health and the environment, including an international conference on the risks of climate change contributing to the spread of historical pollution and affecting Baltic Sea environmental quality; seminars on the impact of pollution in Liepāja’s Karosta Canal on the Venta river basin district and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea; the management and reduction of pollutants and their impacts on human health and the environment; a cultural-historical information day; and the preparation of informative videos and printed materials. Working together for a green Europe! The project is funded under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. The total project cost is EUR 4,737,722.26, of which EUR 4,027,063.92 is funding from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Signs Contract for Karosta Canal Remediation Works
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 03. februāris, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Authority Signs Contract for Karosta Canal Remediation Works The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority has signed a contract with Eko osta Ltd for remediation of the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja and removal of historically contaminated sediments. Under the contract, remediation must begin after the Karosta Canal remediation programme has been prepared and approved, but no later than 1 April 2023, and must be completed by 30 November 2023. Approximately 164,000 cubic metres of contaminated sediment are to be dredged at a total contract value of EUR 3,497,260.00. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is continuing the project “Remediation Works at the Historically Contaminated Site of the Karosta Canal in the Port of Liepāja” to reduce the adverse impacts of historical sediment pollution on the environment, human health and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea. The remediation will remove sediments from the canal bed that fail to meet regulatory standards and contain 400 tonnes of hazardous chemicals. The project is financed under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. “This long-planned and unique project will enable the Liepāja SEZ Authority to achieve several objectives: address environmental and ecological issues in the Baltic Sea region, remove the canal from HELCOM’s list of Baltic Sea ‘hot spots’ and create opportunities for further business development in the Karosta Canal basin and adjacent areas,” emphasised Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. Project manager Ivo Koliņš noted that the entire public would benefit from the project, as it would help achieve the objectives and measures of the Helsinki Commission (HELCOM) Baltic Sea Action Plan: restoring the Baltic Sea to good ecological status, with natural biodiversity and functioning ecosystems, a clean, healthy and productive marine environment and sustainable use of marine resources for current and future generations. As a result, Liepāja residents would no longer face risks arising from historical pollution, and both the ecological condition of the sea and overall environmental quality would improve significantly. The project continues earlier efforts to clean the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja. With EU Cohesion Fund financing, the first phase of the project, “Clean-up of the Historically Contaminated Site of the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja”, was completed by 2015. Large quantities of human-made waste, including scrap metal, concrete structures and timber, were removed and disposed of over 78 hectares of the canal. Around 60,000 cubic metres of polluted sediments were also removed from the most heavily contaminated 10-hectare section and deposited at a specially equipped site at the eastern end of the canal. The canal’s overall ecological condition improved considerably: concentrations of petroleum products and heavy metals in sediments fell several times over, although they still did not meet the requirements of Cabinet of Ministers regulations. The Karosta Canal clean-up at the Port of Liepāja is a project of European significance, and its outcomes must reflect best practice in implementing environmental protection projects. One project partner, the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA), is participating to share examples of similar remediation work in Norway and provide knowledge to Latvian specialists responsible for maintaining the achieved improvements in the future. The Karosta Canal remediation works at the Port of Liepāja will be implemented under the project “Remediation Works at the Historically Contaminated Site of the Karosta Canal in the Port of Liepāja” by the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority in cooperation with the Norwegian Institute for Water Research and the association “Baltijas krasti”. The project implementation period runs from 1 August 2021 to 31 December 2023. The project budget is EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000.00 in co-financing from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. “Working together for a green Europe” Was this information useful? title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Participates in the Largest Wind Energy Industry Exhibition
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. aprīlis, 2025 Liepāja SEZ Authority Participates in the Largest Wind Energy Industry Exhibition Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis and his adviser on renewable energy projects, Jānis Lapiņš, are attending the largest annual wind energy exhibition, “WindEurope Annual Event 2025”, in Copenhagen, Denmark, from 8 to 10 April. Over three years, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has become part of the European renewable energy ecosystem and has worked systematically, step by step, towards building an offshore wind support base at the Port of Liepāja and promoting other sustainable industry projects. Together with the management of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) and Minister for Climate and Energy Kaspars Melnis, the Liepāja SEZ Authority management met investors, project developers, manufacturers and existing partners Van Oord and Euroports over two days. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is continuing work begun three years ago on the planned offshore wind farm support base and heavy-lift cargo terminal at the Port of Liepāja. This will also enable other new projects, including manufacturing facilities on the former Liepājas Metalurgs steelworks site and services required by the wind energy industry. WindEurope is an annual event held in Copenhagen in 2025, attracting 15,000 visitors and 500 exhibitors. It is the most important annual event for the European wind energy industry, which employs 188,000 people. Denmark is the birthplace of wind energy, and the country continues to set wind power records. It is the only country in Europe to generate more than half its electricity from wind — as much as 55%. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Strengthens Cooperation with the Ports of Lübeck and Hamburg in Germany
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 17. aprīlis, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Authority Strengthens Cooperation with the Ports of Lübeck and Hamburg in Germany Port development, green energy and the strengthening of transport corridors were the main topics at the Hamburg and Lübeck Port Days, attended by Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis and adviser Jānis Lapiņš. At the Latvia–Germany Port Days in Hamburg and Lübeck on 14 and 15 April, participants discussed improving existing cooperation in logistics, sustainable energy and the transformation of port development. Renewable energy, its successful transmission and use depend largely on effectively combining expertise in industry, energy and maritime affairs. Liepāja and Lübeck’s outer port of Travemünde are directly connected by the Stena Line ferry service six times a week. The route is often referred to as an extension of the German motorway network. The Liepāja SEZ Authority signed a cooperation agreement with the Port of Lübeck Authority in 2016 and with the Port of Hamburg in 2021. The Latvian delegation was led by Minister of Transport Atis Švinka. The visit concluded with a Latvia–Germany Port Days forum. During a panel discussion, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis highlighted the importance of long-standing partnerships and innovation for strengthening port competitiveness, safety and sustainability, as well as future joint projects. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is already actively involved in developing the Baltic–Germany electricity interconnector, with Liepāja identified as a potential onshore connection point. An agreement has also recently been concluded on developing a Nordic–Baltic hydrogen ecosystem linked to Germany, again identifying Liepāja as an onshore connection point. According to Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis, these developments would create opportunities for Latvia to export wind and solar electricity while opening the door to new energy-intensive investment projects in Liepāja. The Latvia–Germany Port Days aimed to promote cooperation between German and Latvian transport and logistics companies by discussing current industry issues, strengthening existing contacts in person and establishing new business relationships among port authorities and companies from both countries. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Developing the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 22. novembris, 2024 Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Developing the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre European Hydrogen Week has concluded in Brussels. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis attended to discuss planned projects in the Liepāja SEZ with cooperation partners. The projects involve using renewable resources to produce hydrogen, which could then be used in CO2 processing, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production and, potentially, a hydrogen-powered aircraft manufacturing facility. Together, these initiatives form the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre. On 20 November, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), in cooperation with the Latvian Embassy in Brussels and Baltic hydrogen organisations, hosted a reception bringing together the Baltic hydrogen community and its partners. Speakers included Mārtiņš Kreitus, Latvia’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the European Union; Aivars Starikovs, Director of the Latvian Hydrogen Association and a board member of Hydrogen Europe; and Egita Aizsilniece-Ibema, Head of the Latvian Innovation and Technology Representation in Brussels. The four-day conference and exhibition featured discussions and networking. More than 220 exhibitors presented innovative technologies, national and regional ambitions, and market-ready products. Key conclusions: Improve links between hydrogen and the energy sector; Connect stakeholders throughout the value chains; Develop the necessary infrastructure and provide appropriate financial support for assets that can ensure grid flexibility. According to the official European Hydrogen Week statement, the event brought together participants from across Europe’s hydrogen sector and promoted knowledge exchange and business development planning. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Improving Infrastructure for Fishermen at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. janvāris, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Improving Infrastructure for Fishermen at the Port of Liepāja When weather conditions become suitable for construction, the Liepāja SEZ Authority will begin building an access road to Berth No. 92. The work is financed by the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Action Programme 2021–2027. The project will create a publicly accessible 364-metre road at the Port of Liepāja, including smart lighting and stormwater drainage. Following procurement, the work will be carried out by CTB Ltd, which submitted the most economically advantageous tender of EUR 303,617.32. The project is scheduled for completion by 31 December 2026. Access to Berth No. 92 is currently practically impossible, preventing fishermen from making full use of it. The Authority has agreed with fish-processing company Syfud on amendments to the lease agreement and secured funding from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund to begin road construction in spring, once weather permits. CTB Ltd will build publicly accessible infrastructure — road surfacing, stormwater drainage and lighting — providing a modern, safe and efficient transport link between the city and the Port of Liepāja and supporting fisheries development and exports. The project aims to improve access to port berths, develop a sustainable blue economy and support fishing and aquaculture communities. The road will lead to a fish landing site used by coastal fishermen and improve access to coastal facilities. For reference: Project funding is provided by the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Action Programme 2021–2027, measure U31421.2 “Strengthening the Development of Port Infrastructure”, sub-measure U31421.2.01, Action 1. On 8 November 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Authority received Rural Support Service Decision No. 10.9.2-11/24/3984-e approving project No. 24-00-UL05-U31421.201-000003, “Construction of an Access Road at the Port of Liepāja”. The project supports strategic objective SM2 of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Development Plan 2023–2035: maintaining and improving the competitiveness of the Port of Liepāja, including maintaining and developing port infrastructure to support fisheries enterprises. The project is consistent with Action R1 “Strengthening Port Infrastructure Development” under strategic objective M4 of the Liepāja District Partnership’s Community-Led Local Development Strategy 2023–2027.
