title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Improving Infrastructure for Fishermen at the Port
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 25. marts, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Improving Infrastructure for Fishermen at the Port The Liepāja SEZ Authority has started building an access road to Berth No. 92, co-financed by the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Action Programme 2021–2027. The project provides for a publicly accessible 364-metre road with smart lighting and stormwater drainage. CTB Ltd, which submitted the most economically advantageous tender of EUR 303,617.32, is carrying out the work. Under the contract, construction must be completed by 1 September 2026. Berth No. 92 forms part of Liepāja’s historic fishing port, but access was blocked after a fish-canning plant expanded during the Soviet era, preventing coastal fishermen from using it properly. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis explained that after the plant changed owners, the Authority agreed with the new owner, Syfud, to amend the lease agreement and clearly designate the access road. “The road to the berth had been identified, but it took several more years to secure financing from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund. The active construction season has begun, and work on the new road is now in full swing so that it can be ready by the end of summer.” CTB Ltd will construct publicly accessible infrastructure — road surfacing, a stormwater drainage network and lighting — creating a modern, safe and efficient transport connection between the city and the Port of Liepāja and promoting fisheries development and exports. The aim is to improve access to port berths, support the sustainable blue economy and develop fishing and aquaculture communities. The road will provide access to a fish landing site for coastal fishermen and improve access to coastal facilities. In the second half of the year, the Authority will also launch another project to reconstruct Berth No. 92 in two stages with co-financing from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund. For reference: Project funding is provided by the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Action Programme 2021–2027, measure U31421.2 “Strengthening the Development of Port Infrastructure”, sub-measure U31421.2.01, Action 1. On 8 November 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Authority received Rural Support Service Decision No. 10.9.2-11/24/3984-e approving project No. 24-00-UL05-U31421.201-000003, “Construction of an Access Road at the Port of Liepāja”. The project supports strategic objective SM2 of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Development Plan 2023–2035: maintaining and improving the competitiveness of the Port of Liepāja, including maintaining and developing port infrastructure to support fisheries enterprises. The project is consistent with Action R1 “Strengthening Port Infrastructure Development” under strategic objective M4 of the Liepāja District Partnership’s Community-Led Local Development Strategy 2023–2027. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Plans for an Offshore Wind Energy Industry Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea
text: 20. septembris, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues Plans for an Offshore Wind Energy Industry Hub in the Eastern Baltic Sea At a seminar organised by LIAA on 20 September on the business potential of offshore wind energy in Latvia, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis outlined progress towards creating an offshore wind support base at the Port of Liepāja and developing an industry hub in the eastern Baltic Sea region, supported by manufacturing and logistics capacity as well as education and specialist training. Under the Baltic Sea spatial plan, five potential offshore wind farm sites have been identified in Latvian waters, all within 100 km of Liepāja; the planned wind farms of all three Baltic states lie within a 250 km radius. As Hmieļevskis emphasised at the seminar, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has been working for some time towards its objective of becoming an offshore wind energy industry hub in the eastern Baltic Sea region. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said: “None of the ports on the eastern Baltic coast currently has suitable infrastructure: at least 15–20 hectares of space with two 200-metre berths capable of handling heavy loads. We believe Latvian port infrastructure should be used to build Latvian projects, and Liepāja has everything needed to create it — available land inside the port basin and favourable geotechnical ground conditions providing the required load-bearing capacity. With this in mind, we have prepared a development concept for the Port of Liepāja’s Outer Harbour, providing for the first-stage development of 39 hectares. We have developed a technical solution, identified the investments needed, and prepared an implementation roadmap and timetable. The project would take four years to deliver, which fits the planned construction schedules for offshore wind farms in the region while leaving some contingency time.” At the beginning of the seminar, LIAA’s ELWIND project managers discussed opportunities in Latvia’s offshore wind value chain, current developments in the ELWIND project and planned procurements. Latvia enjoys a unique geographic position in the middle of the Baltic Sea, with strong prevailing winds and comparatively shallow waters. The country’s offshore wind energy potential is approximately 15 GW, the largest among its neighbours. The current maritime spatial plan earmarks five areas for offshore wind farm development, and additional areas may be designated in the future. But what does this potential mean for the local economy? Some Latvian businesses already participate in the offshore wind value chain by training specialists, supplying raw materials to component manufacturers and servicing wind farms. As the sector expands rapidly, shortages are emerging at various stages of the value chain, creating excellent opportunities for Latvian businesses to help address them. Was this information useful? title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues the Karosta Canal Remediation Project
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 20. septembris, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Authority Continues the Karosta Canal Remediation Project On 19 and 20 September this year, experts from the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority and the association Baltic Coasts visited Oslo on a study exchange and met project partners from the Norwegian Institute for Water Research under project No. NFI/AK/02, “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja.” The purpose of the exchange was to gain further experience in successfully applying monitored natural recovery, or natural self-cleaning, to the Karosta Canal following the remediation works planned under the project. The approach will make use of naturally occurring biodegradation processes that reduce the bioavailability or toxicity of pollutants in the sediments. Working together for a green Europe! title: Liepāja SEZ Authority and Fokker Next Gen N.V. Sign a Memorandum of Cooperation
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. decembris, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Authority and Fokker Next Gen N.V. Sign a Memorandum of Cooperation The memorandum of cooperation sets out the stages of a project to develop a new hydrogen-powered aircraft. These include establishing a centre of excellence in hydrogen aircraft operations engineering in Latvia, focusing on ground handling, airport infrastructure and hydrogen infrastructure. For the development and manufacture of next-generation aircraft, Fokker Next Gen N.V. also intends to establish in Latvia a centre of excellence for hydrogen aircraft operations, focusing on ground handling, as well as a maintenance and documentation support centre to prepare documentation for airlines and aircraft maintenance facilities. The plans also include a final assembly line operating alongside the main assembly line in the Netherlands. Fokker Next Gen N.V. recognises the advantages of the Liepāja SEZ and, through this memorandum, expresses its interest in conducting a feasibility study for a final assembly facility for new hydrogen-powered aircraft at Liepāja International Airport (LPX), which is within the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. Fokker Next Gen N.V. CEO Juriaan Kellermann outlined the company’s plans: “The well-equipped Liepāja Airport, with extensive land suitable for our assembly line, is an excellent potential location for our facility. Its direct maritime connection with the Netherlands and expected proximity to future hydrogen production plants are significant advantages. The business-friendly environment in the region could also be highly favourable for our operations. We are excited about the opportunity to work with the Liepāja Special Economic Zone and other stakeholders to build a strong aviation ecosystem in Latvia. This initiative aims to support a possible final assembly line in Liepāja in the future, operating alongside the line in the Netherlands and significantly expanding our ability to manufacture innovative hydrogen-powered aircraft.” Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis noted that Liepāja has historically been one of Latvia’s leading regional industrial centres, with rich traditions and experience. Over the last 25 years the city has built an integrated, high-quality business environment combining the port, manufacturing, airport, road and rail access, something appreciated by the Dutch company Fokker Next Gen N.V. Hmieļevskis added: “Liepāja also has a history of aircraft manufacturing. About a century ago, some 15 aircraft for the Latvian Aizsargi organisation were built at the Tosmare ship-repair plant, then known as the Naval Port Workshops. The aircraft were transported on rafts to the Liepāja Northern Airfield on the other side of the Karosta Canal for test flights. Liepāja can do it today, too.” To advance such an ambitious project in Latvia, Fokker Next Gen N.V. CEO Juriaan Kellermann also signed a memorandum with Riga Technical University Rector Tālis Juhna, expressing an interest in jointly expanding research and innovation capabilities and developing a regional aviation innovation ecosystem, including efforts to attract national and international funding for education, research and innovation. Building a hydrogen aircraft operations engineering centre of excellence in Latvia will require drawing on existing scientific and educational expertise through high-level research, EU and other external funding, and commercialisation of research results so innovative technologies can reach the market. Developing highly skilled human capital is equally important. The Dutch company Fokker Next Gen also signed a memorandum with Latvia’s Ministry of Economics, contributing to the development of a green-energy cluster on the Kurzeme coast. “Through this project, Fokker Next Gen will accelerate the development of hydrogen technologies. This is especially relevant in the context of the ELWIND offshore wind farm, as it could stimulate future demand for hydrogen fuel,” said Iveta Strupkāja, Acting Director of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, adding that several other companies have also expressed readiness to participate in the hydrogen cluster. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority Begins Removing Historical Pollution from the Karosta Canal
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 13. aprīlis, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Authority Begins Removing Historical Pollution from the Karosta Canal The Liepāja SEZ Authority continues implementing the project “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja,” aiming to reduce the harmful impact of historically polluted sediments on the environment, human health and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea. The remediation contractor is EKO OSTA Ltd, which submitted the most economically advantageous tender and was awarded the contract. The work involves dredging approximately 164,000 m³ of contaminated sediments at a total contract value of EUR 3,497,260. The project is financed under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment.” The Karosta Canal remediation programme was approved in early April. EKO OSTA Ltd mobilised the necessary equipment and began removing contaminated sediment from the canal, with completion scheduled by 30 November 2023. The work will remove sediment that fails to meet legal standards and contains approximately 400 tonnes of hazardous chemical substances. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis explained that the Karosta Canal environmental remediation project differs significantly from the Authority’s other projects: while it also supports development, it must first deal with the Soviet military legacy. “Environmental and ecological issues matter greatly. That is why it is so important to remove sediment from the Karosta Canal bed, where almost the entire periodic table can be found, and eliminate this HELCOM Baltic Sea hotspot. It is a long-planned, unique project that will make a cleaner environment possible, end concerns about oil slicks in the Karosta Canal and allow active business development in the canal basin and surrounding areas.” The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority warns that rainbow-coloured films of petroleum products may be visible on the Karosta Canal during the work. The contractor, Eko Osta Ltd, will collect these and ensure contaminated sediments are deposited only in the designated area. The project will help achieve the objectives and actions of the Helsinki Commission (HELCOM) Baltic Sea Action Plan: restoring a good ecological condition in the Baltic Sea, with natural biodiversity and dynamics, clean, healthy and productive waters, and sustainable use of the marine environment for present and future generations. The results will reduce residents’ exposure to historical pollution and substantially improve marine ecology and the surrounding environment. This project continues previous efforts to clean the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja. With EU Cohesion Fund support, the first phase of the project, “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja,” was completed by 2015. Large quantities of man-made debris, including scrap metal, concrete structures and wood, were removed and disposed of across 78 hectares. About 60,000 m³ of contaminated sediment was also removed from the most polluted ten-hectare area and deposited in a specially equipped facility at the eastern end of the canal. Cleaning the Karosta Canal is a project of European significance, so its outcomes must follow best practice in environmental protection. One of the partners, the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA), will share experience from similar remediation projects in Norway and provide expertise to Latvian specialists responsible for maintaining the improvements over time. The work is implemented by the Liepāja SEZ Authority together with NIVA and the Baltic Coasts association. Working together for a green Europe! The project is financed by the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment.” Total project costs amount to EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000 in Norwegian Financial Mechanism funding. title: Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2026 Budget Focuses on Development
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 10. februāris, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2026 Budget Focuses on Development The Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2026 budget has been prepared conservatively and in a balanced manner, ensuring the performance of its core functions while continuing development-oriented investment projects in the port and industrial areas. The strategic priorities for 2026 are greater operational efficiency, infrastructure construction, digital port management and stronger cybersecurity. The Liepāja SEZ Board has approved a 2026 budget with planned turnover of EUR 17.9 million. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis stresses that the priority this year is to maintain stable operations in uncertain conditions. “This year we will continue work on reconstructing Berth No. 46, significantly increasing the port’s long-term competitiveness. We will continue developing infrastructure required by fishermen, constructing an access road to Berth No. 92 under a Rural Support Service project and reconstructing the berth itself. In 2026 we will continue supporting the growth and expansion of existing businesses, constructing streets and utility networks in the Liepāja Industrial Park and improving existing infrastructure. We will also continue environmentally sustainable investments, including remediation of contaminated areas at the former Liepājas metalurgs factory.” In 2026 the Authority will continue working with developers on sustainable industrial projects aimed at climate neutrality, reducing CO2 emissions and producing and using renewable energy. The Authority’s budget revenue comes from port activities and property lease payments, as well as investment and financial activities and international projects. Expenditure covers core activities intended to boost economic activity, attract investment and maintain and construct infrastructure, creating a high-quality business environment. Finance Director Ilze Rendniece notes the importance of a balanced budget with prudent revenue and expenditure forecasts, ensuring core operating costs and the fulfilment of financial and EU project commitments. The budget is based on a projected cargo turnover of 6.9 million tonnes in 2026 and existing property lease agreements. The Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2026 budget is a financial plan for implementing its development priorities and securing the long-term competitiveness of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone as a unified economic ecosystem: 1. Maintenance and development of port infrastructure. Reconstruction of Berths No. 46, 92 and 82 at the Port of Liepāja. Development of infrastructure for the safe mooring of RO-RO ferries. Maintaining sufficient water depths in the port basin. Construction of an access road for fishermen. Maintenance of railway infrastructure, buildings and watercraft. Objective: ensure stable port operations with annual cargo turnover of 6.9 million tonnes, increase capacity and competitiveness, and attract new cargo. 2. Development of industrial areas. Construction of streets and utilities in the Liepāja Industrial Park. Construction of sections of Martena Street and Eksporta Street. Cleaning up and remediating industrial areas, including demolition of derelict structures. Objective: attract new investors and increase economic activity. 3. Digital transformation and cybersecurity. Creation of a digital port management system. Digitalisation of security systems. Measures to meet cybersecurity requirements. Objective: improve operational efficiency and reduce security risks. 4. Environmental safety and sustainability. Compliance with environmental and safety requirements. Environmental quality monitoring in the port area. Dismantling the fuel-oil storage facility and remediating contaminated soil at the former Liepājas metalurgs plant. Objective: ensure environmental sustainability and reduce ecological risks. 5. Financial stability and sustainability. Fulfilling existing commitments and investment projects. 6. Strengthening staff qualifications and capacity. Ensuring continuity of expertise and conducting necessary certification and training. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: LAMPwood and PLIX Receive the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s Special Recognition Awards
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. aprīlis, 2026 LAMPwood and PLIX Receive the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s Special Recognition Awards For the second year in a row, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has participated in judging the national final of Latvia’s best student-run companies, awarding its special recognition prize in both the lower-secondary and upper-secondary categories. This year, the lower-secondary award went to LAMPwood for creating a sustainable and distinctive interior product — a lamp. The judges also praised its aesthetically designed stand, engaging logo, confident presentation, cohesive team, growth-oriented approach and products reflecting the spirit of Liepāja. LAMPwood is a student company from Liepāja State Gymnasium, founded by Raivo Egmanis and Emīlija Betrama. The upper-secondary award went to PLIX for developing and manufacturing a compact plastic recycling machine — a sustainable solution supporting the circular economy. The team demonstrated innovative improvements to the equipment, mastered the necessary production software and adopted a knowledge-, experimentation- and development-based approach. PLIX is a student company from Riga State Technical School, whose members are Marks Žihars, Laura Krasņikova and Tomass Lībenzobs. Student-run companies offer young people the chance to learn their first business skills while still at school, taking a product from idea to sale. Students from Liepāja have always been active and achieved strong results. These companies encourage and promote entrepreneurship through practical learning, sparking curiosity, building confidence and motivating students to pursue new goals. From 27 to 28 April, Liepāja hosts “Gen-E” Young Entrepreneurs Days, the national final for Latvia’s student-run companies, organised by the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) and Junior Achievement Latvia (JA Latvia). Over two days, 31 of the country’s best teams will present their products and business ideas, competing for the chance to represent Latvia at the European final in Riga this year. Over the two days, teams from 31 of Latvia’s best student-run companies will present their products and business ideas, competing for the chance to represent Latvia at this year’s European final in Riga. Ten lower-secondary and 21 upper-secondary student-run companies have qualified, having demonstrated outstanding product development, entrepreneurial thinking and presentation skills throughout the academic year. title: Liepāja SEZ CEO Visits KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 05. marts, 2025 Liepāja SEZ CEO Visits KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm The technology planned for the sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production facility at the Port of Liepāja was developed by the Swedish company Swedish Biofuels AB together with scientists from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and grant funding from the US military sector. A prototype plant in Stockholm, located on the university campus alongside classrooms and laboratories, combines carbon and hydrogen molecules to produce around 3,000 tonnes of sustainable fuel annually. According to Swedish Biofuels AB, its technologies offer a viable alternative to fossil fuels, helping aviation, transport, industry and business move towards a more responsible and secure future. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis stressed the importance of examining every project planned for Liepāja in depth. “Detailed discussions with technology suppliers and investors allow us to assess the nature of a project, its economic benefits, safety, environmental impacts and other considerations. Together with municipal and SEZ experts, I take this approach for practically every major project to ensure a new plant fits into the city without creating inconvenience or risk. That is why environmental and safety questions were a key part of our discussions. Green fuel itself is colourless and practically odourless before fragrance additives are introduced, since impurities do not enter the product during manufacturing.” “Seeing the fuel plant itself and the meticulous approach used to develop the technology and documentation for other facilities, it is clear that everything is handled responsibly. Fuel production takes place literally next door to lecture rooms and a coffee area, without noise, smells or smoke. That answers many concerns from the outset. Why is this fuel needed? Aviation is one of the world’s major CO₂ emitters, and Europe has set a goal of using green SAF fuel for 65% of flights by 2050. For Liepāja, this is an opportunity to become a centre for future industries, create jobs, open new research opportunities for scientists at RTU Liepāja Academy and enable other businesses to develop the next generation of technologies,” said Hmieļevskis. The SAF plant at the Port of Liepāja is planned by LSEZ SIA NorSAF. KBR, one of the largest US energy technology companies, with turnover exceeding USD 6 billion and experience in the space, energy and defence industries, has been engaged to produce and install equipment based on the technology. title: Businesses Operating in the Liepāja SEZ Review the Past Year
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 11. decembris, 2024 Businesses Operating in the Liepāja SEZ Review the Past Year On 10 December, entrepreneurs operating in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone gathered for their traditional year-end event to review the year’s achievements, share experiences and discuss cooperation for the coming year. The Liepāja SEZ Authority has organised the annual event since 2013. Like several preceding years, 2024 presented businesses with major challenges, demanding creative approaches to maintain continuity and stability. Addressing representatives of transport, logistics and manufacturing businesses in the Liepāja SEZ, CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis thanked everyone for their work during the year and their determination to drive Liepāja’s economic development. The Liepāja Special Economic Zone is a business area shaped by the companies that work, develop, collaborate, create jobs and build modern production facilities there. These activities generate stable revenue for state and municipal budgets and support the socioeconomic development and well-being of the city and region. Traditionally, businesses that achieved something significant during the past year were honoured. 2024 SUSTAINABILITY AWARD — AE PARTNER LSEZ SIA For sustainable business practices and responsible resource use 2024 BUILDING AWARD — NORPLAST PIEMARE LSEZ AS For constructing a new production facility at the port 2024 BOLD INITIATIVE AWARD — SIA ULTIMA For the ability to adapt to unconventional freight transport solutions 2024 INVESTMENT AWARD — SIA ICS PROPERTY For local investment in manufacturing development 2024 INVESTMENT AWARD — SIA ICS STEEL For local investment in manufacturing development 2024 INVESTMENT AWARD — SIA SYFUD For the largest investment Businesses received an award created by artist Herberts Erbs, combining Liepāja’s strong industrial and port traditions with a vision of a sustainable future. About the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority: The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority creates a high-quality, attractive business environment and advances the zone’s development through coordinated management and transparent conditions. It attracts entrepreneurs and investors working in smart, sustainable, high-value-added sectors, especially manufacturing, green energy and technology, creating skilled jobs with competitive pay. title: New ICS Steel Production Building Completed in the Liepāja SEZ
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. janvāris, 2024 New ICS Steel Production Building Completed in the Liepāja SEZ ICS Steel Ltd began developing its factory concept in 2018, demonstrating how a hobby can become a business. Co-owner Ingus Sudmalis from Liepāja originally enjoyed chrome-plating metal parts in his workshop and soon discovered strong demand for the service. As the company’s production manager, Sudmalis said that this encouraged him to establish the business and plan its own production facility. The new facility is designed to provide various metal surface treatments, including galvanising, chrome plating, nickel plating and electropolishing. ICS Steel began operations in rented premises at the Liepāja Business Centre in 2022. The company currently employs 22 people and expects to expand its workforce in response to demand for metalworking services. Board member Uldis Klapers stressed that Liepāja has many metalworking companies, both existing and prospective customers. “Demand is strong because companies today need to optimise costs and time as much as possible. High-quality metal surface coating was previously unavailable in Liepāja, so manufacturers sent their parts abroad for finishing. Now ICS Steel can coat parts made by Liepāja’s metalworking companies with the necessary materials quickly and to a high standard.” It took around five years to turn the original idea into a new factory, overcoming various obstacles along the way, but the result was worth it. ICS Steel worked closely with the Liepāja SEZ Authority to bring the plan to life. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said he was pleased to see local entrepreneurs building new factories alongside Scandinavian-owned companies. “It is essential for Latvian-owned companies to develop in Liepāja and throughout Latvia, because that also demonstrates the strength of our country’s economy.” ICS Steel continues testing new equipment at its facility and plans to reach full production capacity in March. Production manager Ingus Sudmalis is confident that within two years ICS Steel will be the strongest company in its field in the Baltics. “We have Europe’s largest electropolishing line for stainless steel. The only other comparable line is across the ocean, in America. No one else can process components of this size; we are unique in that regard. We developed an innovative technical solution to make it possible, because previously it could hardly be done.” As it plans further expansion, ICS Steel intends to build two additional production buildings next to the new factory over the coming years. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 13 October
text: 16. oktobris, 2023 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 13 October On 13 October 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Board held its regular meeting, reviewing and supporting three investment projects by Liepāja SEZ companies totalling EUR 446,531.76 and considering several issues relating to property, leases, rights of first refusal and disposals. Long-term land lease agreement The Liepāja SEZ Board decided to conclude a 20-year land lease agreement with Latvijas Mobilais Telefons Ltd for the property at 18 Atmodas Boulevard in Liepāja. The 600 m² plot will be used to operate and maintain a mobile telecommunications base station with a radio tower and conduct associated commercial activities. Rights of first refusal The Liepāja SEZ Board decided not to exercise its right of first refusal for the property at 2 Zviedru Street in Liepāja, situated within the SEZ, because it is not needed for the Authority’s functions. Disposal of real estate The Board agreed to the disposal of the plot at 1A Cukura Street in Liepāja because it is not needed for the Authority’s functions. Implementation of investment projects The Board reviewed and supported three investment projects by Liepāja SEZ companies totalling EUR 446,531.76. MetARS plans to purchase welding equipment and a welding fume filtration system for EUR 8,761.76. The project is scheduled for 20 October 2023 to 31 December 2024. According to its business declaration, MetARS is a small enterprise and may receive the maximum permitted aid intensity of 60% for these investments. LIEPAJA BULK TERMINAL LTD continues investing in measures to prevent dust from cargo handling from spreading beyond the terminal. Between 20 October 2023 and 31 August 2025, the company plans a ship-loader aspiration system to collect dust, at a total cost of EUR 349,770. LIEPAJA BULK TERMINAL LTD is a large enterprise and is eligible for a maximum aid intensity of 40%. The Board also supported an investment project by Ekers Stividors LP Ltd to purchase and install a bulk handling grab for fine-fraction cargo. The project is planned for 18 October to 1 December 2023, at a total cost of EUR 38,000. According to its declaration, Ekers Stividors LP is a medium-sized enterprise and the maximum permitted aid intensity is 50%. By this point in 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority had concluded 11 investment agreements with SEZ companies, with total planned investment of EUR 4,835,371.52. Was this information useful? title: Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 15 July
text: 16. jūlijs, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 15 July At its regular meeting on 15 July this year, the Liepāja SEZ Board approved the Authority’s 2025 annual report and decided not to exercise rights of first refusal, to conclude a new ship agency agreement and to award several procurement contracts. Approval of the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2025 annual report The Board approved the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2025 annual report. Turnover for the reporting year was EUR 17.14 million, EUR 1.72 million higher than the previous year, and the year ended with a profit of EUR 1.01 million. Port dues were the largest source of revenue. As a multifunctional port, the Port of Liepāja has maintained stable cargo turnover averaging around 7 million tonnes annually over the past decade. In 2025, the port handled 6.9 million tonnes, with locally generated cargo accounting for more than 52%. New food-related liquid cargoes were attracted from Central Asia. The port served 1,154 vessels and 99,942 passengers. Rights of first refusal The Board decided not to exercise its right of first refusal for a warehouse building forming part of the property at 103C Brīvības Street in Liepāja, within the SEZ. The transaction is a sale between 2 G projekts Ltd and RĀDAL Ltd for EUR 45,000 excluding VAT. The property was assessed as unnecessary for the Authority’s functions. Ship agency services agreement The Board decided to conclude an agreement with Brenners Shipping Ltd for ship agency services at the Port of Liepāja. After reviewing the submitted documents, the Harbour Master’s Service found that the company met the requirements for concluding such agreements and could begin providing ship agency services. Charter of a multifunctional vessel The Board decided to conclude a charter agreement with LVR Flote Ltd for a multifunctional vessel. The vessel selected through procurement will maintain floating navigation aids and port infrastructure, break ice and serve as a replacement pilot boat. Purchase of a multibeam echo sounder system The Board decided to conclude a EUR 158,500 contract excluding VAT with GeoStar Ltd for the supply and installation of a multibeam echo sounder system for the Liepāja SEZ Authority. It will be fitted to the Authority’s boat Pērkone to measure depths in port waters and support safe vessel navigation. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 15 September
text: 15. septembris, 2023 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 15 September At its regular meeting on 15 September 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Board adopted four decisions. It amended the Karosta Canal remediation agreement, extended the contract for maintaining navigable channels and depths in the port basin, decided to conclude a novation agreement and supported an investment agreement with Terrabalt LSEZ Ltd. Extension of an agreement The Liepāja SEZ Board decided to sign an amendment agreement with AQUATEX Ltd to the contract concluded on 11 October 2022 for maintenance of navigable channels and depths in the Port of Liepāja, exercising the contractual option to extend it for up to one year. After reviewing progress on the Karosta Canal remediation project and the circumstances affecting it, the Board decided to extend the contract by 31 calendar days. On 18 July 2023, a FAB-500 aerial bomb manufactured in 1952 was discovered during contaminated sediment remediation works in the canal, interrupting operations for several days. The work is now being carried out with maximum safety precautions, considerably slowing the previously planned daily volume of sediment removal and transport to the disposal site. Implementation of an investment project The Board decided to conclude an agreement with Terrabalt LSEZ Ltd for the investment project “Purchase of a New MAFI R 332 Terminal Tractor”, to be implemented between 21 September 2023 and 30 June 2025 at a total cost of EUR 192,000. Novation of an agreement The Board decided to conclude a novation agreement for lease rights, replacing the obligations under the lease concluded on 1 April 2004 between the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepaja Bulk Terminal LTD LSEZ Ltd for the property at 41 Atslēdznieku Street in Liepāja. Baltic System Transport Ltd will replace Liepaja Bulk Terminal LTD LSEZ Ltd as the contracting party. The basis is the sale agreement of 11 April 2023, under which Baltic System Transport Ltd became the new owner of the property; the ownership was registered in the Land Register by the Kurzeme District Court. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 17 January
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 18. janvāris, 2024 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 17 January Liepāja SEZ company status The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed and approved Crimppi Ltd’s application and documents requesting Liepāja SEZ company status. Crimppi, a leading Finnish manufacturer of wiring harnesses and electronic components, plans to open a factory in Liepāja at the Vecās Ostmalas Biznesa Parks LSEZ Ltd site as early as this spring. Implementation of investment projects The Board reviewed and supported three investment projects by Liepāja SEZ companies, totalling EUR 2,710,053.47. Crimppi Ltd plans to establish a production facility in Liepāja by 31 December 2026, investing in modern technologies and purchasing two production machines for EUR 222,208.94. Baltic Biofuel Company LSEZ Ltd plans to implement the investment project “Open-Sided Shelter” by 31 December 2024, at a total cost of EUR 37,844.53. Norplast Piemare LSEZ JSC plans to build a production building at 37 Atslēdznieku Street in the Port of Liepāja by 31 December 2025. The investment project amounts to EUR 2,450,000. In 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded 15 investment agreements with SEZ companies, with total planned investments of EUR 5,481,903.28. Agreement on commercial activities The Board reviewed and supported a three-year business plan submitted by GF Powdercoating LSEZ Ltd for operations in the Liepāja SEZ, specifying projected net turnover, the number of jobs and the company’s average wages for 2024–2026. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 June
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 20. jūnijs, 2024 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 June On 18 June 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Board held its regular meeting. It considered eight agenda items, adopted six decisions and heard information reports on Liepāja SEZ operations and planned development projects. Investment agreement. The Board considered an application by JM Properties, a Liepāja SEZ company, for the project “Construction of a New Production Building at 11 Virssardzes Street, Liepāja” and supported its implementation from 19 June 2024 to 31 December 2025, for a total of EUR 6.5 million. JM Properties is a property developer, and the new facility will support the expansion of Jensen Metal’s production. Amendments to property agreements. The Board decided to extend until 31 January 2025 the agreement with BaltEx Bulk concerning reservation of the land plot at 7 Pulvera Street, Liepāja, in the Liepāja SEZ. The purpose is to prepare a minimum-composition construction design for the “Construction of a Cargo Area at 5 Pulvera Street, Liepāja”. The Board also permitted KB Tosmare to sublet approximately 400 m² of land at 42/44 Ģenerāļa Baloža Street to Tolmets Kurzeme, subject to the lease concluded between the Liepāja SEZ Authority and KB Tosmare on 3 November 2021. The Board also consented to the mortgaging of the building rights granted to ICS Property under its 29 April 2019 agreement with the Liepāja SEZ Authority, as security for obligations, in accordance with that agreement. Demolition of a building. To continue developing the Liepāja Industrial Park, create new industrial development areas and begin infrastructure construction on the former Liepājas metalurgs site, integrating the area into Liepāja’s urban structure and returning it to economic use through environmentally friendly and sustainable industrial development in line with the local plan and Development Plan, the Board approved the demolition of a minor structure at 94A Brīvības Street, Liepāja. Free-zone status. The Board supported the request by Norplast Piemare, a Liepāja SEZ joint-stock company, to grant free-zone status to its territory at 11/13 Kaiju Street, Liepāja, and to revoke free customs zone certificate No. 13 for Port of Liepāja Berth 64/65 and certificate No. 15 for Berths 73/74/75/76. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 March
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 18. marts, 2024 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 March 2024. gada 18. martā notika kārtējā Liepājas speciālās ekonomiskās zonas (Liepājas SEZ) valdes sēde, kurā izskatīja un atbalstīja Liepājas SEZ kapitālsabiedrības statusa piešķiršanu SIA “AE Partner”, trīs Liepājas SEZ kapitālsabiedrību ieguldījumu projektus par kopējo summu 5,41 milj. EUR, pieņēma lēmumus par nekustamo īpašumu pirmpirkuma tiesībām un precizēja ilgtermiņa nomas līgumu. Tāpat Liepājas SEZ valde nolēma iestāties biedrībā “WindEurope”. Liepāja SEZ company status To continue growing and implement the investment project “Construction of a New Production and Administrative Building at 1/3 Ganību Street, Liepāja”, AE Partner decided to enter into an agreement to conduct business in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone and become a Liepāja SEZ company. AE Partner is a Danish-owned company operating in Liepāja since 2003. In recent years its output and turnover have increased significantly, with annual turnover exceeding EUR 74 million. It is one of Liepāja’s largest employers, employing 540 people. The company produces high-quality automation systems and designs and manufactures electrical panels. It plans to expand production, build a new facility and create new jobs. The Board decided to grant AE Partner Liepāja SEZ company status and conclude an investment agreement for the period from 1 April 2024 to 31 December 2025. AE Partner owner Klaus Ravn said: “I am very grateful that this support will allow us to continue growing and creating good jobs in Liepāja.” Implementation of investment projects The Board considered and supported two additional investment projects by Liepāja SEZ companies, totalling EUR 440,241.55: PUMAC LIEPAJA, a Liepāja SEZ company, plans the project “Landscaping and Creation of Car Parking Spaces for a Tenant” from 1 April to 31 December 2024, with a total value of EUR 156,166.00. Vecās Ostmalas Biznesa Parks, a Liepāja SEZ company, plans the project “Combining Production Premises and Adapting Them for the Tenant’s Business Activities” from 25 March to 31 December 2024, for EUR 251,093.78. In 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded 15 investment agreements with SEZ companies, with planned investments totalling EUR 5,481,903.28. In 2024, the Board supported and concluded three investment projects worth a total of EUR 4,129,605.00. Maintenance of depths in port waters. To ensure safe navigation in the Port of Liepāja, the Board reviewed and approved plans for maintaining shipping channels in 2024 and decided to conclude a contract with UAB Green Line Shipping for maintaining channel and harbour-basin depths. The company was selected through procurement after submitting the most economically advantageous tender at the lowest price. Amendments to a cooperation agreement. As part of the first stage of the Liepāja Industrial Park development project and in accordance with the agreement concluded with the Central Finance and Contracting Agency, the Board decided to amend its cooperation agreement of 27 April 2023 with Liepājas ūdens. The amendments clarify work on three street sections, including street infrastructure and lighting, external water-supply networks, domestic sewerage, heating networks, external electrical networks and customer electricity connections. Planned activities. The Board decided not to approve the part of DG Termināls’ proposed new waste recovery activity involving construction and installation of a rubber and plastic waste pyrolysis plant. After evaluating the environmental impact assessment (EIA), its findings and conditions, the interests of local residents and existing and planned polluting activities under the permit, the proposed activity was found unacceptable from environmental and public-interest perspectives. The Board stressed that the assessment must address not only environmental impacts but also human health, safety and cumulative risks to surrounding infrastructure. The EIA did not sufficiently detail measures in the event of accidents or adequately assess impacts on the environment, health and life in such events. Rights of first refusal: the Board also decided not to exercise its rights of first refusal over the property at 117 Brīvības Street and a one-fifth undivided share of properties at 117A and 121B Brīvības Street, Liepāja. The Board also decided not to exercise its right of first refusal over the property at 35A Jaunā ostmala, Liepāja. Membership of WindEurope. Since 2022, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has worked actively to establish an important renewable-energy industry centre in the Port of Liepāja. The Liepāja SEZ Development Plan and the city’s spatial plan envisage development of the Outer Harbour area for port terminals. WindEurope is one of the industry’s leading organisations, bringing together major companies and supporting information exchange and joint policy development. The Board decided to join WindEurope to strengthen the Port of Liepāja’s competitiveness and international visibility and create conditions for a new industry to develop in Liepāja and the region. WindEurope promotes the production and use of wind energy in Europe. It has more than 500 members in over 50 countries, including major wind-energy manufacturers, component suppliers, research institutes, national wind and renewable-energy associations, developers, contractors, electricity suppliers, financial firms, insurers and consultants. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 October
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 24. oktobris, 2024 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 18 October At its regular meeting on 18 October 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Board granted Liepāja SEZ company status to BALTU Terminals, supported five investment projects by SEZ companies totalling just under EUR 1 million and amended port charges and building-rights agreements. Port charges. In accordance with Cabinet Regulation No. 256 of 23 May 2023, the Authority annually reviews whether port fees and service tariff limits require adjustment. Analysis of European Central Bank consumer price index data for January–August 2024 showed an average index of 2.30% for Latvia’s transport sector, indicating rising costs. As these affect all areas of port operations, a corresponding increase in charges was proposed. To maintain competitive conditions relative to other Latvian ports, the Authority submitted a proposal to increase the channel fee by two euro cents. The Board reviewed and approved this amendment. The Board also approved a two-euro-cent increase in the charge for using common port infrastructure and related facilities per tonne of cargo loaded or unloaded. The proposed changes were discussed and agreed with companies operating in the Port of Liepāja and took effect on 1 January 2025. Liepāja SEZ company status. The Authority received an application from BALTU Terminals requesting SEZ company status and an agreement to conduct business in the zone. After reviewing the documents, the Board decided to grant the status. Implementation of investment projects. The Board supported five investment projects by SEZ companies worth EUR 925,110 in total. Jensen Metal plans to acquire modern technical equipment for its new production building at 11 Virssardzes Street, Liepāja, between 22 October 2024 and 31 December 2025, investing EUR 410,000.00. Jensen Metal also plans another project with the same title and implementation period worth EUR 52,000.00. AE Partner plans to purchase measuring instruments between 23 October 2024 and 1 February 2025 for EUR 8,500.00. Northside Business Park plans to purchase two overhead cranes for Production Building No. 19 between 1 November and 31 December 2024 for EUR 36,300.00. BALTU Terminals plans to purchase machinery and equipment for stevedoring services from 1 November 2024 to 31 March 2025, for EUR 418,310.00. In 2023, the Authority concluded 15 investment agreements with Liepāja SEZ companies, with planned investments totalling EUR 5,481,903.28. By 1 October 2024, the Authority had concluded 14 agreements for investment in modern technology and construction, with planned investments totalling EUR 16,864,976. Amendments to building-rights agreements. The Board decided to amend the agreement with MOLS L to add the construction projects “New Bulk Cargo Warehouse” and “Construction of Railway Scales”, setting 31 December 2026 as the completion deadline. The Board also decided to amend the building-rights agreement of 1 March 2019 with Karosta LP, setting 31 December 2027 as the deadline for completion of all construction projects included in it. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 22 April
text: 29. aprīlis, 2026 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 22 April At its regular meeting on 22 April this year, the Liepāja SEZ Board adopted 11 decisions concerning EUR 1.25 million in business investments, commercial activity in the SEZ and amendments and clarifications to agreements. Ship agency services in the Port of Liepāja. The Board decided to conclude an agreement with Sparrow Line Logistics for the provision of ship agency services in the Port of Liepāja. Implementation of investment projects The Board reviewed and supported four investment projects by Liepāja SEZ companies totalling EUR 1.25 million. RT metāls will implement the project “Purchase of an Automatic Surface Grinding Machine” by 31 October 2026 for EUR 35,000.00. AE Partner will implement the project “Installation of Mezzanine Warehouse Platforms and a Lift System” by 31 December 2026 for EUR 207,500.00. Caljan will implement the project “Purchase of Welding Equipment for Production” by 30 June 2026 for EUR 44,000.00. Ekers Stividors LP will implement the project “Purchase of an Electric Multifunctional Crane” by 31 December 2026 for EUR 960,000.00. In total, the Authority concluded 21 investment agreements in 2025 worth EUR 3.71 million and two agreements in 2026 worth EUR 2.1 million. Commercial activities in the Liepāja SEZ The Board decided to conclude an agreement with BaltEx Bulk to conduct commercial activities in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone until 2028. On 23 February 2026, a change in ownership of BaltEx Bulk was registered: the new 100% shareholder is SVEASKOG BALTFOR, a limited liability company from Sweden. Changes to a lease agreement The Board approved the request by TRANSIT TERMINĀLS to increase its leased area at Berth 69 and 43 Atslēdznieku Street, Liepāja, to provide more space for liquid-cargo handling, since the existing area limits full use of vessel mooring facilities. Reservation of property lease and building rights The Board decided to extend until 30 April 2027 the reservation agreement for lease/building rights with NORSAF to prepare a minimum-composition construction design for the “NORSAF Production Facility and CO₂ Terminal”. Development of the design was affected by a decision during the research stage to change the planned technology. Real estate auction The Board approved the Procurement Commission’s decision to declare the auction for the property at 1 Naglu Street, Liepāja, unsuccessful. The Board decided to conclude a 30-year lease agreement with Sadales tīkls for property at 6/8 Ostas Street, Liepāja, to manage and maintain the existing 10 kV distribution point. title: Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 25 September
text: Contact person Inese Matisone Head of the Manager’s Office Tālr: E-pasts: inese.matisone@lsez.lv 28. septembris, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 25 September At its regular meeting on 25 September this year, the Liepāja SEZ Board adopted decisions on an investment agreement, waiving rights of first refusal, an auction and amendments to earlier decisions. It also approved the updated Liepāja Special Economic Zone Development Plan for 2018–2035 and the Port of Liepāja Development Programme for 2023–2027. Updating the Liepāja SEZ Development Plan The Board approved updated versions of the Liepāja SEZ Development Plan for 2018–2035 and the Port of Liepāja Development Programme for 2023–2027, adapting them to market changes, the geopolitical situation and new development directions. The revision combines the two planning documents into one, assesses previous development results, updates the statistical database and regulatory framework, and adds new priorities including renewable and alternative-energy projects. The plan aims to strengthen Liepāja as an industrial, logistics and energy centre by developing the Outer Harbour, offshore wind projects, NATO naval infrastructure and the Liepāja Industrial Park. Green-economy projects, including sustainable aviation fuel, hydrogen and CO₂ infrastructure, are also priorities. The Authority emphasises that the updated development plan is essential for sustainable development of the port, industry and business, attracting investment and creating jobs in the region. Liepāja SEZ companies invest in development The Board plans an investment agreement with Liepāja SEZ company Brimer for EUR 3.36 million to construct a new production and administrative building at 37 Atslēdznieku Street, Liepāja. The project is planned for 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2028. The company qualifies as a medium-sized enterprise, with a maximum permissible aid intensity of 50%. Brimer Liepaja is part of Norway’s Brimer Group and specialises in the design and manufacture of large fibreglass-composite products, offering services from engineering and design through manufacture, transportation and installation. The Board also decided to conclude an investment agreement with Jensen Metal for the project “Purchase of New Production Equipment”. The company plans to invest EUR 133,000 between 30 September 2026 and 31 May 2027. The maximum permissible aid intensity for eligible costs is 40%. Paid services at the Port of Liepāja The Board approved a price list for paid services, expanding the range available to port companies and other customers. The decision reflects demand from port operators and other market participants and aims to make more efficient use of the Authority’s infrastructure and technical resources. The Authority will offer certain paid services outside the port’s core functions, without financing them from port charges. Customers will be able to use hydrographic surveying, hydrographic data post-processing, specialised boat services, oil-contaminated water treatment and equipment rental. Prices were set using detailed cost calculations and market analysis to cover costs fully and remain competitive. The new price list will enter into force after publication on the Authority’s website. Electricity supply agreement The Board supported concluding an electricity supply agreement with Enefit for the period from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027. Two tenders were received, and Enefit’s offer of EUR 155.73/MWh was judged the most economically advantageous. The agreement will provide electricity for the Authority’s needs and for business operations of tenants in the Port of Liepāja and the Liepāja Industrial Park. Reliable electricity supply is essential for continuous port and industrial park operations and further development. Repeat auction for property at 6 Dūmu Street The Board approved the rules for a repeat electronic auction of the property at 6 Dūmu Street after the previous auction failed for lack of bidders. The property is in the Liepāja Industrial Park and consists of a 46,766 m² land plot and a scrap-processing building with a total area of 25,181.7 m². The starting price remains EUR 480,000, based on a valuation by LATIO. Disposal of the property is part of the Industrial Park development strategy to attract investment and develop the site. Auction proceeds are intended for further industrial park development and obligations associated with disposal. Rights of first refusal The Board decided not to exercise its rights of first refusal over a 1.5-hectare land plot at 31A Cukura Street in the SEZ or over properties at 6/9 Vecā ostmala, 1 Fēniksa Street and 23 Jaunā Street, Liepāja. After assessing the need for the plots, the Authority concluded that they were not required for its functions. After the transaction, the new owners plan to use the land for their company’s development project. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. maijs, 2024 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 27 May On 27 May 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Board held its regular meeting, considering 11 agenda items and adopting four decisions. It also heard information reports on SEZ operations and planned development projects. Investment agreement. The Board reviewed and approved the AE Partner Liepāja SEZ company’s investment project “Purchase of Packaging Equipment”. The project is planned for 1 June to 31 July 2024, with a total investment of EUR 9,765.00. Novation of a lease agreement. On 17 June 2006, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded a lease with Amserv Krasta for the property at 146B Brīvības Street, Liepāja, to build a car dealership and conduct other commercial activities. The lease runs until 16 July 2031. Following an application from Liepaja Property, the Authority decided to novate the lease by updating the lessee’s name to Liepaja Property, aligning the lease with the Land Register. Amendment of a building-rights agreement. On 14 May 2018, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded an agreement granting BaltEx Bulk building rights at 11 Pulvera Street, within the Port of Liepāja, for the project “Warehouse 1”. The agreement runs until 1 June 2038. After reviewing the application, the Board supported enlarging the cargo-storage area by relocating the fence and agreed to amend the building-rights agreement. Tugboat services. After reviewing the submitted documents, the Board decided to conclude an agreement with UAB Mabrocona for tugboat services in the Port of Liepāja. Was this information useful? title: Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 4 March
text: 10. marts, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 4 March On 4 March this year, the Liepāja SEZ Board held its regular meeting and considered matters relating to tugboat services at the Port of Liepāja, an agreement granting building rights in the Liepāja Industrial Park, two real estate reservation agreements and the disposal of real estate. Tugboat services at the Port of Liepāja Tugboat services at the Port of Liepāja will continue to be provided by Towmar Liepājā Ltd. The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed the documents submitted and decided to conclude an agreement with Towmar Liepājā Ltd for the provision of tugboat services at the port. The decision to conclude a tugboat services agreement with Towmar Liepājā Ltd aims to promote competition in the market for such services at the Port of Liepāja by entrusting them to private-sector companies. This directly implements the purpose of Section 18 of the Law on Ports: commercial activities in a port may be carried out under an agreement, subject to the prescribed minimum requirements. In this legal relationship, the Liepāja SEZ Authority acts solely as a public-law supervisory body overseeing compliance with safety and technical requirements and does not itself engage in commercial activity in this market. Agreement granting building rights On 10 November 2025, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and ZET Ltd signed an agreement reserving building rights for a property at 111A Brīvības Street in the Liepāja Industrial Park. Having fulfilled the reservation agreement conditions, the company confirmed its readiness to sign an agreement granting building rights to construct and commission a 5 MW battery energy storage system (BESS) by 29 March 2027. Having evaluated the documents, the Liepāja SEZ Board decided to conclude an agreement with ZET Ltd granting building rights for the property at 111A Brīvības Street in the Liepāja Industrial Park until 1 March 2056. Consent to the disposal of property The Liepāja SEZ Board considered the disposal by auction of the property at 13 Sarkanā Street in Liepāja, organised by its owner, the Liepāja City Municipality. Since the property is not required for the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s core functions, the Board agreed to its disposal. Reservation of building rights for land plots The Liepāja SEZ Board considered and decided to conclude two agreements reserving building rights for land plots: With VIA-S Properties Ltd, for two years, to begin implementing a modular housing production facility project on approximately 3.3 hectares at the junction of Inženieru and Eksporta Streets in the Liepāja Industrial Park; With CIS Liepaja Ltd, for two years, covering two land plots in the Liepāja SEZ which, after being combined, will form a property of approximately 31.7 hectares. The company plans to develop a green hydrogen production plant using PEM electrolysis technology. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 7 December
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 08. decembris, 2023 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 7 December The Liepāja SEZ Authority’s 2024 budget The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed and approved the Authority’s budget for 2024: operating revenue of EUR 15,766,038, operating expenditure of EUR 12,460,072 and investment cash flow of EUR 2,777,339. The Board also approved the Authority’s budget forecast for the following five years. The operating revenue forecast takes account of expected cargo throughput by stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja, the approved port charges for 2024 and expected income from property leases. In 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Authority will continue work on three major development projects: reconstruction of the ferry berth (Berth 46), transformation of the former Liepājas metalurgs plant into the modern Liepāja Industrial Park, and development projects in the Port of Liepāja’s outer harbour. Implementation of investment projects The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed and supported an investment project by Roechling Industrial Liepaja LSEZ Ltd totalling EUR 200,000. The company plans to purchase universal robotic arms and related equipment between 27 December 2023 and 31 December 2024. According to its declaration of enterprise size, Roechling Industrial Liepaja LSEZ Ltd is a medium-sized enterprise and the maximum permitted aid intensity for these investments is 50%. In 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded 15 investment agreements with SEZ companies, with a total planned investment of EUR 5,481,903.28. Disposal of real estate The Liepāja SEZ Board considered and agreed to the disposal of the land plot at 1 Laboratorijas Street in Liepāja because the property is not needed for the Authority’s functions. Real estate lease and building rights agreements On 31 January 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and BaltEx Bulk Ltd signed an agreement granting building rights for the land plot at 5 Pulvera Street in Liepāja, within the SEZ, to prepare a preliminary construction design for a cargo storage area. The Board examined documents submitted by BaltEx Bulk Ltd and noted that changes in market and geopolitical circumstances have affected cargo types, requiring amendments and additions to the cargo categories and corresponding changes to the preliminary construction design. The Liepāja SEZ Board decided to conclude an agreement with BaltEx Bulk Ltd extending the reservation agreement until 31 July 2024. The Board also decided to amend the lease agreement concluded on 5 March 1998 between the Liepāja SEZ Authority and NORPLAST PIEMARE LSEZ JSC for properties at 7 Kaiju Street and 37 Atslēdznieku Street in the Port of Liepāja. The Board approved NORPLAST PIEMARE LSEZ JSC’s request to separate the part of the property at 37 Atslēdznieku Street from the original lease and conclude a separate lease agreement for it. On 3 April 2019, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and EB Liepājā Ltd concluded an agreement granting building rights for the property at 11 Zemgales Street in Liepāja to implement the construction project for a new production building and reconstruction of two buildings at that address. The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed and approved the leasing of the newly built production facility and office building to Golden Fields Factory LV Ltd. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 19 August
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 20. augusts, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Board Decisions of 19 August At its regular meeting on 19 August, the Liepāja SEZ Board adopted seven decisions concerning an investment agreement, rights of first refusal, auction results and a contract to implement the reconstruction of Berth 46. It also supported participation in the project “Science-based Solutions to Promote Climate-resilient Adaptation of the Baltic Sea Coast” and amended previous decisions on security services and the digitalisation of data processing and analysis. Investments by Liepāja SEZ companies The Board considered Caljan’s investment project “Expansion of the Assembly Department — Development of Infrastructure for Assembly and Testing of Telescopic Conveyors”, planned from 24 August to 31 December 2026 at a total cost of EUR 121,500.00. It decided to conclude an investment agreement. Caljan is one of Liepāja’s leading metalworking, engineering and automation companies. It designs and manufactures logistics automation equipment, including telescopic conveyors for loading and unloading freight, parcels and shipments. Its products are exported worldwide to e-commerce, postal and logistics customers, including Amazon. Having operated in Liepāja for twenty years, the company continues to create jobs and increase its turnover and exports. Rights of first refusal The Board decided not to exercise its right of first refusal over the property at 15 Lazaretes Street, Liepāja, as it is not required for the Authority’s core functions. The property comprises nine buildings, the largest a former boiler house. Owner LM Sēta has signed a purchase agreement with Situācijas plāns. The buyer plans to convert the buildings into a factory making compact wooden “Tiny House” homes, expanding its operations in response to growing demand. Auction results The Board reviewed and approved the results of the electronic auction for the property at 1 Naglu Street, in the future Liepāja Industrial Park. The highest bidder was FLESS, a Liepāja SEZ company providing IT-sector logistics services, including storing, assembling and preparing networking equipment for distribution. Reconstruction of Port of Liepāja Berth 46 The Liepāja SEZ Authority received an opinion from the Central Finance and Contracting Agency (CFLA) confirming that the “Reconstruction of Port of Liepāja Berth No. 46” project meets the conditions for European Union Cohesion Fund support under Priority 3.3, “Strengthening Military Mobility — Railways and Ports”, of the 2021–2027 Cohesion Policy Programme. The Board decided to sign an agreement with CFLA to implement the project and receive the funding. The works include reconstructing the sheet-pile wall, constructing the berth superstructure and mooring platforms, installing fenders, building cargo ramps, deepening the seabed to minus 12 metres, and developing the necessary transport and engineering infrastructure. Berth 46 was built between 1972 and 1975 to service Soviet naval vessels and submarines. It is the only berth in Liepāja suitable for RO-RO/RO-PAX ferries and is important for military transport and cargo movements. The powerful engines used during regular ferry berthing and departure place much greater strain on the structure than vessels did in the 1970s and 1980s. Despite repairs, structural defects and ongoing deterioration continue to worsen the berth’s overall technical condition. In 2025, Berth 46 handled 112,041 vehicles carrying a total of 1.646 million tonnes of cargo and 6,863 maritime container units carrying 0.074 million tonnes. Participation in a LIFE project The Board supported the Authority’s participation as a partner in “Science-based Solutions to Promote Climate-resilient Adaptation of the Baltic Sea Coast”, led by the Latvian Environment, Geology and Meteorology Centre (LEGMC). An application is planned under the LIFE 2026 “Adaptation to Climate Change” subprogramme. Drawing on climate projections and coastal geological conditions, the project aims to assess shoreline changes, identify coastal risks and develop scientifically grounded approaches to adapting the Baltic Sea coast to climate change. title: Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 8 October
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 10. oktobris, 2025 Decisions Adopted by the Liepāja SEZ Board on 8 October On 8 October 2025, the Liepāja SEZ Board held its regular meeting, granting SEZ company status to AI industri bygg and approving three investment projects totalling approximately EUR 1 million. It also decided to conclude nine agreements for mooring services in the Port of Liepāja, approved auction results and addressed property, lease and reservation rights. Liepāja SEZ company status The Board reviewed and approved the application and documents submitted by AI industri bygg for Liepāja SEZ company status. AI industri bygg is a Latvian-owned company which purchased a property at 3 Grīzupes Street, Liepāja, in 2024 to regenerate a degraded site and develop a business and manufacturing centre. The site formerly housed a gas filling station operated by Latvijas Propāna Gāze. Implementation of investment projects The Board supported three investment projects by SEZ companies worth EUR 988,237.04 in total: AI industri bygg plans to renovate the façade of the building at 3 Grīzupes Street, Liepāja, by 31 December 2026, investing EUR 473,237.04. RT metāls plans to purchase a hydraulic bending press by 31 March 2026 for EUR 315,000.00. Caljan plans to integrate robotic welding technology into its manufacturing operations by 31 January 2026, investing EUR 200,000.00. Auction results As part of the Liepāja Industrial Park’s development, the Authority offered several properties at auction to stimulate business activity. The Board approved the results for the property at 94 Brīvības Street, Liepāja, where Nordic Steel Latvia submitted the highest bid. The auction of the property at 98 Brīvības Street ended without a sale, and the Board decided to organise a new auction. Mooring services in the Port of Liepāja Five years ago, the Liepāja SEZ Authority outsourced vessel mooring services to improve operational efficiency. The decision has proved successful. With the existing contracts approaching expiry, the Board reviewed and approved new agreements with nine operators to provide mooring services in the Port of Liepāja. Was this information useful? text: 19. februāris, 2024 Secretary General of the Baltic Ports Organization Bogdan Ołdakowski Visits Liepāja The Baltic Ports Organization brings together ports from eight countries, including Liepāja. It aims to ensure economically, socially and environmentally sustainable development of maritime transport and the port industry in the Baltic Sea region and to promote cooperation between ports. Founded in Copenhagen in 1991, the Baltic Ports Organization is a regional association that supports its members by cooperating with partners across the Baltic Sea region.
