title: Liepāja SEZ Company NorSAF and US-based KBR Sign Licensing Agreement for SAF and eSAF Production in Latvia for the European Market
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. maijs, 2026 Liepāja SEZ Company NorSAF and US-based KBR Sign Licensing Agreement for SAF and eSAF Production in Latvia for the European Market NorSAF, an oil and chemical product storage and transshipment terminal planning to build Northern Europe’s largest sustainable aviation fuel (SAF and eSAF) plant in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone, has signed a perpetual licence agreement with US engineering company KBR for the PureSAF® technology. Developed by Swedish Biofuels AB, with KBR as its exclusive global marketing partner, the technology gives NorSAF exclusive rights to use it and lays the groundwork for Europe’s first commercial-scale plant capable of producing 100% drop-in sustainable aviation fuel without blending it with fossil fuel. Unlike conventional sustainable aviation fuels that must be blended with fossil fuel, PureSAF contains aromatic components that make it compatible with modern aircraft engines. This allows the fuel to be used in existing aviation infrastructure without major technical changes. The plant is expected to begin operating in 2031 and produce 100,000 tonnes of SAF/eSAF annually. It plans to produce SAF from CO₂ and second-generation bioethanol, and synthetic aviation fuel (eSAF) from green hydrogen and biogenic CO₂. Renewable electricity will power hydrogen production through electrolysis; combining this hydrogen with captured carbon will create a complete green-energy cycle. The process is estimated to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 83% compared with conventional aviation-fuel production. All feedstocks are planned to be sourced in Europe, strengthening energy independence and industrial resilience. The project follows the EU ReFuelEU Aviation framework, which requires a gradual increase in SAF use in aviation: 6% by 2030, including at least 0.7% eSAF, rising to 70% by 2050, including at least 35% eSAF. The fuel produced in Liepāja will supply European airlines, helping reduce their carbon emissions. By developing Liepāja into a sustainable-fuel hub, NorSAF and KBR aim to strengthen Latvia’s role in international aviation. “We are pleased to cooperate with KBR to introduce PureSAF technology in Europe. Recent global events have made it clear that energy independence is no longer only an economic issue; it is also a national and regional security priority. By producing sustainable 100% drop-in fuel from European feedstocks, we are creating a resilient and self-sufficient energy ecosystem that reduces dependence on external fossil-fuel markets and strengthens European industry,” says Jānis Kisiels, a member of the NorSAF board. “We are proud to be part of this significant project, which will support Latvia’s transition to cleaner aviation and reinforce Europe’s leadership in sustainable-fuel innovation. PureSAF technology makes it possible not only to significantly increase SAF production, but also to use CO₂ and synthesis gas in a single plant to create fully functional aviation fuel without blending it with conventional fuel,” says Jay Ibrahim, President of KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions. Further development of the project, including the start of construction in the Port of Liepāja, will depend on securing the necessary support and strategic partners. PureSAF was developed by Swedish Biofuels AB, and KBR is the exclusive licensing and commercialisation partner. The technology is currently certified for a 50/50 blend with fossil fuel, while certification for 100% drop-in use is ongoing in Europe. Industry participants expect the necessary approvals from international standards organisation ASTM, which develops technical standards for aviation-fuel producers, could be obtained this year. Test flights by the Swedish military and US Air Force have demonstrated that PureSAF can fully replace conventional jet fuel, behaving like Jet A-1 even without blending. Other SAF technologies generally require mixing with fossil fuel at approximately 10–50%, while PureSAF can be used undiluted, potentially reducing petroleum dependence and helping decarbonise aviation. About NorSAF NorSAF is a Latvia-based liquid petroleum and chemical storage and transshipment terminal and sustainable aviation fuel developer. Together with Avia Solutions Group, one of the world’s largest full-service aircraft leasing providers, it is developing the first world-class SAF and synthetic SAF (eSAF) production facility in the Baltics, within the Liepāja SEZ. The project is valued at more than EUR 1 billion. NorSAF will use Avia Solutions Group’s aviation infrastructure, including Baltic Ground Services’ expertise in SAF supply and distribution. About KBR KBR supplies science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and businesses worldwide, including NASA and the US armed forces. Approximately 36,000 employees serve customers in more than 80 countries, with operations in 28 countries. KBR specialises in technology, high-value services and long-term operations and maintenance solutions. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Developers Sought for Two Historically Significant Properties in Karosta Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 02. februāris, 2024 Developers Sought for Two Historically Significant Properties in Karosta Industrial Park The historic buildings on Zemgales Street have been designated as architecturally and culturally significant urban heritage. Reconstruction must preserve structural and finishing solutions, existing building volumes, original window divisions and smooth sheet-metal roofing. The maximum building height is three storeys. At the same time, the properties lie within Karosta Industrial Park and are zoned for mixed development with an industrial function. “This is a logical step in continuing the development of Karosta Industrial Park. Having seen and assessed the office and production building of EB Liepāja, commissioned at the end of 2022, where Karosta’s historic architecture was successfully restored and integrated, other businesses have also shown interest,” says Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. He stresses that development is easier when there are tangible examples to see. “I am very pleased that several other companies are interested in incorporating Karosta’s historic buildings into their development projects, including production facilities and logistics centres. An auction is a good way to identify an investor so that two more historic buildings on Zemgales Street can be restored in the coming years.” The principal permitted use of the land and buildings is multifunctional: low-impact manufacturing, commercial premises, retail outlets and service facilities. Public buildings are also permitted, but residential development is not allowed. To encourage the restoration of historic buildings or their integration into new developments, the auction rules require the successful bidder to obtain confirmation that design conditions have been met within 24 months of the purchase agreement taking effect. Construction specified in the auction rules and agreement must begin within 25 months and be completed within 48 months of that date. EB Liepāja recognised Liepāja as an industrial city that has always respected cultural and historical heritage, integrating this heritage into its production building by combining Karosta’s historic architecture with modern industry and creating higher-value manufacturing space. EB Liepāja board member Māris Pētersons previously stated that the modern factory would not have been built without the supportive attitude and involvement of the municipality and the Liepāja SEZ Authority. Construction was carried out by UPTK. Background: The idea for Karosta Industrial Park emerged in 1999, aiming to give a former military base a new purpose, integrate it into the city, create jobs, increase tax revenue for city and state budgets, and make more funding available for education, culture, sport and other projects. Building new factories in Karosta remained impractical or unattractive to investors until 2015, when the municipality and the Liepāja SEZ Authority developed almost 20 hectares of the area for business use. title: Prime Minister: Liepāja Is on a Path of Development
text: 05. aprīlis, 2024 Prime Minister: Liepāja Is on a Path of Development Liepāja is on a stable development path that must be maintained by supporting investors’ projects, reducing bureaucratic requirements, strengthening competitive education and supporting the National Armed Forces’ plans to develop a military port in Karosta. This was emphasised by Prime Minister Evika Siliņa during her regional visit to Liepāja on Friday, 5 April. “Liepāja is a centre of culture and tourism as well as manufacturing. The city is preparing to become European Capital of Culture in 2027, and many new manufacturing companies have emerged rapidly in recent years. Continued infrastructure development is important, with appropriately targeted European Union funds and other financing sources, as well as reduced red tape, playing a major role. Equally important are the skills and knowledge needed by the city’s companies. It is therefore welcome that Liepāja University has just joined Riga Technical University to strengthen its specialisation in engineering and technology for industrial development in the city and region,” Siliņa says. The Prime Minister visited AE Partner, which specialises in high-quality automation systems and electrical control panels; the newly built drinking-water export terminal of Eipu; and Global Wolf Motors, which makes Mosphera military scooters. A discussion was also held about the key challenges and development plans of Liepāja businesses. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: No Ammonia Plant Planned; Hydrogen Production to Move Further Offshore
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 30. aprīlis, 2025 No Ammonia Plant Planned; Hydrogen Production to Move Further Offshore At a working meeting, CIS Liepāja CEO Tor Arne Pedersen announced that, following agreement with the Liepāja SEZ management, the proposed hydrogen production plant would be moved further north into the port waters. In response to changing markets and demand, CIS Liepāja has also abandoned the development of a green ammonia production project. Tor Arne Pedersen stressed that safety comes first. “From the very beginning of the project, we have sought the best locations and technological solutions for the green hydrogen plant and terminal. We take safety very seriously and fully understand that it is critically important to the project. That is why we have examined different ways of addressing safety as effectively as possible. This matters to us as developers, to the municipality and to the Liepāja SEZ Authority.” During the meeting, Pedersen again presented the project concept and progress, the company’s shareholders and its experience in developing and advancing projects. Asked why Liepāja had been chosen, he explained that the company had initially considered Norway, Sweden and Finland, where a shortage of high-voltage grid capacity was the main obstacle, before looking at the Baltic countries. Recommendations from the Norwegian Embassy in Latvia and Liepāja’s high-quality business environment, together with the benefits of its special economic zone, played an important role. Preliminary studies, risk assessments and environmental impact assessments are now under way. A joint working meeting brought together the leadership of the Liepāja SEZ and City Council, municipal councillors, investment-project developers, the State Environmental Service and environmental organisations to review progress on sustainable-industry projects in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. title: Stable Operations at the Port of Liepāja in 2025
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 24. janvāris, 2026 Stable Operations at the Port of Liepāja in 2025 As a multifunctional port, Liepāja has maintained stable cargo throughput averaging 7 million tonnes a year over the past decade. The pattern continued in 2025, when 6.9 million tonnes were handled, 0.19 million tonnes or 2.53% less than the previous year. Local cargo continued to account for more than 52%. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis notes that ports are still transforming, with logistics routes and cargo types changing. “Working closely with port businesses, the municipality and the government, we have adapted flexibly and effectively to market conditions, replacing some cargo types with others and developing new investment projects.” Dry bulk remained the Port of Liepāja’s largest cargo group in 2025 at 4.55 million tonnes. Agricultural cargo continued to dominate, including grain grown by local farmers and grain from Central Asian countries. Imports of Argentinian soy and Brazilian sugar via Liepāja to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan also continued. Agricultural and energy cargo (woodchips and pellets) declined slightly owing to warm winters and cool, rainy summers, while building materials increased, particularly cement produced in Brocēni. Ro-ro freight transported by Stena Line’s regular Liepāja–Travemünde (Germany) ferry service accounted for the largest share of general cargo. The number of units carried increased by 4% in 2025. A project to reconstruct the ferry berth has begun, and the tender submission stage has concluded. Construction is planned to start this year and be completed by the end of 2027, improving military mobility and enabling dual use of the berth. The annual value of goods carried on the ferry is approximately EUR 4 billion. In 2025, the port stabilised the liquid bulk segment, attracted new food-grade liquid cargo from Central Asia and increased liquid cargo throughput to 0.3 million tonnes. Food-grade liquids, including rapeseed oil and molasses, accounted for 63% of all liquid cargo. Overall, liquid cargo remains a relatively small part of the port’s business. During 2025, the Liepāja SEZ Authority, businesses and investors continued work on sustainable-industry projects involving renewable-energy production and supply. Work also continued on a NATO support base at the port, reconstruction of Berth 46 and modernisation of port operations as part of military-mobility and dual-use initiatives. In 2025, the Port of Liepāja handled 1,154 vessels and 99,942 passengers. The year’s most unusual cargo consisted of two ship-unloading machines, each weighing approximately 350 tonnes, which were fully assembled at the port over six months before being shipped to Canada. Liepāja remains a popular stop for sailors and an emerging cruise destination. The marina welcomed 193 yachts in 2025. Three cruise ships called at the port during the year, and eight are planned for 2026. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Water Terminal in the Liepāja SEZ Commissioned
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. oktobris, 2024 Water Terminal in the Liepāja SEZ Commissioned On 7 October, the Liepāja Building Authority approved the commissioning of the “Water Filling Terminal at 117 Oskara Kalpaka Street”. The project developer is EIPU and the construction contractor is UPTK. The terminal has a total developed area of 18,000 m². Commissioning marks the end of construction and the start of the drinking-water terminal’s certification process. The newly constructed terminal has been designed to be environmentally and people friendly. Once all necessary permits and certificates have been obtained, it plans to export drinking water to countries experiencing shortages. Planned throughput is up to 3 million tonnes per year. In 2020, EIPU signed a land-lease reservation agreement with the Liepāja SEZ Authority for the property at 117 Oskara Kalpaka Street to implement the “Water Filling Terminal” project. Following extensive research and preparation of the construction design, work on the terminal began in 2022. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Norwegian Experience in Sustainable Restoration of Contaminated Waterbeds Following Remediation
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. jūnijs, 2022 Norwegian Experience in Sustainable Restoration of Contaminated Waterbeds Following Remediation At a knowledge-sharing seminar on 3 June entitled “Reducing and Preventing Pollution: Effective Environmental Management Systems in Industrial Waterways”, representatives of the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) shared both successful and less successful experiences of natural recovery in contaminated waterbodies following the partial removal of polluted sediments. Experts from Latvia’s State Environmental Service, Liepāja City Council and the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority also discussed pollution reduction. The event was organised under the “Remediation of the Historically Contaminated Site in the Karosta Canal of the Port of Liepāja” project, implemented by the Liepāja SEZ Authority in cooperation with NIVA and the Baltic Coasts association. NIVA research director Marianne Olsen presented “Contaminated Sediments in Norway”, describing the country’s approach to contaminated sediment management. Norway has mapped polluted sites since 1998, while its 2007 National Action Plan identified 17 priority remediation sites in fjords and ports. Priorities were based on environmental and human-health risks. Common remediation methods include dredging contaminated sediments where required to maintain navigation depth, depositing sediments on land or at designated marine sites with containment, and covering cleaned seabeds with thin layers of active or inert materials to support sustainable recovery. NIVA researcher Sigurd Øxnevad presented “Environmental Monitoring of a Small Fjord (Vikkilen) in Southern Norway in 2021 — Five Years After Remediation Actions”, outlining a successful case of sustainable environmental recovery. He described Vikkilen fjord, home to a shipyard since 1946. Shipyard operations released tributyltin (TBT), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and heavy metals into the fjord. Much of the pollution came from antifouling ship paints and sandblasting, with sediment TBT concentrations reaching 93 mg/kg. The relevant chemicals were banned worldwide in 2008. Remediation took place in 2014–2016, removing most of the contamination from the seabed and covering it with geotextile, sand and gravel. Regular monitoring subsequently assessed benthic fauna and chemical concentrations in sediment, blue mussels and snails. Pollution had particularly harmed snails, affecting their reproduction and population recovery. Their condition improved by 2016, and since then no snails showing pollution-related harm have been found. NIVA senior researcher Hilde Cecilie Trannum presented “Long-term Biological Effects of Capping with Thin Layers of Activated Carbon in the Grenland Fjords, Norway”, discussing a less successful example that provides important insight into natural processes and human impacts. The researcher explained that benthic habitats contain polychaete worms, molluscs, echinoderms, crustaceans and many other organisms. The Grenland fjords have a long history of dioxin and mercury pollution from magnesium factories that operated for fifty years until 2002. In two test areas, Ormerfjord at approximately 30 metres depth and Eidangerfjord at approximately 95 metres, a thin layer of powdered activated carbon mixed with clay was applied to the seabed. Chemical and ecological monitoring was conducted one month, one year, four years and nine years after sediment removal and activated-carbon capping. Chemical analyses showed improvements, including reduced dioxin dispersion and accumulation and up to 90% lower dioxin uptake by mussels and polychaetes. Surprisingly, biodiversity suffered, especially among echinoderms, whose benthic populations fell by half. This and other examples demonstrate the importance of carefully choosing a site-specific approach to ecological recovery after contaminated sediments are removed. Liepāja City Council Environment Department head Dace Liepniece presented “Sustainable Environmental Management and Restoration of Degraded Areas: Liepāja City Council’s Experience”. She described the rehabilitation of Zirgu Island, the largest of the 15 islands in Lake Liepāja. Developed in stages for active recreation, the site now provides 17,550 m² of improved public space, including an 824-metre walking trail with viewing platforms, rest areas and outdoor exercise equipment. Dace Liepniece also reported on work addressing a component of the Karosta Canal pollution hotspot listed by the Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission (HELCOM): untreated wastewater entering the Baltic Sea through the canal. Between 2006 and 2009, Cohesion Fund support was used to eliminate untreated wastewater discharges into the canal and sea, collect wastewater from Karosta and divert it to treatment systems, and construct or reconstruct water-supply and sewer pipelines to enable environmentally sound wastewater management. State Environmental Service project implementation group head Madara Zingere presented “Contaminated Site Management Systems: Opportunities to Be Seized”. She described improvements to the register of contaminated and potentially contaminated sites under the project “Digital Transformation of the Contaminated Site Management Model”, also called “PPPV Digitalisation” (No. LV-CLIMATE-0006). The PPPV register currently lists 3,603 contaminated or potentially contaminated sites: 263 contaminated, 2,606 potentially contaminated and 734 non-contaminated sites (surveyed or fully remediated). Information is presented as a list and on a map with municipality, parish and waterbody layers. Established in 2004, the current register has a complex and fragmented management process, partly paper-based information flows and gaps in up-to-date information. A digital contaminated-site management system is planned to support high-quality identification, investigation and remediation of contaminated locations, improving soil, ground, groundwater and surface-water quality, restoring the environment at and around the sites, and preventing risks to public health and nature. The seminar’s final presentation was given by Liepāja SEZ remediation expert Pēteris Blumats. Entitled “Remediation and Environmental Monitoring: Reducing Environmental Impacts”, it outlined the environmental risks and planned activities of the Karosta Canal remediation project. Latvia’s Climate Change Adaptation Plan to 2030 identifies several risks for Liepāja. Rapid changes in sea level can wash accumulated pollutants from the slopes of the Karosta Canal into the water as an oil film, potentially carrying them into the open Baltic Sea. Accordingly, a monitored natural recovery approach is planned for the Karosta Canal until 2035, following remediation works under this project. These works envisage removing 202,247 m³ of sediment that does not meet statutory standards and contains 400 tonnes of contaminants. The aim is to establish the ecological conditions needed for sustainable environmental development. Monitored natural recovery, or self-purification, relies on natural biodegradation processes that reduce the bioavailability or toxicity of pollutants in sediment. Long-term monitoring will continue during and after remediation of the Karosta Canal, covering surface water, sediments (chemical and biological parameters) and groundwater. The project implementation period runs from 1 August 2021 to 31 December 2023. The project budget is EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000.00 in co-financing from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. “Working together for a green Europe” Was this information useful? title: Third Stage of Karosta Canal Environmental Remediation Completed
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. decembris, 2023 Third Stage of Karosta Canal Environmental Remediation Completed The project is funded under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. A total of 145,199 cubic metres of historically contaminated sediment, containing approximately 298 tonnes of hazardous chemicals, was removed during the third stage of the Karosta Canal remediation project. The work in the Karosta Canal was carried out by SIA “Eko osta” under the signed contract and the approved Karosta Canal remediation programme. Remediation started in April 2023 and was completed on 5 December 2023. The total contract value was EUR 3,334,877.50 excluding value-added tax. Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš emphasised the significance of the work, noting that contamination in the Karosta Canal led HELCOM to designate Liepāja a pollution hotspot in 1992. “It was an extremely complex situation: in one small canal there was Soviet military heritage, sunken ships and submarines, and more than 100 different elements of the periodic table. This meant that Latvia, Liepāja and the Baltic Sea region had to gradually clean up the canal, and that is what we have been doing step by step.” Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis noted that the port, including the Karosta Canal, is an integral part of the Liepāja SEZ and must be cared for, including dealing with the legacy of the Soviet era. “To develop shipping and build new terminals in the port, we had to clean the canal, and that has been done. A great deal of work has been accomplished.” With support from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority implemented the third stage of Karosta Canal remediation to make a substantial contribution to mitigating climate-change risks and preventing historical pollution from spreading into the Baltic Sea and surrounding environment. Project manager Ivo Koliņš emphasised that work would continue and that clear short- and long-term actions had been established to minimise historical contamination and its impact on the entire Baltic Sea ecosystem. Karosta is becoming an increasingly important part of Liepāja’s social, economic and everyday life. The canal cleanup carried out through the project will allow residents and visitors to enjoy Karosta in a cleaner, higher-quality environment, helping aquatic ecosystems recover and reducing pollution. title: Access Road to Berth 92 at the Port of Liepāja Nears Completion
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 20. augusts, 2026 Access Road to Berth 92 at the Port of Liepāja Nears Completion The Liepāja SEZ Authority continues improving infrastructure for fishermen by constructing an access road to Berth 92. The project is funded by the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Programme 2021–2027. It includes a 364-metre public access road, smart lighting and a stormwater drainage system. Following procurement, SIA “CTB” is carrying out the work, having submitted the most economically advantageous offer of EUR 303,617.32. Construction is scheduled for completion by the end of August. Until now, access to Berth 92 at the Port of Liepāja has been severely restricted, making it practically unusable for fishermen. To change this, the Liepāja SEZ Authority agreed with fish-processing company Syfud to amend its lease, secured funding from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund and began road construction in the spring of this year. According to Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis, final construction works are under way so this much-needed infrastructure can be commissioned soon. “The new access road will not only improve conditions for the fishing industry but also provide access to other port infrastructure, including the Liepāja Lighthouse.” In parallel, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality are collaborating on a layered multimedia exhibition inside the lighthouse. Across five floors, projections, sound, light and animated historical stories will introduce visitors to the history of the Port of Liepāja, from its beginnings to the present day. SIA “CTB” is building public infrastructure comprising the roadway, stormwater drainage networks and lighting. This will create a modern, safe and efficient transport connection between city infrastructure and the Port of Liepāja, while supporting the fishing industry and export opportunities. The project aims to improve access to berths at the Port of Liepāja, develop a sustainable blue economy and support the growth of fishing and aquaculture communities. The new road will give coastal fishermen access to a fish landing site and improve accessibility to other coastal facilities. Main project benefits: a 364-metre access road; a stormwater drainage system; energy-efficient smart lighting; improved access to Berth 92 and the fish landing site; support for the fishing industry and export opportunities; easier access to the Liepāja Lighthouse and other coastal sites. About the project Funding comes from the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund under the Fisheries Development Programme 2021–2027, measure U31421.2 “Strengthening Port Infrastructure Development”, sub-measure U31421.2.01 “Action 1”. On 8 November 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Authority received the Rural Support Service decision approving the project application “Construction of an Access Road at the Port of Liepāja”. The project supports strategic objective SM2 of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Development Plan 2023–2035, which envisages maintaining and strengthening the competitiveness of the Port of Liepāja, including port infrastructure maintenance and improvement to support fishing businesses. The project is also consistent with the Liepāja District Partnership community-led local development strategy 2023–2027 and its strategic objective M4, action R1 “Strengthening Port Infrastructure Development”, helping achieve the programme’s goals. title: Made in Liepāja Youth Ideas Workshop and Competition Concludes
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 18. februāris, 2025 Made in Liepāja Youth Ideas Workshop and Competition Concludes The “Made in Liepāja” youth ideas workshop, organised by the Liepāja SEZ Authority, concluded with an animated discussion and a business lunch. All general-school students were invited to contribute to shaping the business environment. In cooperation with the Education Authority and the city’s schools, a competition sought young people’s ideas for developing Liepāja’s economy. In total, 39 submissions were received, from individual students and groups. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasises that young people are the driving force behind the city’s future: their knowledge, creativity and initiative will be crucial to Liepāja’s development. It is therefore important to involve them early in discussions about business, the fundamentals of economic growth and industry prospects. “This certainly helps young people better understand their interests, recognise future opportunities and choose suitable careers. It also gives them insight into industrial trends and the city’s economic goals. Educated, enterprising and determined young people form a strong foundation for Liepāja’s growth,” he says. He was particularly pleased by the students’ conclusions and proposals, which demonstrated analytical and strategic thinking as well as a genuine desire to help shape the city’s future. A specially appointed jury of representatives from the Education Authority, Liepāja SEZ Authority and local businesses evaluated submissions from schools and Liepāja State Technical School. After lengthy discussions, the jury selected five entries for encouragement prizes — Liepāja gift cards — and five award-winning entries. Their authors took part in a discussion and business lunch with Uldis Hmieļevskis. Afterwards, the young participants said it was valuable to discuss entrepreneurship and decision-making and learn how Liepāja’s business environment is formed, including less visible challenges faced by businesses. The workshop and competition took place as part of the “Made in Liepāja” exhibition. Participants selected one of the proposed topics, conducted research at the exhibition by interviewing business owners and company representatives, and prepared conclusions and recommendations. The Liepāja SEZ Authority thanks all the active students and their teachers. When the weather becomes warmer, all participants will also be invited on a tour to see Liepāja’s economic environment and activities in the SEZ first-hand. title: Feasibility Assessment of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site Completed
text: Contact person Ivo Koliņš Head of Port Infrastructure Projects Department Tālr: (+371) 26457292 E-pasts: ivo.kolins@lsez.lv 05. novembris, 2024 Feasibility Assessment of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site Completed From 1 August to 31 October 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority implemented the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment” Bilateral Cooperation Fund initiative entitled “Preparation of a Technical and Economic Assessment for Development of the Historic Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja” (hereinafter the Initiative). The Karosta Canal and its historic seabed pollution form a unique contaminated site harming the Baltic Sea environment, not only in Latvia but across the Baltic Sea region. Since 1994, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has undertaken targeted work to restore the canal. Major remediation campaigns in 2015 and 2023 removed more than 200,000 m³ of contaminated sediment, which was placed in the historic contaminated sediment disposal site in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja. This site is a specially enclosed section of the canal waters designed for safe containment of the deposited sediment. Despite numerous studies of the environmental situation and completed remediation work, the further development of the sediment disposal site had not previously been studied, including how to limit the spread of pollutants, consider development alternatives or evaluate management scenarios. Under the Initiative, the Liepāja SEZ Authority therefore worked with Norwegian partners — the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) and Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI) — which have extensive expertise in remediation of historic marine pollution and in establishing and managing contaminated sediment disposal facilities. Together they developed alternatives for the site and identified the most promising management scenarios. Based on the preliminary assessment, NGI and NIVA recommended removing the remaining Karosta Canal seabed areas with the highest pollutant concentrations. Removing an additional 100,000 m³ of historically contaminated sediment in the final remediation stage would take up to 196 tonnes of hazardous chemicals out of the canal environment. When evaluating alternatives to reduce greenhouse gas and hazardous-substance emissions from the deposited sediment, the best-performing option was to install an additional 60-centimetre-thick protective layer isolating the contaminated material. Working together for a green Europe! The project is funded under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total project costs are EUR 264,500.00, all of which is financed by the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Port of Liepāja Handles 739,202.18 Tonnes of Cargo in October
text: 21. novembris, 2023 Port of Liepāja Handles 739,202.18 Tonnes of Cargo in October October 2023 was a busy month for stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja, which handled 739,202.18 tonnes of various cargoes. This was the highest monthly cargo volume of the year and the busiest October in the port’s history. In October, 573,200 tonnes of dry bulk cargo were handled. Grain and grain products made up the largest share, at 444,100 tonnes, more than in September of the same year (271,600 tonnes) and October of the preceding year (310,800 tonnes). Construction materials and renewable energy resources, including woodchips and wood pellets, also maintained stable volumes in the dry bulk segment. Ro-ro freight continues to grow, supported by development projects carried out by LSEZ SIA “Terrabalt” and construction of a new road connection by the Liepāja SEZ Authority. This helped ferry operator Stena Line establish six regular weekly sailings to Travemünde, Germany. The next step needed for further development is reconstruction of Berth 46. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis says the ferry route carries goods worth EUR 4 billion every year. “We can imagine how important this route is to Latvian manufacturers and the economy as a whole.” During Finance Minister Arvils Ašeradens’ working visit to Liepāja, the berth reconstruction was discussed. The minister said export-capable industries are a top government priority. “They need channels to deliver their products to other countries. Europe is our main export market. The Port of Liepāja is performing very well, and it is clearly our duty to find a way to provide the transport infrastructure. We discussed it today and will consider with the Ministry of Transport how it can be resolved.” In the general cargo segment, the downturn in the timber market continues to affect throughput. Liquid cargo has also declined substantially for the second consecutive year and now accounts for only 4% of all cargo. In October 2023, the Port of Liepāja served 112 ships and 6,268 passengers. The largest single shipment, 53,300 tonnes, was loaded by “Liepaja Bulk Terminal Ltd” onto the vessel Al Saad for delivery to Spain. Both of the port’s largest stevedores handled more than 200,000 tonnes each, well above previous months: LSEZ SIA “Liepaja Bulk Terminal Ltd” handled 297,679.44 tonnes and LSEZ SIA “Ekers Stividors LP” handled 205,800.90 tonnes. In the first nine months of that year, the port handled 5,928,273.17 tonnes of cargo, welcomed 1,168 ships and recorded 82,695 arriving and departing passengers. Was this information useful? title: Navigation Safety Improved in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 06. jūnijs, 2024 Navigation Safety Improved in the Karosta Canal at the Port of Liepāja With the installation of ship-protection guide structures beside the O. Kalpaks swing bridge in the Karosta Canal, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has completed the final component of EU Cohesion Fund project No. 6.1.1.0/17/I/004, “Restoration of the Hydraulic Structures of the Karosta Canal and Northern Entrance”. The project restored safe navigation through the northern port entrance, renovated the Karosta Canal breakwaters, dismantled Berth 1 and installed lighting in the canal, meeting its objective of improving navigation safety. The Karosta Canal is a technically complex waterway with heavy ship traffic. Its relatively narrow fairway, entrance breakwaters, protruding shoreline and especially the structures of the swing bridge complicate vessel movements and increase the risk of maritime accidents. Installing protective guide structures reduces the risk of a ship colliding with the bridge because of human error or technical problems, threatening vessel safety and traffic through the canal. The works cost EUR 2,370,583.00 in total, including EUR 1,349,192.20 from the EU Cohesion Fund. The guide structures comprise two separate installations on the southern and northern sides. Each consists of 15 steel tubular piles driven into the canal bed and connected by horizontal pipes. Each installation is approximately 98 metres long and fitted with navigation signs and composite sliding surfaces. They are designed to protect the swing bridge against collisions with vessels up to the following dimensions: Deadweight capacity — 25,000 tonnes; Length overall (LOA) — 180 metres; Beam — 28 metres; Draught — 8.6 metres. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasises the importance of preventing incidents like the 2006 collision, when the tanker “Anna” struck the northern section of the Karosta bridge, cutting traffic across the canal for several years and forcing Karosta residents to take a much longer route to the city centre. The project has substantially improved maritime safety and navigation. “Previously the maximum permitted vessel width for entering the Karosta Canal safely was 24 metres; now it is possible to accommodate wider ships.” Ivo Koliņš, Head of the Liepāja SEZ Authority’s Port Infrastructure Projects Department, says that completion of the ship guide structures near the Karosta swing bridge marks the end of EU Cohesion Fund project No. 6.1.1.0/17/I/004. Alongside the guide structures, the project included reconstruction of Berth 1, restoration of Karosta Canal breakwaters and installation of night lighting in the Karosta and Pilots’ canals. Together, these measures have significantly improved navigation safety. During the EU funds programming period 2014–2020, the Liepāja SEZ Authority implemented a broad programme to develop shared port infrastructure, placing particular emphasis on navigation safety through the following projects: “Development of Land Access Roads to the Port of Liepāja”, total eligible costs: EUR 5,853,368.57; “Improvement of Water Infrastructure at the Port of Liepāja”, total eligible costs: EUR 30,287,974.95; “Restoration of the Hydraulic Structures of the Karosta Canal and Northern Entrance”, total eligible costs: EUR 4,013,191.10. These projects directly support the goals of Latvia’s National Development Plan 2014–2020. Multimodal transit corridors comprising roads, railways and ports play an important part in national economic development: they increase the volume of goods transported, encourage new processing and service industries, and help Latvia and its residents benefit from the country’s advantageous geographical location. title: Van Oord Signs Agreement to Build Offshore Wind Support Base and Heavy Cargo Terminal in Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 20. marts, 2024 Van Oord Signs Agreement to Build Offshore Wind Support Base and Heavy Cargo Terminal in Liepāja To promote offshore wind energy development in the Baltic Sea, leading industry company Van Oord Dredging and Marine Contractors B.V. (Van Oord) plans to establish a world-class offshore wind farm support base and heavy cargo terminal at the Port of Liepāja. This is provided for in a land reservation agreement concluded between Van Oord and the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Authority. During the two-year reservation period, Van Oord will carry out preparations including research, business planning, design and the recruitment of industry partners. The Dutch company plans to begin building the offshore wind support base in the outer harbour of the Port of Liepāja in 2026, with commissioning expected by mid-2027. The new terminal will address the shortage of port infrastructure capacity needed to build wind farms in the Baltic Sea. It will also handle other oversized cargo and support manufacturing. A 55-hectare area will be created through land reclamation, providing new multifunctional cargo-handling facilities and space for manufacturing and assembly operations. Van Oord project manager Mark Bot said: “Van Oord aspires to be an initiator in accelerating the energy transition. This project is a strong example of how Van Oord can fulfil that role and bring positive change for future generations.” By becoming a developer of port infrastructure associated with offshore wind projects in the Baltic Sea, Van Oord actively supports the transition to renewable energy. Its commitment to building this much-needed infrastructure reflects the company’s aim of creating a better world for future generations. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis welcomed the decision of Van Oord, one of the offshore wind industry’s major players, to choose Liepāja as a centre for Baltic Sea wind energy. “The offshore wind support base at the Port of Liepāja will promote economic development and attract substantial foreign investment focused on a sustainable economy and green energy production. This is only one of Liepāja’s projects that will strengthen energy independence in Latvia and Europe.” Under the signed land reservation agreement, Van Oord will act as developer and investor, designing and building the offshore wind support base and heavy cargo terminal in the outer harbour of the Port of Liepāja. The project will occupy 55 hectares of the total 560-hectare area. The outer harbour is a unique part of the port, protected by breakwaters, with three port entrances and extensive opportunities for offshore wind and green energy projects. title: Declaration Signed to Establish the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 19. novembris, 2024 Declaration Signed to Establish the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre A significant declaration has been signed on the creation of the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ), bringing together several strategically important private investment projects focused on green energy, smart manufacturing and innovation. The signatories include private investors implementing development projects — Van Oord, Euroports, Smulders, CIS Liepāja, GI Termināls and Fokker Next Gen Latvia — together with the Liepāja SEZ Authority, Liepāja City Council, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA) and Riga Technical University. The joint declaration seeks to give these projects the highest priority on the government agenda and secure necessary state support through simplified procedures and approvals, access to financial instruments and infrastructure investment. The projects will contribute to the sustainability of Latvia’s economy, establish new high-tech industries and promote GDP growth and industrial development. The Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre aims to become a central player in green energy and innovative technologies in the Baltic region. Total planned investment could exceed EUR 4 billion between 2025 and 2035. Planned projects: Offshore wind support base and heavy cargo terminal at the Port of Liepāja — infrastructure to support construction of Baltic Sea wind farms and manufacturing plants for oversized structures near port berths. Implemented by Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders. Hydrogen plant and terminal — production of hydrogen using renewable energy sources. Implemented by CIS Liepāja. Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant — SAF production to help the aviation sector transition to more environmentally friendly energy sources. Implemented by GI Termināls. Hydrogen-powered aircraft production — manufacturing passenger aircraft at Liepāja Airport to help decarbonise aviation. Implemented by Fokker Next Gen Latvia. CO₂ export terminal — storage and transport of carbon dioxide captured from industrial and energy-related emissions. Implemented by GI Termināls. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis noted that the scale of private investment is unprecedented not only in the Liepāja SEZ but in Latvia as a whole. It will establish entirely new industries based on green hydrogen and oxygen production, CO₂ transport and storage, and the recovery of thermal energy, while creating opportunities for other businesses to use these resources as raw materials. “By choosing Liepāja as the location for their projects, investors demonstrate Latvia’s determination to develop green energy and smart manufacturing. The Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre will enable the region to become a leader in renewable energy and industrial innovation, attract further investment and create jobs in other sectors. Attracting investments of this scale requires professional cooperation among all parties, including the state, municipality and educational institutions. That is why we have agreed to treat the individual projects as one whole and present them as the Liepāja Sustainable Industry Centre,” Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasised. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is working to connect these projects and investors, identifying additional synergies and opportunities for new projects. Hydrogen is planned as a feedstock for SAF production and fuel for Fokker Next Gen aircraft, while CO₂ will also be needed for SAF production. Transforming the former Liepājas Metalurgs steelworks into a green industrial park will help attract other manufacturers that can use H₂, CO₂, O₂ and thermal energy as inputs. Riga Technical University plays an important role in developing sustainable industries by providing educational and research programmes through RTU Liepāja Academy. Cooperation with the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia to facilitate project implementation, as well as the involvement of Liepāja City, is equally important. About the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority: The Liepāja SEZ Authority provides a high-quality, attractive business environment and promotes the coordinated development of the SEZ territory under clear conditions. It attracts investors in smart, sustainable, high-value-added industries, particularly manufacturing, green energy and technology, creating skilled jobs with competitive salaries. title: Memorandum Signed on Sustainable Aviation Fuel Plant in the Liepāja SEZ
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 17. septembris, 2024 Memorandum Signed on Sustainable Aviation Fuel Plant in the Liepāja SEZ During a trade mission to the United States organised by the Ministry of Economics and the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, a memorandum of cooperation was signed on 16 September between US company KBR and Liepāja SEZ company GI Termināls to establish a sustainable aviation fuel production facility. KBR is a leading US provider of engineering design solutions. Under the agreement, it will supply proprietary engineering technology and equipment for a new sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) plant with planned capacity of up to 100 kilotonnes per year. The aviation fuel is planned to be produced from CO₂ emissions and hydrogen. The partnership also covers consulting and other support, with the Liepāja project scheduled for implementation by 2030. KBR Senior Vice President of Sustainable Technologies Aman Ahmad noted that this would be the company’s first project in the Baltic region and welcomed the introduction of KBR technology to the Baltic market. KBR’s portfolio includes around 20 patented technologies for the efficient processing of resources such as CO₂. “The arrival of a global player such as KBR in Latvia is an important step towards sustainable innovation. Sustainable aviation fuel production and investment in hydrogen technologies, driven by cooperation between these two companies, will undoubtedly advance Latvia’s energy sector and strengthen our industrial competitiveness,” said Minister of Economics Viktors Valainis. The Liepāja SEZ Authority, together with the municipality and national government, is developing several important investment projects to establish Liepāja as a centre for sustainable business. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said the SAF project fits well alongside several other large-scale private investment projects planned in the SEZ over the next five to seven years. Land reservation agreements have already been signed for an offshore wind support base and heavy cargo terminal, a hydrogen plant and a CO₂ export terminal. These projects will attract significant investment, promote sustainable use of H₂, O₂ and CO₂, and encourage innovation across a wide range of industries. About US company KBR KBR supplies science, technology and engineering solutions to governments and companies around the world. It employs approximately 36,000 people globally and operates in more than 30 countries. KBR works with customers worldwide to provide technology, value-added services, and long-term operations and maintenance, delivering consistent service and predictable outcomes. title: Agreement Signed on Funding Infrastructure in Liepāja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 11. janvāris, 2024 Agreement Signed on Funding Infrastructure in Liepāja Industrial Park As the transformation of the former Liepājas Metalurgs steelworks into a modern green industrial park continues — a process started in 2018 — attracting public funding is a logical next step. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis welcomed the funding, which will allow construction of essential business infrastructure on the former factory site to move from planning to implementation. “Securing funding for infrastructure is a major step towards creating Liepāja Industrial Park and gradually reopening previously inaccessible areas to residents and investors in the coming years. We envision a modern, sustainable industrial environment that creates new, well-paid jobs and hosts businesses operating according to sustainability principles.” Construction under Stage 1 of the “Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure Development” project must be completed by 31 December 2025. The park is to become a modern business environment attracting technologically advanced and innovative companies, supporting production of high-value-added goods and aligning with the European Green Deal and circular-economy principles. Under the approved strategy, implementation of the overall Liepāja Industrial Park project is expected to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 jobs. The Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City are developing the industrial park at the former Liepājas Metalurgs site, between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected NATURA 2000 nature area. Background: • In 2018, the Ministry of Economics, Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, SIA FeLM, Liepāja City Council and Liepāja SEZ Authority signed a memorandum of intent on developing the former Liepājas Metalurgs site. • In 2021, a development programme for the former steelworks territory was approved and an inter-agency agreement with Liepāja City Council was signed for its implementation. • In 2022, the local spatial plan for the former Liepājas Metalurgs site was approved. • In 2022, a remediation programme was prepared for the former Liepājas Metalurgs site. • In 2023, the Liepāja Industrial Park (LIP) Development Strategy 2023–2028 was approved. • In 2023, several construction designs were prepared for infrastructure development works in the area. • In 2023, a project application was submitted for the first street construction works in LIP, and a decision approving funding was received. • In 2023, a lease agreement was signed with SIA Liepājas Steel, valid until 31 December 2025, for dismantling and removing an electric steelmaking furnace. title: Letter of Intent to Be Signed on Modern Power Supply Infrastructure
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 16. oktobris, 2025 Letter of Intent to Be Signed on Modern Power Supply Infrastructure The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority and Liepāja City Municipality will sign a letter of intent with Latvian electricity transmission system operator AS Augstsprieguma tīkls (AST) to cooperate on infrastructure needed for a Germany–Baltic electricity interconnection in Liepāja. The agreement provisionally identifies a site at Laboratorijas Street 22/28. “New interconnections mean new opportunities for Latvia and the Baltic states as a whole. They integrate us more closely into electricity and ancillary-service markets and create conditions for new renewable energy projects, economic growth and new businesses in Latvia. Every new interconnection improves the reliability and stability of electricity supply, which is especially important in today’s geopolitical situation. AST is actively developing additional links with Estonia and Lithuania and exploring long-term connections with Sweden or Germany. Much work remains on the German link before an investment decision can be made and the project’s benefits for Latvia confirmed. When that confidence is established, we want to be ready for the next step. The signed letter of intent will strengthen Liepāja’s case as the Baltic–German interconnection’s terminal point. It will also open considerable development opportunities for Liepāja. We welcome the constructive cooperation with the Liepāja SEZ Authority and the municipality, both of which recognise the project’s benefits for the city and regional economy,” said AST board member Arnis Daugulis. Although still at an early feasibility stage, Liepāja’s decision demonstrates its determination to participate in the project and create conditions for a substantial increase in the electricity capacity available locally. That would support economic growth in Liepāja and the wider region by attracting modern, electricity-intensive manufacturing businesses. Liepāja SEZ CEO and City Council member Uldis Hmieļevskis said the Baltic–German interconnection could allow Latvia to become an exporter of wind and solar electricity while enabling new energy-intensive investment projects in Liepāja. Continuing nationally and regionally significant transmission infrastructure development, AST and the Lithuanian and German transmission operators Litgrid and 50Hertz have begun work on Baltic Hub, a major subsea electricity interconnection between Germany and the Baltic states. The approximately 600-kilometre hybrid connection would have a total capacity of 2 GW. It requires a landing location for the subsea cable, integration into the existing onshore transmission grid and a new high-voltage substation. The project is currently at an early stage: operators from all three countries are jointly examining its economic viability, financing options and other questions, including whether the optimal Baltic connection point is in Lithuania or Latvia. The Liepāja SEZ Authority regularly consults AST management and specialists to plan secure, sustainable electricity infrastructure over the long term. The letter of intent builds on successful cooperation between Liepāja and AST. In 2024, the SEZ Authority, port company Liepājas SEZ TERRABALT SIA and heavy-cargo carrier SIA ULTIMA helped deliver Latvia’s first synchronous condenser to AST’s Grobiņa substation. The equipment helps maintain inertia and stability in the transmission grid — especially important following the historic synchronisation of Baltic electricity networks with continental Europe and as more renewable generation is integrated. title: Liepāja SEZ Thanks Businesses Operating in Its Territory
text: 15. decembris, 2023 Liepāja SEZ Thanks Businesses Operating in Its Territory This year, the Liepāja SEZ Authority thanked enterprising and creative businesses for their achievements in 2023 at the Liepāja Interior Museum. As Liepāja SEZ Board Chairman Uldis Sesks noted, the venue was more than symbolic: the historic building dates back to the period when trade and the port were just beginning to develop in Liepāja. Special awards for achievements in 2023 went to: • Vecās Ostmalas Biznesa Parks, for confident and well-considered industrial park development; • SIA Dzelzsbetons MB, for its purposeful development and production of innovative products; • SIA Mols-L, for sustainable growth and resource use. • As modern technologies become part of everyday life, an award was also given to the company most active on LinkedIn. The winner was Liepāja SEZ company Vecās Ostmalas Biznesa Parks. This year, the businesses received an award made by artist Herberts Erbs, featuring a historic red brick topped with a glass pyramid. title: Public Meeting on the Environmental Impact Assessment for the Planned NorSAF Sustainable Aviation Fuel Plant
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 05. marts, 2026 Public Meeting on the Environmental Impact Assessment for the Planned NorSAF Sustainable Aviation Fuel Plant On the evening of 4 March, an initial public consultation meeting on the environmental impact assessment (EIA) for the planned NorSAF sustainable aviation fuel plant took place, with detailed explanations and discussions. The aim was to inform residents about the proposal and explain the steps to be taken as part of the EIA process. The meeting was held at Liepāja State Technical School and attended by 162 people in person and 51 remotely via Zoom. Before the NorSAF sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) project can proceed, an EIA must be completed. In accordance with a programme issued by the State Environmental Service (SES), this will involve detailed studies of the proposed technologies, production processes and, most importantly, their effects on people and the environment. Stages of the EIA procedure: On 14 January 2026, the SES decided to initiate the EIA procedure; On 20 February 2026, the initial public consultation was announced in a newspaper. Information letters were sent to residents whose properties are adjacent to the planned production site; On 4 March 2026, the public consultation meeting took place; Until 12 March 2026, residents, state authorities and local government institutions were invited to send proposals for the EIA programme to the State Environmental Service by email at pasts@vvd.gov.lv or by post to Rūpniecības Street 23, Riga, LV-1045. Within one month, the SES prepares the EIA programme based on the application and the outcome of the initial public consultation. Sector experts will assess the technologies, environmental impacts and safety issues in accordance with the programme and prepare the report. A public consultation on the completed report will take place in the second half of 2026. The EIA procedure will conclude with an opinion from the SES on the planned facility’s effects on people and the environment. NorSAF, a company operating in the Liepāja SEZ, is developing a sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) project. It has a strategically important role in reducing CO₂ emissions from European aviation and helping to achieve the European Union’s sustainability and climate-neutrality objectives. NorSAF aims to establish a modern, safe and environmentally responsible facility that complies with EU environmental requirements and international safety standards. The project envisages using sustainable feedstocks and supporting aviation’s transition to lower-emission solutions. The company supports the national strategy to move towards an entirely green power grid and plans to use only renewable energy to operate the plant. More information: www.norsaf.com/lv About the technologies The project is based on PureSAF®, a licensed technology from US company KBR — a unique Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ-SKA) solution. The technology was developed in cooperation with Swedish Biofuels, which has worked on innovative SAF solutions for more than 20 years. PureSAF® has been tested for several years by the Swedish Armed Forces, DARPA (USA), the US military, Lufthansa and various research commercialisation organisations. A small pilot plant funded by the European Commission has also operated for several years at a technical university campus in Stockholm, Sweden. KBR is responsible for scaling and engineering the technology. It is one of the world’s leading engineering companies, with more than a century of experience in industrial projects in the energy, chemicals, infrastructure and defence sectors. For the past 60 years, KBR has also provided technology and engineering solutions for NASA space programmes, demonstrating high standards of quality, safety and innovation. More information: www.kbr.com/en What does this project mean for Liepāja and the region? Around 200 new high-value-added jobs in engineering, chemistry, energy and logistics, plus approximately 200 jobs during construction. Development of businesses in the city and region, including the hospitality and leisure sectors. Long-term tax revenue for municipal and national budgets. Stronger positioning of Liepāja as a climate-neutral city and a centre of industrial innovation in the Baltics. A contribution to Latvia’s energy independence and security. This is a strategically important national energy-security and economic-development project that has already received Green Corridor status. It is aligned with Latvia’s RIS3 development strategy, supports climate objectives, strengthens the regional economy and positions Liepāja as a future centre for green energy and aviation fuel in Northern Europe. title: New LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare Production Facility Begins Operations
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 17. janvāris, 2025 New LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare Production Facility Begins Operations The newly built LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare plant for large fibreglass structures began operations at the end of last year. It is the first factory built at the Port of Liepāja directly next to a berth, allowing products to be loaded efficiently onto ships and exported by sea. The facility has created around 40 jobs with competitive pay. It covers 1,935 m² and represents an investment of approximately EUR 2.5 million. LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare is part of the Norwegian-owned Entec Group, which entered Liepāja several years ago. Until now the company had operated as a stevedore, organising the export of large fibreglass structures manufactured in Saldus. “Building this new plant is an important step in BRIMER’s development in Latvia, as it will allow us to double our production capacity here and manufacture very large composite products for the oil industry, which previously could not be produced in Latvia. Being located directly beside a port berth offers logistics advantages and makes it easier to ship cargo to customers,” emphasised Norplast Piemare board member Gatis Ginters. The new factory currently manufactures protective covers for subsea cables used in oil and gas extraction and transport. Preparations are also under way to produce fish-farming tanks. Gatis Ginters explained that the tanks will be very large: “Their diameter will be 40 metres and their height 20 metres. Our main customer is currently Saudi Arabia. We manufacture the tank components here, transport them to Saudi Arabia and assemble the large tank there. Because daytime temperatures in Saudi Arabia are very high, assembly will take place only at night, when it is below 20 degrees Celsius.” Over the past seven years, 26 new factories have been built in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. This illustrates the long-term development strategy of the Liepāja SEZ, in which the port and industry develop in close synergy and complement one another. As Entec Group director Haavard Haanes previously noted: “This factory is a significant strategic step for Entec Group, linked to long-term growth. Why Liepāja? It is a wonderful place, but there are also three key reasons. First, Liepāja supports companies and investors and offers the opportunity to build a factory in the port. Second, the Special Economic Zone provides assistance and makes development easier and faster. Third, Liepāja can supply qualified employees, from financial specialists and project managers to production workers. We greatly appreciate the infrastructure and business environment advantages offered by the Liepāja SEZ.” Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis stressed that the project combines the energy sector, the port and manufacturing in a new way, helping Liepāja become a sustainable industry centre on the eastern Baltic Sea coast and complementing existing businesses with new, safe and environmentally friendly industries. LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare currently employs around 40 people from Liepāja. If orders increase, the company plans to move to two shifts and hire another 20–30 employees. It also plans new production buildings with an area of 2,000–3,000 m². Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: Seminar “Practical Sustainability” Takes Place
text: 22. janvāris, 2025 Seminar “Practical Sustainability” Takes Place The “Practical Sustainability” seminar held at the Liepāja SEZ Authority on 22 January provides an opportunity to learn about current sustainability and lending issues. Such initiatives help businesses and organisations adapt to rapid technological development and global change by offering practical knowledge about sustainable financing and how it can support business growth. SEB Head of Sustainability Viktors Toropovs and Head of SME Financing Ģirts Priede shared expert insights into financing sustainable development. These opportunities are especially relevant to businesses seeking to integrate sustainability principles into their operations and obtain financing to support their objectives. The seminar is especially valuable to Liepāja SEZ companies and other local businesses, helping them understand recent trends in lending and develop strategies that meet market requirements as well as environmental and social responsibility standards. title: RTU and Liepāja Municipality to Boost the Region’s Industrial Potential
text: 02. decembris, 2024 RTU and Liepāja Municipality to Boost the Region’s Industrial Potential Riga Technical University (RTU) is ready to contribute its knowledge and experience in partnership with Liepāja City Council and the Liepāja SEZ Authority to strengthen Liepāja’s industrial potential and train highly skilled specialists capable of developing innovations that advance the city and region. Opportunities for cooperation were discussed at the RTU Council meeting held in Liepāja on 28 November. “One of RTU’s principal tasks is to promote the development of Latvia’s economy by educating new specialists and creating new products and innovations. RTU’s resources in Liepāja, particularly RTU Liepāja Academy, which is so important to the region, enable the university to offer its research and educational potential to help drive economic growth in Liepāja and Kurzeme,” said RTU Council Chair Andris Vanags. RTU aims to create a new educational ecosystem together with Liepāja, strengthening capacity in engineering, high technology and innovation while maintaining and developing the humanities and social sciences traditionally represented at RTU Liepāja Academy. The university also seeks to advance engineering education and help address the shortage of mathematics and natural science teachers in Latvian schools. RTU’s leadership sees the university as a strong partner for Liepāja. Following the consolidation of higher education, the RTU ecosystem now includes two major regional institutions: RTU Liepāja Academy and RTU Liepāja Maritime College (LJK). Together under the “RTU Liepāja” brand, they offer expertise for regional development. Liepāja is pursuing ambitious projects involving renewable energy, green hydrogen, sustainable aviation fuel and the capture and processing of CO₂ emissions. “RTU and RTU Liepāja are important partners in research and the development of new study programmes, helping create and advance high-value-added sustainable industry projects in Liepāja while educating highly skilled young professionals,” said Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš. Representatives of RTU Liepāja presented their achievements and future plans to the municipal and special economic zone leadership. RTU Liepāja Academy intends to strengthen engineering studies by specialising in hydrogen technology research. An academic group and hydrogen laboratory are being established to work actively with Latvian and international partners. Hydrogen research is one of RTU’s scientific excellence areas and is also pursued by its Faculty of Natural Sciences and Technology. Building on its strengths in education and the humanities, RTU Liepāja Academy also plans to establish a modern neuroscience laboratory to support local industry by helping businesses understand customer behaviour and increase competitiveness. RTU Liepāja Maritime College has also increased its capacity, recruiting 11 new lecturers with maritime expertise. The European Maritime Safety Agency (EMSA) has assessed the quality of the college’s education; the accreditation process has begun, lifelong-learning provision has been strengthened, and maritime education is being promoted to attract new students.
