title: Local Plan to Open Jaunliepāja Canal Waterfront Submitted for Public Consultation
text: 01. augusts, 2024 Local Plan to Open Jaunliepāja Canal Waterfront Submitted for Public Consultation A local development plan has been prepared for part of Jaunliepāja to open a currently closed canal waterfront to the public and establish conditions for balanced residential and public development. The draft plan was submitted for public consultation from 29 July to 6 September 2024 to collect residents’ views and institutional opinions. The plan covers 10.77 hectares of Jaunliepāja beside the Trade Canal, between the Tram Bridge and the Old Cemetery and adjoining Kaiju, Jelgavas and Aldaru streets. Part of the area is currently within the restricted boundaries of the Port of Liepāja. The main proposed solutions focus on creating a diverse, sustainable public space with buildings, amenities and landscaping. By restoring the historic street network, the plan would reopen links to the waterfront and provide access to the proposed pedestrian promenade from the Tram Bridge and Aldaru, Kroņu, Kapsētas and Jelgavas streets. Existing development would be organised into three new blocks partly reflecting the waterfront’s historic layout. The local plan proposes changing the land-use designation from port technical infrastructure to mixed-use central development. Alongside preserving and renovating historically valuable buildings, this would allow new apartment buildings, offices, shops and service facilities, as well as tourism, leisure, sports and cultural facilities and related amenities. Mixed-use central development would be permitted in the block between the Trade Canal and Kaiju Street and on the opposite side of Kaiju Street. “An open, publicly accessible Jaunliepāja waterfront will give our city not only a new appearance, but also new life and energy for Jaunliepāja. These changes will affect the daily lives of Liepāja residents, particularly those living in Jaunliepāja. I therefore invite people to take an active role in shaping their city by participating in the local plan consultation: examine the proposed solutions, join discussions and share their views,” said Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš. The Jaunliepāja canal waterfront is intended to become an important part of the city’s public space, with streets, squares, green corridors and a pedestrian promenade offering views of Old Liepāja. Planting will be a major landscape feature, while existing railway tracks and port infrastructure elements will be incorporated into the public space. “Cargo ships are getting larger, and the Trade Canal has become too narrow and shallow for them. Cargo operations have gradually moved to other areas of the port: Winter Harbour, Freeport and Karosta. The berths on the Old Liepāja side of the Trade Canal are already publicly accessible, with fishing vessels and yachts mooring there and people enjoying walks. Restaurants, offices and hotels have moved into former port warehouses. We envision similar development on the Jaunliepāja side of the canal,” said Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. The plan sets out detailed land-use and building regulations, including building zones, density and height limits. It also proposes infrastructure integrated with surrounding areas, including pedestrian and cycle routes, streets and utility networks. Vehicle movements would be kept to a minimum, mainly to provide access to buildings. Only emergency and service vehicles would be allowed on the pedestrian promenade. The proposal would also connect two existing cycle-route sections between Aldaru Street and the Tram Bridge, helping create a continuous city cycling network. Full details of the local plan for the area between Kaiju, Aldaru and Jelgavas streets and Jaunā ostmala can be found: on the national geospatial information portal www.geolatvija.lv, under Spatial Development Planning (https://geolatvija.lv/geo/tapis#document_25742); on the municipal website www.liepaja.lv, under Public Participation – Public Consultations (https://www.liepaja.lv/aktualas-apspriesanas/); in person in the ground-floor lobby at Peldu Street 5 during office hours. Two meetings will be held so that residents and institutions can review and assess the proposed amendments to the spatial plan: 21 August at 18:00 – an in-person walk through the local planning area (meeting location to be confirmed); 28 August at 17:00 – an online public consultation meeting via Zoom. To help prepare the participant list, please register in advance and indicate which meeting you wish to attend by completing the form at epakalpojumi.liepaja.lv/lv/projects/preview/366/ or emailing your name, surname and represented sector to buvvalde@liepaja.lv. Please register at least one day before the event (by 20 August for the site visit or 27 August for the Zoom meeting) to receive information about the consultation arrangements. Comments and suggestions on the draft local plan are invited until 6 September 2024 inclusive: electronically via the national geospatial information portal https://geolatvija.lv/geo/tapis#document_25742, signing in through latvija.lv using online banking or an e-signature; in person or by post to Liepāja Building Authority, Peldu Street 5, Liepāja, LV-3401, or by email to buvvalde@liepaja.lv. Individuals must provide their name, surname, residential address and telephone number; legal entities must provide their name, registration number, address and telephone number. For further questions and consultations, contact the Liepāja Building Authority by telephone on 63 404 725. The local plan amending the Liepāja spatial plan for the area between Kaiju, Aldaru and Jelgavas streets and Jaunā ostmala up to O. Kalpaka Street has been prepared in accordance with the planning brief issued by Liepāja Building Authority and approved by Liepāja City Council at its meeting on 10 November 2022. It also incorporates residents’ opinions collected in a survey before the drafting process began. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Saeima Approves Amendments to Tax Rules for Freeports and Special Economic Zones
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. februāris, 2024 Saeima Approves Amendments to Tax Rules for Freeports and Special Economic Zones The version of the Law on the Application of Taxes in Freeports and Special Economic Zones approved by the Saeima includes several provisions that could support Liepāja SEZ companies, attract new investors and reduce competitive disadvantages relative to other special economic zones in the Baltic Sea region. The most important amendments are: Extend the period during which anticipated wage costs are eligible until 31 December 2035 (previously 31 December 2024). This will help Liepāja continue to attract skilled and well-paid workers. Allow tangible assets to be acquired through finance leases. Make shipbuilding and synthetic fibre industries eligible for support under the law. The Liepāja SEZ Law stipulates that the zone was established to develop and promote trade, industry, shipping, air transport and the international exchange of goods through Latvia. Its tasks include attracting investment in manufacturing and infrastructure and creating new jobs in Liepāja, thereby promoting development across the region. From the establishment of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone in 1997 through 2023, its companies invested approximately EUR 403 million in total, including in modern technologies. In 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded 15 investment agreements with Liepāja SEZ companies, with planned investment totalling EUR 5,481,903.28. In 2024, the Liepāja SEZ Board approved five investment projects with total planned investment of EUR 4.390 million. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: SEB Bank Provides EUR 2 Million for Norplast Piemare Factory Construction
text: 26. jūlijs, 2024 SEB Bank Provides EUR 2 Million for Norplast Piemare Factory Construction SEB Bank has granted EUR 2 million in financing to Liepāja Special Economic Zone company Norplast Piemare AS for the construction of a new factory in the Port of Liepāja. The planned facility will cover almost 2,000 square metres, with construction expected to be completed in autumn 2024. It will manufacture exceptionally large composite products that could not previously be produced in Latvia. Its location beside a port berth will provide logistical advantages and simplify the transport of oversized cargo. Norplast Piemare is a subsidiary of the Norwegian ENTEC Group, which entered Liepāja several years ago when its shares were acquired by Entec Norplast. The Norwegian-owned Entec Norplast was established in Latvia in 2001 and specialises in fibreglass products used in marine safety equipment, oil extraction, transport, recreation, wastewater treatment, fish farming and other sectors. The company already has a factory in Saldus and exports its products worldwide. “SEB Bank has worked with Entec Norplast for a long time. The company has carved out a niche in manufacturing specialised large-scale composite products. The new factory will produce, for example, large fish tanks, for which a port location is important for transport. We are pleased to support the expansion of manufacturing in Latvia and to cooperate with an internationally recognised and respected company that continues to grow here,” said SEB Bank board member Arnis Škapars. “This factory is an important strategic development step linked to our companies’ long-term growth. We are expanding businesses, and the new facility in Liepāja gives us both the opportunity to grow and a unique way to ship large composite structures directly to customers from a deep-water berth. We are pleased that our financial partner, SEB Bank, has recognised the potential of businesses operating in such a specialised field. The growth story of Entec Norplast and Norplast Piemare in Latvia will continue with even greater momentum, now with two factories in Saldus and Liepāja,” said Entec Norplast CEO and Norplast Piemare board chair Māris Meija. title: Seminar to Discuss Karosta Canal Pollution and Its Effects on the Environment and Human Health
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 07. oktobris, 2022 Seminar to Discuss Karosta Canal Pollution and Its Effects on the Environment and Human Health A seminar and discussion entitled “The Effects of Pollution on Human Health and the Environment: Historical and Everyday Pollution” will take place at Liepāja University on 13 October 2022 at 10:00. Experts from the Latvian Institute of Aquatic Ecology and Liepāja City Council will describe the effects of pollution on the environment and human health and the work carried out to reduce it. Experts from Liepāja University and the Liepāja Special Economic Zone will focus on the practical aspects of reducing pollution in Karosta Canal and the effects of those measures on the environment and human health. This is the third educational seminar in the information campaign for the Liepāja SEZ Authority project “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja”. The seminar aims to educate the public about the impacts of historical and everyday pollution on the environment and human health, highlighting present and future risks and the steps being taken to mitigate them. Karosta Canal is part of everyday life and socioeconomic development in Liepāja. Cleaning the canal will improve environmental quality and biodiversity in the canal and the ecology and water quality of the Baltic Sea, while giving residents of Liepāja and Karosta and visitors a cleaner, healthier and more pleasant place to live, grow and relax. Historically, military base activities have significantly affected environmental quality in Karosta Canal. Pollution includes petroleum products such as benzene, xylene and hydrocarbons, as well as heavy metals including mercury, arsenic, lead, zinc, copper and cadmium, concentrated in the canal’s silt and sand deposits. The Karosta Canal ecosystem is degraded, with very limited flora and fauna. Pollution in the canal also affects nearby perch, which migrate to other waters such as Lake Liepāja. Perch found there have markedly elevated mercury concentrations. Pollution therefore spreads beyond the local area through food chains, affecting other levels of the ecosystem and ultimately people. The project continues work to clean Karosta Canal that began in 2015. Earlier stages removed man-made debris such as scrap metal, concrete and timber and established a specially equipped containment area for contaminated sediments at the eastern end of the canal, where some pollutants have already been deposited. The work significantly improved the canal’s ecological status: concentrations of petroleum products and heavy metals in sediments fell severalfold, but remain above the limits set by Cabinet regulations. To meet environmental improvement objectives for Karosta Canal and the Baltic Sea, remediation work will remove 202,247 m³ of non-compliant sediment from the canal bed, containing 400 tonnes of contaminated deposits. The project is financed through the Norwegian Financial Mechanism’s 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total costs amount to EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000 in Norwegian Financial Mechanism funding. Working together for a green Europe! Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Port of Liepāja Handles 619,715.82 Tonnes of Cargo in September
text: 12. oktobris, 2023 Port of Liepāja Handles 619,715.82 Tonnes of Cargo in September In September, 619,715.82 tonnes of various cargoes were handled at the Port of Liepāja. Agricultural and ro-ro cargo flows remain stable, while approaching winter traditionally increases shipments of renewable energy resources, including wood chips. Together with businesses, the Liepāja SEZ Authority continues to attract new cargo groups, including from Central Asian countries. Dry bulk remained the largest cargo category in September at 430,700 tonnes (423,800 tonnes in September 2022). Agricultural commodities dominated this segment, with volumes affected by variable and unfavourable summer weather and growing competition. According to Juris Matvejevs, head of LSEZ SIA Liepaja Bulk Terminal Ltd, the transport and logistics sector has changed substantially in recent years, making cargo flows harder to plan and forecast. Nevertheless, the company continues to attract cargo. Its stability is supported by storage capacity and the ability to handle more than 30 types of cargo at the same time. LSEZ SIA Liepaja Bulk Terminal Ltd handled 219,856.59 tonnes in September (154,480 tonnes in September 2022), considerably more than a year earlier. Agricultural cargo remains one of the most variable categories, with pronounced seasonality and an active grain season lasting only four to five months, depending on the harvest. Building materials continue to provide stable dry bulk volumes, largely thanks to cement produced in Latvia. Autumn also brings higher shipments of wood chips, a renewable energy source used for heating in Scandinavian countries. Sugar imported from Brazil and forwarded to Uzbekistan has become a relatively new cargo type over the past year: the Port of Liepāja handled 33,000 tonnes of sugar in September 2023 alone. Other new cargoes include various metal ores and ferroalloys. To showcase the advantages of the Port of Liepāja and discuss the development of international transport and logistics services and infrastructure, as well as the reduction of barriers to global trade, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis and port businesses participated in the sixth International Transport and Logistics Business Forum “New Silk Way” and the “TransLogistica Kazakhstan 2023” exhibition. “Kazakhstan, like other Central Asian countries, is one of the cooperation partners of Port of Liepāja businesses. As logistics routes change, agricultural products and metal alloys are exported, while sugar, soybeans and engineering products are shipped to Central Asia through Liepāja,” said Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. Freight ferry services provided by Stena Line and LSEZ SIA Terrabalt also play an important role in supply chains, offering the most direct connection between Latvia and Germany. In September, the port company Terrabalt handled 155,461.87 tonnes (143,430 tonnes in September 2022). In September 2023, the Port of Liepāja served 118 ships and 7,304 passengers. The largest export shipment was 33,000 tonnes of Latvian-grown wheat loaded onto the vessel “Aviona” at DanStore terminal berths. The largest import was sugar carried by “Tai Harvest” and unloaded at Liepaja Bulk Terminal Ltd. In the first nine months of the year, the Port of Liepāja handled 5,189,070.99 tonnes of cargo, served 1,056 ships and recorded 76,427 arriving or departing passengers. Was this information useful? title: Traffic Restrictions on O. Kalpaks Bridge During School Holidays
text: 19. oktobris, 2023 Traffic Restrictions on O. Kalpaks Bridge During School Holidays From 23 to 29 October, O. Kalpaks Bridge will be periodically closed to pedestrians and motor vehicles. Changes in traffic arrangements will be indicated by road signs. The closures are necessary to install protective barriers in Karosta Canal near O. Kalpaks Bridge and prevent future accidents that could result in prolonged bridge closures, as happened after the 2006 accident. Under the construction method, the four central piles can only be driven when the swing bridge across Karosta Canal is open, allowing normal bridge operations to resume as quickly as possible. The ship-protection barriers will consist of 26 tubular piles driven into the Karosta Canal bed using vibration and impact methods. Project manager Ivo Koliņš asks residents for understanding, as the construction will cause some inconvenience. “During the school holiday week, traffic arrangements will change and the bridge will be periodically closed to pedestrians and vehicles. Until the work is completed, the installation of the piles will also create a low, booming sound during daylight hours. The contractor, AS BMGS, has extensive experience with similar work and promises to complete it as quickly as weather conditions allow.” The work must be completed within 30 days. AS BMGS submitted the most economically advantageous tender, valued at EUR 2,370,583.00 excluding VAT. To improve navigational safety and minimise the risk of accidents, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority continues to implement EU Cohesion Fund project No. 6.1.1.0/17/I/004, “Reconstruction of the Hydraulic Structures of Karosta Canal and the Northern Gates”. On 23 October this year, AS BMGS will begin the final component of the project: installing protective barriers at the supports of O. Kalpaks Bridge in Karosta Canal. Barriers are planned on both sides of the bridge to protect it against possible collisions. The most recent major accident occurred in 2006, when the Georgian tanker “Anna”, commanded by an inattentive captain, struck the northern support of the bridge, causing damage so severe that repairs took four years. The barriers are designed to withstand the impact of a moving vessel up to 150 metres long. Because the bridge, built in 1906, is an engineering heritage monument, care is being taken to preserve its historic appearance. During the 2014–2020 EU funds planning period, the Liepāja SEZ Authority implemented an extensive programme to develop shared infrastructure at the Port of Liepāja, with particular emphasis on improving maritime safety through the following projects: Project “Development of Land Access Routes to the Port of Liepāja”, total eligible costs: EUR 5,853,368.57; Project “Improvement of Water Infrastructure at the Port of Liepāja”, total eligible costs: EUR 30,287,974.95; Project “Reconstruction of the Hydraulic Structures of Karosta Canal and the Northern Gates”, total eligible costs: EUR 4,013,191.10. These projects directly support the objectives of the National Development Plan of the Republic of Latvia for 2014–2020. Multimodal transit corridors, linking roads, railways and ports, play an important role in the country’s economic development. They enable increasing volumes of goods to be transported and encourage new processing and service industries in Latvia, helping the state and its residents benefit from the country’s advantageous geographical position. title: This Year’s Grain Season Starts Later Than Usual at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. septembris, 2026 This Year’s Grain Season Starts Later Than Usual at the Port of Liepāja In August 2026, stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja handled 341.83 thousand tonnes of various cargoes. Dry bulk traditionally represented the largest category, including agricultural products, building materials and wood chips, at 188.16 thousand tonnes. General cargo was the second-largest group at 153.24 thousand tonnes, of which 129.2 thousand tonnes were carried on the regular Liepāja–Travemünde ferry service to Germany. The volume of cargo handled in August 2026 was lower than the average for the same period in other years.* 2026 – 84.01 thousand tonnes; 2025 – 161.7 thousand tonnes; 2024 – 184.7 thousand tonnes; 2023 – 212.6 thousand tonnes; 2026 – 217.2 thousand tonnes. * Grain handled in August, in thousands of tonnes, by year Historically, and since operations resumed in the 1990s, the Port of Liepāja has deliberately developed its grain terminals, emphasising local cargoes (around 50% of the total, with the remainder being transit cargo), including exports of grain grown in Latvia. In early August 2026, grain terminals at the port began accepting Latvian barley and wheat under existing contracts. Their combined simultaneous storage capacity is approximately 730 thousand tonnes. The largest dry bulk terminal at the Port of Liepāja, LSEZ SIA Liepaja Bulk Terminal LTD, has signed contracts with leading Latvian grain exporters, including Baltic Agro, Latraps and Linas Agro, for the period from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. The company also works with international businesses such as Archer Daniels Midland (ADM). According to its board chair, Juris Matvejevs, Latvian grain is arriving more slowly than in previous years. The first export shipment of Latvian wheat left Liepāja only on 6 September, when the Panamax-class vessel “Tuo Fu 8”, carrying 65,486.39 tonnes, departed for Abu Dhabi. The terminal also works with Central Asian countries, exporting agricultural products to EU countries and importing Argentine soybeans and Brazilian sugar. Its partners include ADM (USA), one of the world’s leading traders and processors of agricultural commodities. ADM purchases, stores, transports and processes grain and oilseeds, connecting farmers to food, feed and industrial markets worldwide. The second-largest grain terminal, DanStore, was established in 1999 as a joint venture between the Danish companies Svane Shipping and Scanmills. In 2003, the international agricultural commodity trader and processor Bunge became a strategic partner, helping create and develop the specialised dry bulk terminal. DanStore currently operates under contracts that include Latvian grain companies Baltic Agro and Agerona. Wheat grown by Latvian farmers is now being loaded aboard the Handysize-class vessel “Jera” for delivery to Nigeria. Local cargoes have always been a priority for the Port of Liepāja’s stevedoring companies. However, to ensure even use of handling capacity, they also contract with the world’s largest freight logistics operators. Approximately half of the port’s cargo originates in Latvia, while the other half is transit cargo. In recent years, considerable effort has gone into developing a transit corridor with Central Asian countries. If grain transit to third countries is restricted, global grain—and therefore food—prices could rise sharply, potentially contributing to inflation in Europe, including Latvia, and worldwide. title: Topping-Out Ceremony for Mols L’s New Warehouse
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 17. augusts, 2026 Topping-Out Ceremony for Mols L’s New Warehouse Stevedoring company Mols L is building a warehouse of approximately 5,000 square metres at the Port of Liepāja, significantly expanding its storage facilities. Total investment is approximately EUR 1.55 million. The new warehouse will accommodate around 20,000 tonnes of cargo, including agricultural products and wood pellets. This will increase the capacity of Mols L’s enclosed warehouses to 60,000 tonnes. For comparison, before 2015 the port company’s warehouse capacity was just 9,000 tonnes. The warehouse is being built by SIA AJ Meistars, while the steel roof structures were supplied by the Swedish-owned company Borga. Construction began last autumn, and the facility is expected to enter service in September, when the grain season starts at the port. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Revised Port of Liepāja Regulations Enter into Force
text: Contact person Tālr: E-pasts: 27. augusts, 2024 Revised Port of Liepāja Regulations Enter into Force A revised version of the Port of Liepāja Regulations entered into force on 27 August 2024. The new regulations clarify the duties, functions, powers and responsibilities of the Port of Liepāja Harbour Master, as well as response procedures in the event of maritime accidents. They also update rules governing vessels’ stays in port, mooring and berth operation. According to Harbour Master Gints Ažēns, the revised regulations update requirements for vessel traffic and communications in the port, with safety as the primary focus. title: International Conference on the Impact of Anthropogenic Chemical Pollution on the Baltic Sea
text: 06. oktobris, 2023 International Conference on the Impact of Anthropogenic Chemical Pollution on the Baltic Sea On 11–12 October 2023, Liepāja will host the international conference “Anthropogenic chemical pollution’s impact on the Baltic Sea and its related ecosystems” as part of project No. NFI/AK/02, “Remediation of Historically Contaminated Sites in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja”. Everyone is invited to watch the conference live online. The conference will bring together leading researchers and experts from the Baltic Sea region to share their knowledge and experience in water pollution research and the remediation of contaminated sites. Further information about the conference and its programme is available at: https://ej.uz/konferenesprogramma 11 October 2023, 10:00–18:00: international conference, presentations and panel discussions involving representatives of research and environmental management institutions from Latvia, Estonia, Finland and Norway. On 12 October 2023, participants will have the opportunity to learn more about the history of Karosta, the environmental restoration work carried out under the project and the results achieved. The conference is free and open to everyone. Participation is possible in person or remotely via the live broadcast on 11 October. Working together for a green Europe! The project is financed under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism’s 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total project costs are EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000.00 in Norwegian Financial Mechanism funding. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Stena Line to Acquire Terrabalt and Operate Port Terminals in Liepāja
text: 10. septembris, 2025 Stena Line to Acquire Terrabalt and Operate Port Terminals in Liepāja To further promote trade growth and supply-chain resilience in the Baltic Sea region, ferry operator Stena Line will acquire all shares in the Liepāja port operator Terrabalt. By acquiring the Latvian company Terrabalt, Stena Line will take over operations at the Ro-Ro, dry bulk and general cargo terminal in Liepāja, Latvia’s third-largest port. The Port of Liepāja operates within the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (LSEZ), a free-trade zone established in 1997 that includes the port, industrial areas and airport. Stena Line currently operates two vessels on the Liepāja–Travemünde route. “By investing in Liepāja, we continue to act as a long-term partner to Latvia and help strengthen the country’s competitiveness and economic growth. We believe in a prosperous future for the Baltic Sea region, where investment in infrastructure and closer cooperation between countries will strengthen trade and economic resilience throughout the region,” said Stena Line CEO Niclas Mårtensson. “Trade and supply-chain resilience require a long-term outlook, and we will continue building the future in close partnership with the Latvian state, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone and, of course, our customers,” said Carl-Johan Hellner, Head of Ports and Terminals Operations at Stena Line. Stena Line’s Baltic Sea network also includes several other routes. Two vessels operate between Ventspils and Nynäshamn. Since May 2023, Stena Line has held the rights to provide ferry terminal services at Ventspils, Latvia’s second-largest port. Three vessels serve the Karlskrona–Gdynia route, and the company holds a majority stake in the port operator Karlskrona Baltic Port (KBP). The Trelleborg–Rostock route is served by Sweden’s only two ferries capable of carrying railway wagons, providing important backup capacity and a link to continental Europe. “By acquiring the port operator in Liepāja, we will strengthen our position and create even better conditions for our regional customers in the future. We look forward to developing the port and its infrastructure to ensure safe, high-quality operations,” Mårtensson concluded. Completion of the acquisition remains subject to approval by Latvia’s Competition Council and other authorities. Until approval is granted, the terminals will continue to be managed by their current owners. The transaction value has not been disclosed. About Stena Line Stena Line is one of Europe’s leading ferry operators, with approximately 40 vessels and 20 routes in Northern Europe and the Mediterranean, operating 25,700 sailings each year. The company is an important part of Europe’s logistics network and develops new combined-freight solutions integrating rail, road and sea transport. Stena Line also plays an important role in European tourism through extensive passenger services. Founded in 1962, the family-owned company is headquartered in Gothenburg. It employs 6,200 people and has an annual turnover of SEK 19.5 billion. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. Starptautiska kino projekta ietvaros trīs dienas satiksmei būs slēgts O. title: New Streets Ceremonially Opened in Liepāja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 21. novembris, 2025 New Streets Ceremonially Opened in Liepāja Industrial Park Today, 21 November, newly constructed streets in Liepāja Industrial Park, on the site of the former Liepājas Metalurgs factory, were ceremonially opened with the symbolic cutting of a steel bar and a performance of the song “Dzelzsgriezējs” by Ainars Virga. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis noted that, just as the ironcutter in the band Līvi’s song cuts through the old world, the city is turning a new page in its industrial history and beginning a greener chapter. “The first new streets are only the beginning, the first step toward gradually returning the former Liepājas Metalurgs site to the city and making it publicly accessible. At the same time, it is important to make it attractive to investors who will establish modern manufacturing enterprises offering well-paid jobs based on smart technologies and the basic principles of the circular economy.” The idea of establishing Liepāja Industrial Park was endorsed in a memorandum of intent on 23 August 2018. It stated that the park would ensure efficient use of the historic Liepājas Metalurgs site, contribute positively to the city’s sustainable economic development, increase the number of exporting companies and export volumes, boost direct and indirect tax revenue for the state and municipality, and make rational use of the electrical capacity already available on the site. The memorandum was signed by the Ministry of Economics, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, Liepāja City Council, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority and SIA FeLM. The memorandum was signed on behalf of the Ministry of Economics by the then Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economics, now Minister of Finance, Arvils Ašeradens. “Liepāja works intelligently, cooperating with businesses and developing projects in close synergy with the government and municipality. Liepāja is a success story. Latvia needs strong businesses and places where they can be built and developed so that we can attract investment in high-value-added activities, create export-capable companies and generate new skilled, well-paid jobs. The newly acquired business areas will encourage economic activity not only in Liepāja but also contribute to Latvia’s overall economic growth.” The world is changing, industrial technologies are changing, and attitudes toward the environment are changing. This is not a choice but a necessity. Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš said: “Liepāja is deliberately moving toward greener, smarter and more sustainable development. We have significantly reduced our dependence on fossil energy and are transforming industry into modern, environmentally friendly and competitive manufacturing. By opening the first new streets in Liepāja Industrial Park today, we are literally and symbolically marking the transition from a legacy of heavy metallurgy to climate-neutral, smart and high-value-added industry. This area will become a place where innovation and green energy meet manufacturing and export capacity, showing that Liepāja does not merely follow the European Green Deal but helps shape it.” Recent trends in the global economy show that Europe needs manufacturing centres in various sectors, creating development opportunities for Liepāja as well. Over the next ten years, Liepāja intends to develop a green, high-capacity industrial park on the former Liepājas Metalurgs site. It should become an example of green manufacturing and circular-economy efficiency, creating more than 1,500 new jobs. The world is changing, industrial technologies are changing, and attitudes toward the environment are changing. This is not a choice but a necessity. Liepāja SEZ Board Chair Uldis Sesks said: “We are proud of our industrial traditions, but today we are witnessing an important moment of industrial transformation. We are changing so that industry becomes safer and friendlier to people and the environment. Sustainable thinking is embedded in the DNA of the future green Liepāja Industrial Park, with education, innovation and circular-economy principles clearly established. Today Liepāja needs manufacturing facilities that are friendly to the environment and local residents, export-oriented and capable of attracting sufficient intellectual resources.” At the end of 2023, the Liepāja SEZ Authority secured the first investments for Liepāja Industrial Park and signed an agreement with the Central Finance and Contracting Agency for EUR 10 million in Recovery and Resilience Facility funding to implement the project “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure, Phase 1”. The project provides for 3,865 metres of electricity networks, eight new transformers and three street sections with utilities, including water supply, domestic and stormwater sewerage and district heating. Approximately 2 kilometres of streets have now been built on Inženieru, Eksporta and Dzelzsgriezēja streets. The total value of the completed construction works is EUR 9.23 million. The works were carried out by SIA Aland and SIA CTB. In parallel with the SEZ Authority’s project, the municipality implemented the reconstruction of Meldru Street under the programme “Support for the Development of Public Infrastructure Needed for Business, Promoting the Transition to a Climate-Neutral Economy”. Naglu and Martena streets are also expected to be commissioned by the end of the year. In 2026, construction is planned for the intersection and connecting road between Brīvības, Čuguna and Eksporta streets. Savings will allow an additional 289-metre section of Martena Street to be built next year. An application under the EU Cohesion Policy Programme 2021–2027 has also been approved, enabling the demolition of fuel-oil tanks next year and the connection of the newly built streets into a single network. Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and the City of Liepāja on the former Liepājas Metalurgs site, between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected NATURA 2000 nature area. The site is being developed as a modern business environment to attract technologically advanced, innovative companies manufacturing high-value-added products in accordance with the European Green Deal and environmentally friendly circular-economy principles. Under the approved development strategy, the overall project aims to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 jobs. Background: 2018: The Ministry of Economics, Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, SIA FeLM, Liepāja City Council and Liepāja SEZ Authority signed a memorandum of intent to develop the former Liepājas Metalurgs factory site. 2019: Consolidation of real estate on the former Liepājas Metalurgs site began. 2021: A development programme for the former factory site was approved, and an interinstitutional agreement on its implementation was concluded with Liepāja City Council. 2022: The local spatial plan for the former Liepājas Metalurgs site was approved. 2022: A remediation programme for the former Liepājas Metalurgs site was prepared. 2023: The Liepāja Industrial Park (LIP) Development Strategy for 2023–2028 was approved. 2023: Several construction designs were developed for infrastructure works on the site. 2023: An application for funding the first street construction works in LIP was prepared and submitted, and a positive funding decision was received. 2023: A lease agreement with SIA Liepājas Steel was concluded until 31 December 2025 for dismantling and removing the electric steelmaking furnace. Autumn 2024: Construction of the first street sections and utility networks, and electrification of the entire site, began. 2025: Disposal of existing industrial buildings began. title: Time Capsule Laid in the Foundations of the New LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare Factory
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 30. novembris, -0001 Time Capsule Laid in the Foundations of the New LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare Factory On Wednesday, 26 June, a time capsule containing a message for future generations was embedded in the foundations of the new LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare factory. The facility will produce large fibreglass structures, adding another factory to the Liepāja SEZ and to the Port of Liepāja. It will be located at Berth 64, 37 Atslēdznieku Street, Liepāja, and will cover 1,935 m². Total planned investment in the project is EUR 2.5 million. LSEZ AS Norplast Piemare is a Norwegian-owned EnTEC Group company that entered Liepāja several years ago. Until now, it has operated as a stevedoring company, handling exports of large structures manufactured in Saldus. “Building the new factory is an important step in the development of BRIMER, a company within Entec Group, in Latvia. It will allow production capacity in Latvia to double and enable the manufacture of very large composite products for the oil industry, which previously could not be manufactured here. The factory’s location next to the port berth offers logistical advantages and facilitates shipment to customers,” said Norplast Piemare Board Member Gatis Ginters. Twenty-four new factories have been built in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone over the past seven years, showing that both foreign and domestic investors appreciate the quality of the city’s business environment. “I am pleased that Liepāja continues to strengthen its position as a regional industrial centre. The new factory will not only contribute substantially to our city’s economic growth but will also increase Latvia’s overall manufacturing capacity. Proximity to the port and Liepāja’s logistics advantages make our city an appropriate location for strategically important projects of this kind. We are proud that high-value-added companies choose Liepāja as their base, and I wish the project every success in this important phase of development,” said Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš. Several Entec Group representatives attended the ceremony. Group Director Haavard Haanes said: “For Entec Group, this factory represents an important strategic development step with long-term significance. Why Liepāja? Because it is wonderful here, but also for three key reasons. First, Liepāja supports entrepreneurs and investors and offers the opportunity to build a factory directly in the port. Second, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone provides support and helps businesses develop more quickly and easily. Third, Liepāja can provide skilled employees, from financial specialists and project managers to production workers. We highly value the infrastructure and business-environment advantages offered by the Liepāja SEZ.” Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasised: “It is a real pleasure and a source of pride to announce that another new factory is taking shape. This demonstrates that the current long-term development strategy and philosophy of the Liepāja SEZ work: the port and industry operate and develop in close synergy, complementing each other. This new facility brings together the energy sector, the port and manufacturing at a new level. It marks the Port of Liepāja’s ambition to become an energy hub on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea.” UPTK was selected to build the new industrial hall. Its Director Zigurds Kirhners was brief: “Let it be built! May we all succeed together, and see you in six months at the opening of the new factory.” The time capsule was laid in the presence of Norplast Piemare Board Member Gatis Ginters, Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš, Entec Group Director Haavard Haanes, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis, Liepāja Deputy Mayor Salvis Roga and UPTK Director Zigurds Kirhners. title: Memorandum of Understanding Signed for a Green Hydrogen Plant in Liepāja
text: 02. decembris, 2025 Memorandum of Understanding Signed for a Green Hydrogen Plant in Liepāja On 1 December, a memorandum of understanding was formally signed at the Embassy of the Kingdom of Norway in the presence of the Minister for Climate and Energy, representatives of the Ministry of Economics, an adviser to the Prime Minister and officials from Liepāja municipality. The signatories were hydrogen producer and terminal developer SIA CIS Liepaja and wind-energy producer SIA Vindr Latvia. The memorandum aims to examine long-term renewable-electricity supplies through the national grid for a new green hydrogen plant in Liepāja. It represents an important step toward one of Northern Europe’s largest and most advanced green-hydrogen initiatives: a renewable-energy complex and hydrogen production facility in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone. A long-term power-purchase agreement between an electricity producer and buyer, setting an agreed price and delivery period, would give the buyer a stable and predictable energy supply. At the same time, it would provide the producer with predictable long-term returns on investment in renewable-energy projects and would substantially support renewable-energy development, Latvia’s energy independence and companies’ decarbonisation goals. As previously reported, SIA CIS Liepaja, bringing together Norwegian and Latvian companies, plans to build one of Northern Europe’s largest and most advanced green hydrogen plants in the Liepāja SEZ by 2030, investing more than EUR 550 million and creating at least 100 jobs. The plant is expected to produce approximately 150,000 tonnes of green hydrogen annually, much of which will be exported to Germany and other EU member states, supporting Europe’s transition to a carbon-neutral economy. CIS Liepaja plans to attract more than EUR 1.2 billion in EU investment, while projected annual revenue after full development would exceed EUR 600 million. “Green hydrogen is more than an energy carrier: it is becoming a cornerstone of the green transition. Growing worldwide interest in renewable resources offers Latvia the opportunity to play an important role in tomorrow’s clean-energy economy. For projects of this scale, cooperation among all stakeholders is essential, and we highly appreciate local and national support. Predictable rules, stable governance, access to renewable resources and proximity to continental European markets, combined with an industrial strategy for green hydrogen, create attractive conditions for developing one of Europe’s most competitive and sustainable hydrogen sectors here,” said CIS Liepaja CEO and Board Member Tor Arne Pedersen. “Vindr is proud to support Latvia’s transition to clean, locally generated electricity. Our wind farms in Kurzeme and Latgale will provide reliable, certified renewable energy, create jobs and support regional economic development while strengthening energy security and reducing dependence on imports. We are currently developing a 900 MW renewable-energy project portfolio in Latvia, and this is the first agreement in the country providing for 150 MW to be supplied for green hydrogen production. Through long-term cooperation with CIS Liepaja, we are helping to develop emerging sectors such as hydrogen production and contributing to a stronger, greener and more competitive Latvia. Together, we are turning renewable energy into an engine of sustainable growth and prosperity,” said Vindr CEO and Co-founder Jan-Olav Øderud. “The green transition is a major global challenge, and green hydrogen plays a decisive role. Norway is proud to be among Europe’s leaders in green hydrogen production. Projects such as the partnership between CIS Liepaja and Vindr in Liepāja demonstrate the strong relationship between Latvia and Norway. This is a major cooperation project with enormous energy and potential to promote innovation, sustainability and economic growth throughout the region,” said Norway’s Ambassador to Latvia, Ine Måreng. New technologies combined with renewable-energy resources open unprecedented opportunities for Latvia’s economic growth, international competitiveness and independence. The green hydrogen plant will establish Liepāja as a strong partner and an important location on Europe’s economic map. “Energy independence and energy security are important strategic priorities for our government. Energy-generation projects must be developed with reliable, long-term partners who plan to operate in Latvia for decades. We value energy independence and affordable energy for residents and businesses, and that is why we support the joint CIS Liepaja and Vindr project,” said Minister for Climate and Energy Kaspars Melnis. Liepāja was selected as the location for the green hydrogen plant because of the port’s advantages, recommendations from the Norwegian Embassy in Latvia and the quality of its business environment. The city offers a unique combination of stable infrastructure, access to renewable electricity, fresh water and industrial land, alongside a political environment supportive of sustainable industry. “We are pleased that this project is being implemented in Liepāja, a fast-growing city pursuing the ambitious goal of becoming climate-neutral by 2030. We have worked together on the project for several years and accomplished a great deal. Signing the memorandum of understanding is an important milestone toward its implementation,” said Liepāja City Council Member and Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis. About the signatories SIA CIS Liepaja brings together Norwegian and Latvian companies and is a member of the Norwegian–Latvian and German–Latvian Chambers of Commerce. Its objective is to promote the supply of CO₂-neutral energy to the EU internal market, including Latvia. Its hydrogen production project in the Liepāja Special Economic Zone has been recognised as an investment project of national strategic importance. Vindr was founded in 2019 to develop wind-energy projects in Norway and Sweden and become a leading renewable-energy producer in Northern Europe. It has since expanded throughout the Nordic and Baltic region. SIA Vindr Latvia is developing a portfolio of more than 900 MW of onshore wind projects, focusing on long-term partnerships and bringing international expertise and financing. title: O. Kalpaks Bridge to Close for Three Days for an International Film Production
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 16. oktobris, 2026 O. Kalpaks Bridge to Close for Three Days for an International Film Production From 16 to 24 October, Liepāja will briefly become a filming location for an international production. The city will host filming of an adaptation of “The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo”, from the internationally popular Millennium book series, produced by Left Bank Pictures, known for “The Crown” and “Dept Q”. Oskars Kalpaks Bridge has been selected as one of the series’ key filming locations. The bridge will close to pedestrians and road traffic for three days, and shipping traffic will also be restricted. Filming on O. Kalpaks Bridge will take place from 19 to 21 October. Drivers, cyclists and pedestrians are asked to plan their journeys to and from Karosta in advance and allow additional travel time. Working with the municipality, special buses will run along a diversion route. Details of this service will be posted at both ends of the bridge. Regular public transport will also be diverted. Closure of O. Kalpaks Bridge to pedestrians and vehicles: From 08:00 on 19 October 2026 until 22:00 on 21 October 2026. Access to the square near O. Kalpaks Bridge and to the access road and parking area at the southern breakwater of Karosta Canal will also be restricted during filming. Vessel traffic in Karosta Canal will be restricted during filming. The Liepāja SEZ Authority thanks the stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepāja for supporting this major film project and rescheduling their operations where possible. Five port terminals operate actively in Karosta Canal — Baltic Transhipment Center, Schwenk, DG Termināls, Norsaf and Baltex Bulk — as does LZK, which continues ship repair work at the Tosmare docks. The selection of Oskars Kalpaks Bridge as a central filming location will bring Liepāja significant international attention. The production is expected to reach millions of viewers in different countries, giving the city a powerful platform for raising its profile. Successfully hosting a production of this scale will reinforce Liepāja’s reputation as an internationally connected, professional port city capable of managing complex projects. “It increases the chances of attracting future film, arts and creative-industry projects, bringing long-term economic and reputational benefits to the city and the wider region.” Was this information useful? title: Procurement Continues for Reconstruction of Berth 46 at the Port of Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. decembris, 2025 Procurement Continues for Reconstruction of Berth 46 at the Port of Liepāja The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority is continuing the procurement process for the reconstruction of Berth 46 at the Port of Liepāja. Following an independent expert’s opinion, it has clarified the qualification criteria for potential bidders and extended the bid submission deadline to 7 January 2026. To support the development of freight and passenger ferry connections with the Port of Liepāja and ensure uninterrupted cargo flows, the SEZ Authority launched the procurement process for the reconstruction of Berth 46 on 2 October 2025. The project attracted considerable international interest. On 19 November 2025, the Procurement Monitoring Bureau received a complaint contesting one of the qualification requirements concerning previous experience in similar construction projects. To assess the complaint objectively, the SEZ Authority engaged an independent expert. Based on the opinion received, it revised the qualification requirements, broadening the pool of interested suppliers and appropriately extending the submission deadline. This complies with the purpose of the Law on the Procurement of Public Service Providers: ensuring equal and fair treatment of suppliers without restricting competition. Regular ferry services are strategically important not only to the economies of Liepāja and Latvia but also to EU transport and military mobility. Last year, the berth handled 1.8 million tonnes of cargo with an estimated value of EUR 4 billion. The reconstruction will allow two cargo vessels or freight-passenger ferries up to 240 metres long and with draughts of up to 11 metres to be handled safely at the same time. Works will include additional mooring piles, reconstruction of berth structures and dredging from 10.5 to 12.0 metres. To accommodate modern Ro-Ro and Ro-Pax ferries, a shore-power supply system and local wastewater reception facilities will also be installed. Reconstruction of Berth 46 is expected to be completed by 31 December 2027. Berth 46 is located in the Freeport area of the Port of Liepāja, in the middle of the eastern shoreline. It is 51.5 metres wide, 204.5 metres long on its northern side and 181.0 metres long on its southern side. Built between 1972 and 1975 to berth and service Soviet naval vessels and submarines, it is now used for scheduled services on the Liepāja–Travemünde ferry route. The powerful engines used during berthing and unberthing place considerable stress on the structure. Reconstruction is necessary because construction defects and overall deterioration, despite repair works, are irreversibly undermining the berth’s technical condition and operational safety. title: Karosta Canal Remediation Project Continues
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 22. februāris, 2022 Karosta Canal Remediation Project Continues By the end of April this year, the Liepāja SEZ Authority plans to announce a procurement procedure for remediation works in Karosta Canal to remove historical pollution. It is continuing the project “Remediation of the Historically Contaminated Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja, Phase II”, aimed at reducing the negative impact of historically contaminated sediments on the environment, human health and the ecological condition of the Baltic Sea. For many years, Karosta served as a base for the Soviet Baltic Fleet, including ships and submarines. Naval activities discharged untreated wastewater, petroleum products and heavy metals, including mercury and lead, into the canal. As a result, Karosta Canal became one of the most polluted sites in Latvia. During the first phase of the Karosta Canal remediation project, approximately 50,000 m³ of large-scale waste was removed from the water. In Phase II, the plan is to dredge approximately 200,000 m³ of sediments contaminated with petroleum products and heavy metals, cleaning an area of 36 hectares. After several studies, the Liepāja SEZ Authority concluded that the contaminated sediment layer in some parts of the canal exceeds 1.5 metres. Five of the most polluted locations have been identified for remediation. Ivo Koliņš, Head of the Market Research and Analytics Department at the Liepāja SEZ Authority, explains that remediation will focus on the commercially used part of the canal. “The middle of the canal, where vessels move and propellers cause turbulence, can stir up these materials. When we receive reports of an oil film appearing in the canal, in 90% of cases it is historical pollution.” To achieve the project’s objective, remediation works are expected to remove 202,247 m³ of sediments from the canal bed that do not meet statutory standards and contain 400 tonnes of hazardous chemicals. The project is funded under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total project costs are EUR 5,117,647.05, of which EUR 4,350,000.00 comes from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. Additional information: Between 1994 and 2010, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and government institutions financed dozens of geoecological studies to prepare the Karosta Canal remediation project. The decision to implement Phase I was made only in 2012. With funding from the EU Cohesion Fund, the project “Remediation of the Historically Contaminated Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja, Phase I” was implemented by 31 December 2015. Large-scale man-made waste, including scrap metal, concrete blocks and timber, was recovered and disposed of from an area of 78 hectares. Approximately 60,000 m³ of contaminated sediment was also removed from the most polluted 10-hectare section and deposited in a specially equipped disposal site at the eastern end of Karosta Canal. The project implementation period is from 1 August 2021 to 31 December 2023. The project budget is EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000.00 in co-financing from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. “Working together for a green Europe” Was this information useful? title: Continuing Our Work to Develop Strong and Sustainable Industry in Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 27. septembris, 2024 Continuing Our Work to Develop Strong and Sustainable Industry in Liepāja This week, the Liepāja SEZ Authority participated in the international WindEnergy Hamburg 2024 conference and exhibition to further develop sustainable and renewable energy projects in the industrial and port areas of the Liepāja SEZ. Renewable energy and its successful use depend above all on effectively combining expertise from industry, energy and maritime sectors. At WindEnergy Hamburg 2024, business discussions took place with companies that have already decided to invest in Liepāja and are working towards final investment decisions after completing the preparatory phase. This involves resolving a broad range of environmental, administrative, technical, financial and cooperation issues, as well as customer acquisition and public communication. The Liepāja SEZ Authority’s task is to provide businesses with a clear path towards making these decisions. Proactive, transparent, competent and confident action is essential to deliver planned projects that would make a major contribution to the city, the country and the wider region while improving energy security and stability. All the planned projects will contribute to Latvia’s economy. In the short term, during initial implementation, service providers, educational institutions, designers, environmental consultants and construction companies will benefit. In the long term, the projects will stimulate science and research, create high-value-added export products and generate a significant number of skilled, well-paid jobs, increasing tax revenue for municipal and national budgets. The Liepāja SEZ Authority has long been working with project developers, investors, the municipality and the state to develop sustainable industry in Liepāja, including an offshore wind support base, green hydrogen production and sustainable aviation fuel production. These complementary projects will also encourage the development of education and science. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Construction of Liepāja Industrial Park Continues
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 07. aprīlis, 2026 Construction of Liepāja Industrial Park Continues From 8 to 14 April, traffic on Brīvības Street towards the city centre will be restricted to one lane due to construction work under the project “Development of Street Infrastructure on the Former Liepājas Metalurgs Factory Site, Phase 1”. Following the winter construction break, work on streets and utility networks in the future Liepāja Industrial Park is actively continuing. Construction continues on a section of Čuguna Street and a signal-controlled intersection, which will form a new access road from Brīvības Street, complete with the necessary utilities and landscaping over a length of 120 metres. Construction has begun on a 400-metre extension of Martena Street. A construction design has been prepared and a procurement procedure announced for the dismantling of the fuel-oil storage facility, remediation of the contaminated site and construction of a 400-metre connection to Eksporta Street. Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas Metalurgs factory site, between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets in Liepāja. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected NATURA 2000 nature area. Under the approved development strategy, the aim is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 new jobs. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Businesses Invited to Participate in the “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition on 31 January–1 February 2025
text: 22. oktobris, 2024 Businesses Invited to Participate in the “Made in Liepāja” Exhibition on 31 January–1 February 2025 Liepāja will celebrate its 400th anniversary in 2025. To give residents and visitors the opportunity to discover the business environment of Liepāja and South Kurzeme during the anniversary year, the “Made in Liepāja” exhibition will take place from 31 January to 1 February. Businesses are invited to apply to participate by 26 November. The “Made in Liepāja” exhibition is organised to allow businesses from different industries to present their products and services to residents and visitors, meet potential customers, new employees and partners, and help visitors discover the diverse business environment of Liepāja and the surrounding area. “Liepāja has historically been an industrial city, and we have much to be proud of. Both large enterprises and small and medium-sized businesses operate here, creating unique products and services. I invite entrepreneurs to take part in the ‘Made in Liepāja’ exhibition. It is not only an opportunity to show residents and visitors what they have achieved, but also to meet potential employees and inspire younger generations to pursue their professional careers here in Liepāja,” emphasises Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš. To register for the exhibition, participants must sign in to Liepāja’s electronic application system and complete the application form: https://epakalpojumi.liepaja.lv/lv/projects/preview/390/ . Participation is free of charge. The exhibition will take place at the Liepāja Olympic Centre, 39 Brīvības Street. Throughout 2025, Liepāja will host a wide range of anniversary events bringing together culture, sports, art, entrepreneurship and other fields through activities involving residents. Residents and visitors will be able to take part in events celebrating Liepāja’s historical heritage and inspiring new traditions and future achievements. The public will be invited to participate in activities including the “Made in Liepāja” business exhibition, concerts and performances, anniversary-week events, urban greening initiatives and other occasions. title: Businesses Continue Investing in Development, Building New Production Facilities and a Transformer Substation
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 16. februāris, 2026 Businesses Continue Investing in Development, Building New Production Facilities and a Transformer Substation The first two investment agreements of the year have been concluded with Liepāja SEZ companies, for a total of EUR 2,078,514.00. The Liepāja SEZ Board reviewed and approved both projects, setting the aid intensity and granting the right to apply direct tax relief to the planned investments only after they have been made. The maximum permitted aid intensity for the eligible project costs is 60%. For reference: In 2025, 21 investment agreements were concluded, with total planned investments of EUR 3,709,554.24. title: Business Breakfast by the Lighthouse
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 08. augusts, 2025 Business Breakfast by the Lighthouse On 8 August, the Liepāja SEZ Authority invited guests to its monthly “Business Breakfast” to introduce the newly built Syfud fish processing factory and the Authority’s projects to develop infrastructure required by the fishing industry. Entrepreneurs also had an opportunity to visit the lighthouse, which, in cooperation with the municipality, is planned to open to visitors within about a year with a multimedia exhibition on port history. Starting at 8 a.m., entrepreneurs and representatives of business support organisations gathered on Roņu Street at the entrance to Syfud. Company representatives described how the business was established, the construction process, production, export markets, recruitment and major challenges. The Syfud factory, which manufactures various crab sticks and salmon-based fish products, opened at the end of 2024. At approximately EUR 80 million, it represents one of the largest manufacturing investments in recent years. The company currently employs about 230 people, approximately 100 of whom joined in the last six months. It plans to increase staffing as production grows. Addressing the entrepreneurs, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis explained that the Authority continues to develop infrastructure needed by fishermen at the Port of Liepāja. Three projects have already been completed. The construction design for an access road at 6 Roņu Street, Liepāja, is now in its final stages, intended to provide access to the fish landing site at Berth 92, alongside reconstruction of two port berths. The work will be carried out under action 4.1 M4/R1, “Strengthening the Development of Port Infrastructure”, within the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund’s 2023–2027 Action Plan for the Fisheries Development Programme 2021–2027, under “Implementation of Community-Led Local Development Strategies”. Meanwhile, the municipality is implementing a project to create a multimedia exhibition on the history of the Port of Liepāja inside the lighthouse. Using modern light, sound and video installations, it will tell the history of trade, seafaring and fishing at the port. “Business Breakfast” is a wonderful opportunity to meet in the morning, share experience, find inspiration to work better, more ambitiously, innovatively and intelligently, learn about government support opportunities and make new contacts. “Business Breakfast” is an event organised by a business support team consisting of the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (Vita Liepiņa), Altum (Ilze Zandberga), the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority (Evita Pērkone), Vecās Ostmalas Business Park (Inese Kurvina), Impact HUB Liepāja (Zane Feldmane), Green Tech Latvia (Anete Grundberga), the Latvian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (Roberts Gaižutis), the Kurzeme Planning Region (Signe Bumbiere), the Latvian Rural Advisory and Training Centre (Aleksejs Kačanovs), Liepāja District Partnership (Santa Brāle), South Kurzeme Municipality (Egita Bublauska), Liepāja City Municipality (Arnis Vītols), RTU Liepāja Academy (Dace Medne), and the Norwegian Chamber of Commerce in Latvia (Gatis Ginters). title: Karosta Canal Remediation Project Phase II Begins
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 14. septembris, 2021 Karosta Canal Remediation Project Phase II Begins The Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority is beginning implementation of the project “Remediation of the Historically Contaminated Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja, Phase II”. Its objective is to reduce the negative impact of historically contaminated sediments in Karosta Canal on the environment, human health and the ecological status of the Baltic Sea. Remediation will involve removing 202,247 m³ of sediment from the canal bed that does not meet statutory standards and contains 400 tonnes of hazardous chemicals. The project is financed under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. Total costs amount to EUR 5,117,647.05, of which EUR 4,350,000.00 is Norwegian Financial Mechanism funding. The project will benefit society as a whole by contributing to the objectives and actions of the Helsinki Commission (HELCOM) Baltic Sea Action Plan: restoring the good ecological status of the Baltic Sea, ensuring the diversity and dynamics of its ecosystem, and maintaining a clean, healthy and productive marine environment under conditions typical of the sea. The marine environment should be used sustainably, preserving its potential for current and future generations. As a result of the project, Liepāja residents will no longer face the risk of exposure to historical pollution, and the ecological status of the sea and the quality of the surrounding environment will be significantly improved. According to Liepāja SEZ CEO Jānis Lapiņš, the project is unique and will achieve several goals: addressing environmental and ecological issues in the Baltic Sea region, removing the site from HELCOM’s Baltic Sea list of “hot spots”, and creating opportunities to further develop active business operations in the Karosta Canal basin and adjacent areas. The project is being implemented with the Latvian partner, the association “Baltijas krasti”, and the Norwegian partner, the Norwegian Institute for Water Research. The partners’ experience is essential to achieving the project objectives. Knowledge transfer is needed for successful implementation, along with public information activities about the impact of climate change on historically contaminated sites and the interaction between such sites, human health and the ecological status of the sea. On 13 September 2021, the Liepāja SEZ Authority signed an agreement with the Latvian project partner, the association “Baltijas krasti”. Following coordination with the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Regional Development, an agreement with the Norwegian Institute for Water Research is expected to be signed within the next month. The Authority is simultaneously preparing procurement documentation to identify the most economically advantageous bid for the works. The project must be completed by 31 December 2023, although most of the contaminated soil is expected to be dredged during the 2022 construction season. History: Karosta Canal (cadastral No. 1700 010 0073) is an artificial waterway built in the late nineteenth century for the naval fleet of the Russian Empire. From the second half of the twentieth century, the area was a closed military zone of the naval forces of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR) for approximately 50 years, until their withdrawal from Latvia in 1994. During the Soviet period, the canal was operated without regard for potential environmental harm: ships were refuelled improperly and wastewater was discharged into the canal, with heavy-metal and petroleum contamination far exceeding permissible limits. Toxic substances from these practices accumulated in the canal-bed sediments, creating a serious ecological threat to the Baltic Sea. After the collapse of the USSR and the military withdrawal in 1994, there was no longer a responsible polluter to whom the “polluter pays” principle under the Law on Pollution could be applied. As early as 1992, HELCOM identified Karosta in Liepāja as one of the most polluted military sites in the Baltic Sea region, and the remediation of Karosta Canal was included in the HELCOM Baltic Sea Action Plan. The canal is registered in the Register of Polluted and Potentially Polluted Sites under No. 17004/5138 and appears on HELCOM’s Baltic Sea hot-spot list as Hot Spot No. 48, Liepāja City and Port. Following the collapse of the USSR, the Liepāja SEZ Authority became the manager of the historically contaminated site. The state entrusted it with Karosta Canal (cadastral No. 1700 010 0073) for port operations and with the special sediment disposal site built at the eastern end of the canal in 1998 with PHARE financial support (cadastral No. 1700 010 0306) for managing contaminated sediments. Between 1994 and 2010, the Liepāja SEZ Authority and state institutions financed dozens of geoecological studies to prepare the Karosta Canal remediation project. The decision to implement Phase I was not made until 2012. With EU Cohesion Fund financing, the project “Remediation of the Historically Contaminated Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja, Phase I” was completed by 31 December 2015. Large-scale man-made waste (scrap metal, concrete blocks, timber and other materials) was removed and disposed of from a 78-hectare part of the canal. Approximately 60,000 m³ of contaminated sediments were also removed from the most polluted 10-hectare section and placed in a specially equipped disposal site at the eastern end of Karosta Canal. About the project partners: In implementing the remediation of the historically contaminated Karosta Canal site in Liepāja, the Liepāja SEZ Authority aims to create added value for society by helping meet HELCOM’s Baltic Sea Action Plan objective of restoring the sea’s good ecological status. For additional public benefit, the Authority selected partners with expertise in marine and inland-water environmental projects and a long record of investment in scientific research. They also communicate to the public the close links between human health, the environment and the sustainable use of resources. The public awareness campaign will be implemented by the association “Baltijas krasti”, a member of the international organisation EUCC Coastal & Marine Union since 2010. Its role is to plan and implement communication and publicity activities and prepare their results. It contributes years of experience and knowledge in successful project delivery and in sharing information on environmental and climate issues with the wider public and specific target groups. The Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) will facilitate the exchange of experience among the project partners. NIVA is Norway’s leading institute for basic and applied research on marine and fresh waters. Its research covers a wide range of environmental, climate and resource-related fields. NIVA has world-class interdisciplinary expertise and broad scientific activities, combining research, monitoring, assessment, problem-solving and consultancy services at international, national and local levels. NIVA will demonstrate and provide examples of remediation work at comparable sites in Norway, share expertise with the Latvian personnel who will be responsible for maintaining the remediated site, and prepare practical recommendations for further measures required to remove the site from HELCOM’s hot-spot list. NIVA will contribute its long-established understanding of marine ecology, the actual interactions of pollutants in the environment and methods for correctly assessing their effects on human health and the environment. The institute will in turn gain experience of addressing the legacy of a large contaminated military site in Liepāja and understanding its actual impact on the Baltic Sea’s ecological status. Based on its longstanding experience of implementing earlier phases of the Karosta Canal project, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has concluded that the expertise of professional partners is essential to successful delivery. Karosta Canal remediation is unique on a European scale, and its results must meet best practice in environmental protection projects. NIVA was selected specifically for its expertise in marine ecology. After remediation is complete, the Authority will need knowledge of further ecological research, monitoring and management necessary to ensure that the remediated site meets HELCOM’s Baltic Sea Action Plan objective of achieving good ecological status in the Baltic Sea. The project implementation period is from 1 August 2021 to 31 December 2023. The project budget is EUR 5,117,647.05, including EUR 4,350,000.00 in co-financing from the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. “Working together for a green Europe” Was this information useful?
