title: Construction of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure Begins
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 23. septembris, 2024 Construction of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure Begins Today, 23 September, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Authority ceremonially launched construction of Liepāja Industrial Park by symbolically demolishing the former entrance checkpoint of the “Liepājas metalurgs” factory. The site will be transformed into a modern, green industrial park based on circular-economy principles. First-phase construction has begun, with streets and utility infrastructure to be built in three stages, as well as new electricity distribution networks. The works will partially open the formerly closed factory site to the public and create opportunities to attract the first investors. To build the first streets in Liepāja Industrial Park, several old buildings must be demolished, including the former open-hearth steelworks checkpoint. Liepāja Mayor Gunārs Ansiņš said: “By demolishing the old checkpoint that once controlled access to the Liepājas metalurgs site, we are symbolically turning a new page in Liepāja’s industrial history. I hope that in the years ahead this area will become one of Latvia’s strongest green industrial parks, bringing together successful businesses, creating new jobs and strengthening the economy of the city, region and country.” Phase I of the “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure” project is being implemented using EUR 10 million from the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Based on the procurement results, A-Land will carry out stage 1.1 under a EUR 1.6 million contract and stage 1.3 for EUR 1.85 million; SIA CTB will implement stage 2.1 for EUR 2.8 million. All three street sections will receive utility infrastructure: water supply, domestic sewage, stormwater drainage and district heating networks. AS Sadales tīkls will begin building electricity supply networks alongside the street works. Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis said: “This is only the beginning, the first step towards building streets, pedestrian paths and cycle lanes on the former Liepājas metalurgs factory site, gradually bringing it back into the city and making it publicly accessible. At the same time, it is important to make the area attractive to investors who will establish modern manufacturing businesses, creating well-paid jobs based on smart technologies and circular-economy principles.” Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas metalurgs factory site between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets in Liepāja. It borders Lake Liepāja, a specially protected NATURA 2000 nature area. The park is intended as a modern business environment attracting technologically advanced and innovative companies that produce high-value-added goods in line with the European Green Deal and environmentally friendly circular-economy principles. Under the approved strategy, the overall plan is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 jobs. For reference: In 2018, the Ministry of Economics, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, SIA FeLM, Liepāja City Council and the Liepāja SEZ Authority signed a memorandum of intent to develop the former Liepājas metalurgs site. In 2019, the Liepāja SEZ Authority acquired 10 properties on the former Liepājas metalurgs site, covering a total of 60.6 hectares. In 2021, the development programme for the former Liepājas metalurgs site was approved and an interinstitutional agreement was concluded with Liepāja City Council on its implementation. In 2022, the local spatial plan for the former Liepājas metalurgs site was approved. In 2022, a remediation programme was prepared for the former Liepājas metalurgs site. In 2023, the Liepāja Industrial Park (LIP) Development Strategy for 2023–2028 was approved. In 2023, several construction designs were prepared for the development of infrastructure in the area. In 2023, an application for financing the first street construction works in Liepāja Industrial Park was prepared and submitted, and a positive funding decision was received. In 2023, a lease agreement was signed with SIA Liepājas Steel, valid until 31 December 2025, for the dismantling and removal of the electric steelmaking furnace. At the end of 2023, an agreement was concluded with the Central Finance and Contracting Agency on EUR 10 million in Recovery and Resilience Facility funding to implement Phase I of the “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure” project. title: Infrastructure Construction to Begin at Liepāja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 15. augusts, 2024 Infrastructure Construction to Begin at Liepāja Industrial Park Within the next month, the Liepāja SEZ Authority will start the first construction works to transform the former Liepājas Metalurgs steelworks site into a modern Liepāja Industrial Park based on circular-economy principles. Three procurement procedures for the first new street sections have now been completed, and an agreement on electrification of the area through new modern electricity networks has been approved. Construction is scheduled for completion by 31 December 2025. This will partially open the formerly closed factory territory to the public and allow the first investors to be attracted. The Liepāja SEZ Authority has approved the procurement results for the first street construction works under Phase I of the “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure” project. Work will begin within the next month to transform the former Liepājas Metalurgs factory into a modern green industrial park and begin opening the area to public access. Following procurement, A-Land will implement stage 1.1 for EUR 1.6 million and stage 1.3 for EUR 1.85 million, while SIA CTB will carry out stage 2.1 for EUR 2.8 million. All three street sections will receive utility networks, including water supply, domestic sewerage, stormwater drainage and district heating. AS Sadales tīkls will also begin building electricity supply infrastructure in parallel with the street works. Phase I of the “Development of Liepāja Industrial Park Infrastructure” project is being implemented with EUR 10 million in funding from the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Liepāja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepāja SEZ Authority and Liepāja City Municipality on the former Liepājas metalurgs site between Brīvības, Meldru, Ezermalas, Parka and Zemnieku streets. It borders Lake Liepāja, a protected NATURA 2000 site. The objective is to create a modern business environment that attracts innovative, technologically advanced businesses and encourages the production of high-value-added goods in line with the European Green Deal and environmentally friendly circular-economy principles. According to the approved strategy, the plan is to attract over EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 jobs. For reference: In 2018, the Ministry of Economics, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, SIA FeLM, Liepāja City Council and the Liepāja SEZ Authority signed a memorandum of intent on the development of the former Liepājas metalurgs site. In 2021, the development programme for the former Liepājas metalurgs site was approved, and an interinstitutional agreement on its implementation was concluded with Liepāja City Council. In 2022, the local spatial plan for the former Liepājas metalurgs site was approved. In 2022, a remediation programme for the former Liepājas metalurgs site was developed. In 2023, the Liepāja Industrial Park (LIP) Development Strategy for 2023–2028 was approved. In 2023, several construction designs for the development of the area’s infrastructure were prepared. In 2023, a project application for the first street construction works in the park was prepared and submitted, and confirmation of funding was received. In 2023, a lease agreement was concluded with SIA Liepājas Steel until 31 December 2025 for the dismantling and removal of the electric steelmaking furnace. At the end of 2023, an agreement was concluded with the Central Finance and Contracting Agency on EUR 10 million in Recovery and Resilience Facility funding for Phase I of the Liepāja Industrial Park infrastructure development project. title: Feasibility Study Launched for the Development of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site
text: Contact person Ivo Koliņš Head of the Port Infrastructure Projects Department Tālr: (+371) 26457292 E-pasts: ivo.kolins@lsez.lv 09. augusts, 2024 Feasibility Study Launched for the Development of the Karosta Canal Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site From 1 August to 31 October 2024, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority will implement the Bilateral Cooperation Fund initiative “Preparation of a Technical and Economic Feasibility Assessment for the Development of the Historically Contaminated Sediment Disposal Site in Karosta Canal, Port of Liepāja” under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment” (hereinafter the Initiative). Karosta Canal in the Port of Liepāja, and the historical pollution in its bed, represent a unique contaminated site degrading the Baltic Sea environment, not only in Latvia but throughout the Baltic Sea region. Since 1994, the Liepāja SEZ Authority has pursued targeted measures to restore the canal’s environment. Major remediation campaigns carried out in 2015 and 2023 removed more than 200,000 m³ of contaminated sediments from the canal and deposited them at the historical sediment disposal site in Karosta Canal. This site is a specially enclosed part of the canal waters where contaminated sediments can be stored safely. Despite numerous studies of environmental conditions and remediation in Karosta Canal, and despite completed remediation works, no study had yet addressed the further development of the contaminated sediment disposal site, including measures to prevent the further spread of pollutants deposited there, possible development alternatives and the assessment of management scenarios. Under the Initiative, the Liepāja SEZ Authority will work with Norwegian partners — the Norwegian Institute for Water Research (NIVA) and the Norwegian Geotechnical Institute (NGI). Their considerable experience in remediating historical marine pollution and establishing and managing contaminated sediment disposal sites will help develop alternatives for the disposal site and identify the most promising management scenarios. Working together for a green Europe! The project is financed under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2014–2021 programme “Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation and Environment”. The total cost is EUR 264,500.00, fully financed by the Norwegian Financial Mechanism. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders Join Forces to Develop a Leading Baltic Offshore Wind Energy Hub in Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 25. aprīlis, 2024 Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders Join Forces to Develop a Leading Baltic Offshore Wind Energy Hub in Liepāja Today, 25 April 2024, at “Wind Works”, the largest wind energy conference in the Baltic states, leading marine construction company Van Oord announced a cooperation agreement with international port operator Euroports and steel construction manufacturer Smulders. The companies will form a consortium to develop a leading offshore wind energy hub in the Baltic Sea at the Port of Liepāja. The new terminal at the Port of Liepāja will address the shortage of port infrastructure capacity needed to build offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea. It will also handle other oversized cargo and support manufacturing development. The 55-hectare site will be created through land reclamation, providing new multifunctional cargo-handling infrastructure and space for additional manufacturing and/or assembly facilities. Euroports is one of Europe’s largest port infrastructure companies, with 50 terminals and logistics platforms worldwide, strategically located along key trade routes in Europe and China. Each year, Euroports handles more than 70 million tonnes of liquid bulk, dry bulk and container cargo. Smulders is an international multidisciplinary construction company with more than 1,700 employees in Belgium, the Netherlands, Poland and the United Kingdom, focusing on civil and industrial steel construction and offshore wind projects. Van Oord project manager Mark Bot said: “Signing this cooperation agreement with our partners is a major step towards developing an offshore wind support base and oversized cargo terminal at the Port of Liepāja. It demonstrates not only the interest of important offshore wind industry partners but also the expertise and commitment needed to deliver a project of this scale in Liepāja.” Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis welcomed the fact that leading offshore wind companies had joined forces and selected Liepāja as the most suitable location for a wind farm support base in the Baltic region. “Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders are industry professionals whose combined expertise in wind energy will help transform the energy sector in the Baltic region, bringing positive change for future generations.” The consortium agreement between Van Oord, Euroports and Smulders is the next step towards excellence in every aspect of the project’s development: Pooling and applying expertise from design and construction to commissioning and maintenance. Developing comprehensive solutions for the production of steel components and efficient logistics for transporting wind farm components. Creating optimised supply chains, minimising potential risks and ensuring positive financial performance. Setting high standards for environmental and social responsibility, including circular-economy principles and sustainability. Earlier in 2024, Van Oord signed a two-year reservation agreement with the Liepāja SEZ Authority to develop a world-class offshore wind support base and oversized cargo terminal, expected to begin operations in 2027. title: Amendments Extending Liepāja SEZ Tax Relief Submitted to the Saeima for Approval
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 11. marts, 2026 Amendments Extending Liepāja SEZ Tax Relief Submitted to the Saeima for Approval Today, 11 March, the Saeima Budget and Finance Committee decided to submit the draft law “Amendments to the Law on the Application of Taxes in Free Ports and Special Economic Zones” to the Saeima for approval in its third reading. At the Budget and Finance Committee meeting, Liepāja SEZ CEO Uldis Hmieļevskis stressed that extending the existing tax framework for Liepāja SEZ would provide consistent and clear conditions for attracting investment and supporting regional competitiveness. This is essential both for the stable development of existing investors and for attracting new investors. The amendments provide that Liepāja SEZ companies will be able to conclude investment agreements until 31 December 2035 and apply direct tax relief until 31 December 2050. On 12 February of this year, the Saeima had already approved extending the operation of Liepāja SEZ until 31 December 2050. Liepāja SEZ companies may receive an 80% corporate income tax reduction on dividends and an 80% real estate tax reduction for investments made. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Under the Unified Industry Brand VIA LATVIA, Liepāja SEZ Authority Strengthens Existing Cooperation and Explores New Development Opportunities
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 25. jūnijs, 2026 Under the Unified Industry Brand VIA LATVIA, Liepāja SEZ Authority Strengthens Existing Cooperation and Explores New Development Opportunities To seek new cooperation partners, innovative solutions and development opportunities, Liepāja SEZ Deputy CEO Elans Strazdiņš and Head of the Business and Development Department Raivo Špaks attended Breakbulk Europe 2026 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, from 16 to 18 June. The exhibition is one of the world’s leading events for project cargo, bulk cargo and out-of-gauge logistics. For the fourth time, Latvian ports and industry companies participated under the shared industry brand VIA LATVIA. The exhibition is considered one of the most important networking and business development events in the global logistics sector. The event brought together more than 11,000 industry professionals from over 120 countries, including ports, shipping companies, logistics service providers, industrial manufacturers and infrastructure project developers. Key topics included heavy-lift and oversized cargo transportation, supply-chain digitalisation, sustainability and international cooperation. Was this information useful? Jā Nē 16.10.2026. title: Swedish Company Care of Sweden Opens a Manufacturing Facility in Liepāja
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Governance Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 14. maijs, 2024 Swedish Company Care of Sweden Opens a Manufacturing Facility in Liepāja Today, 14 May, Swedish company Care of Sweden officially opened its new manufacturing facility at the Old Harbour Business Park in Liepāja. The company has assembled a strong team of employees producing medical mattresses. Total investment amounts to approximately EUR 2 million. The Swedish company Care of Sweden has been manufacturing two types of mattresses for 25 years: medical preventive mattresses and electronically controlled medical mattresses. To bring production closer to raw-material manufacturers and suppliers, the company decided to establish a facility in the Baltic States and, after thorough research, chose Liepāja as its location. In spring 2023, Care of Sweden established a subsidiary in Latvia and signed a lease for 3,000 square metres of premises at the Old Harbour Business Park in Liepāja. The premises were built specifically for the company’s needs in less than a year. The Old Harbour Business Park is located within the Liepāja Special Economic Zone, relatively close to the city centre. More than 20 tenants, including Latvian and foreign-invested companies, already operate there. As noted above, Care of Sweden’s decision to establish a manufacturing facility in Liepāja demonstrates the quality of the business environment in Latvia and Liepāja, supported by the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, Liepāja City Municipality and the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority. Care of Sweden’s turnover reached EUR 21 million in 2023, and the company exports its products to approximately 35 countries worldwide. Australia is its largest export market. Why become a Liepaja SEZ Commercial Company The possibility to receive tax benefits - 80% for corporate income tax (dividends) and 80% for real estate tax, possibility to receive up to 60% of investment costs in tax benefits. The possibility to receive the status of a free zone and to apply the benefits of indirect tax and customs procedures. The opportunity to receive support, consultations and participation from the Liepāja SEZ administration and its cooperation partners in solving various issues. The opportunity to develop your business in a quality business environment. Preconditions to become the Liepaja SEZ Company Find out whether the type of business compliance with the requirements for of the Liepāja SEZ capital company. Prepares and submits documents for receiving the status of Liepaja SEZ capital company. The application of the company to obtain the status of the LSEZ Commercial Company shall be subject to the approval by the Board of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone. The company shall enter into an agreement with the Authority (for carrying out its commercial activity in the LSEZ territory), and into an agreement on implementation of its investment project. After the aforementioned approval has been received, the company shall then get re-registered with the Commercial Register of the Republic of Latvia, by adding the wording “Liepaja Special Economic Zone” to the current name of the respective company (firm). The same applies upon registration of a new company. The new company name shall appear in the Statutes and the Registration Certificate of such a company. Once the company has entered into the agreement with the Authority on carrying out its commercial activity in the LSEZ territory, the Authority shall issue a certificate on behalf of the government, affirming that the commercial company is eligible to apply the direct tax incentives, provided by the Law “On the Liepaja Special Economic Zone”, and the Law “On Application of Taxes in Free Ports and Special Economic Zones.” Liepaja SEZ Commercial Companies 47 number of LSEZ companies 2624 number of employees in LSEZ companies (in 2023) 4 252 844,78 € investments in construction and state-of-art technologies (in 2023) 14 659 977,89 € investments, made by the Liepaja SEZ companies, subject to tax incentives (in 2023) AE PARTNER Manufacturer of automation systems and production of electrical panels producer. title: Cruise Ships in Liepaja port
text: Invest in Liepaja Port About Port Ferry traffic Cruising Liepaja Marina Oskars Kalpaks bridge Commercial Companies Development projects Job vacancies Map of territories Cruising Despite that the Port of Liepaja has for many years been mainly recognized as a successful regional cargo transshipment center, the cruising interest has been recently growing, as well. Previously, thousands of tourists each year were arriving to visit the city by sea on board the Ro-Ro ferry on the route Liepaja – Travemunde (Germany), however, we are now looking further to welcome the city guests on board the cruise ships, as well! Today, the City of Liepaja may call itself a truly new cruise destination. The fun of a cruise is equal parts what you do on board and what you do on shore. No cruising experience is complete without a shore excursion – thus, on arrival, the cruise ships are moored alongside the berths in a direct vicinity of the port entrance, from where the tourists can get to the city center in a few minutes by bus or by car. The City of Liepaja offers guided walking or bus tours that allow tourists to experience the local history, culture, cuisine, shopping, to enjoy its landscaped parks, historical and contemporary architecture, the Blue Flag beach and much more. The city guests, preferring the military heritage tourism, are welcome to visit the largest historical military territory in the Baltics – part of the city area, named Karosta, which was built before World War I for the needs of the army. It is unique in the historical and architectural context not only in Latvia, but also the world. Cruise Ships in Liepaja port "Star Legend" The 159-metre-long Star Legend called at the Port of Liepaja on 19 July 2026, bringing 293 passengers to the city. "Silver Dawn" The 212-metre-long Silver Dawn visited the Port of Liepaja on 4 July 2026, arriving with 561 passengers on board. "Silver Spirit" The 211-metre-long Silver Spirit called at the port on 22 June 2026, bringing nearly 600 passengers to Liepaja. "World Traveller" The 126-metre-long cruise ship World Traveller entered the port in August 2025, bringing 170 passengers to Liepāja. "Nordstjernen" The historic vessel Nordstjernen entered the port twice in 2025. In July, the ship—built in 1956—brought 70 passengers to Liepāja from Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. In September, there were already 127 guests on board, including the Singing Men of Texas choir. The 80-metre-long Nordstjernen is a special ship, originally built for the needs of the Norwegian postal service. It was later restored and adapted for cruise voyages while preserving its original appearance. For this reason, Nordstjernen is included on Norway’s list of protected national cultural heritage sites. "Sirena" The 180-metre-long cruise ship Sirena was the second vessel of the cruise line Oceania Cruises to call at the Port of Liepaja on 5 September 2024, the ship brought 633 passengers to Latvia. "Insignia" The cruise ship Insignia entered the Port of Liepaja on 7 August 2024 with 639 passengers on board. The 180-metre-long ship was the first cruise liner to visit Liepaja in 2024. "Bolette" In 2023, only one cruise ship called at the Port of Liepaja. On 9 May, the 238-metre-long cruise ship Bolette brought 995 passengers and 629 crew members to Liepaja. The ship began its voyage in Antwerp (Belgium), then continued to Newcastle (United Kingdom), followed by Visby (Sweden), Tallinn (Estonia), and Riga. "Seven Seas Splendor" The cruise ship Seven Seas Splendor called at the Port of Liepaja twice in 2022. On 8 June, it brought 278 passengers, most of whom were travelers from the United Kingdom, while on 21 July it arrived with 690 passengers from the United States. The 224-metre-long ship visited Sweden, Denmark, Estonia, and Latvia during its cruise. "Balmoral" On 19 July 2022, the Fred. Olsen Cruise Lines vessel Balmoral called at the Port of Liepaja. Balmoral, carrying 667 passengers, was the third cruise ship to visit Liepāja in the summer of 2022. The cruise ship Balmoral began its voyage in Edinburgh. Although most of the passengers were residents of the United Kingdom, travelers from Japan, Australia, and other countries also had the opportunity to explore Liepaja. "Vasco Da Gama" The 219-metre-long cruise ship Vasco Da Gama called at the Port of Liepaja on 6 July 2022. Prior to that, it had visited ports in Norway, Sweden, Germany, and Denmark, before continuing to Riga. Sailing under the Portuguese flag, the cruise ship brought nearly a thousand passengers to Liepaja. "Saga Sapphire" After a break of more than ten years, a cruise ship once again called at the Port of Liepāja in 2018. On 17 August, the cruise ship Saga Sapphire brought 600 passengers. The 200-metre-long vessel began its journey around the Baltic Sea in Dover (United Kingdom), and Liepaja was one of six Baltic Sea ports at which the ship called. Was this information useful? Yes No

text: LSEZ Under the Law on the Liepāja Special Economic Zone, adopted on 17 February 1997, the Liepāja Special Economic Zone comprises the territory of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone, where companies of the Liepāja Special Economic Zone conduct business activities and which is administered and supervised by the Liepāja Special Economic Zone Authority. title: The bridge is open for shipping traffic 4 times a day
text: Invest in Liepaja Port About Port Ferry traffic Cruising Liepaja Marina Oskars Kalpaks bridge Commercial Companies Development projects Job vacancies Map of territories Oskars Kalpaks swing bridge The bridge is open for shipping traffic 4 times a day from 01:00 to 05:00 from 10:30 to 12:00 from 14:30 to 15:30 from 19:30 to 21:00 The time for shipping traffic is fixed, however, should the wind speed exceed 10m/s, or there are no ships scheduled, the bridge will be open for road traffic. Bridge history The bridge across the Karosta Canal bears the name of Oskars Kalpaks - Commander of 1st Latvian Independent Battalion, also known as “Kalpaks Battalion”, however, colloquially it is often called also as the Karosta Bridge. The unique and so far, the only swing bridge in Latvia was opened for traffic on 19 August 1906. The bridge was damaged during World War I and rebuilt soon after the War. In 1926, the steamship “Narne” accidentally crashed into the bridge and destroyed it seriously, and even though repaired, it underwent yet another deliberate damage by the Soviet Army during World War II. Before Latvia regained its independence, the territory of Karosta (War Port, as translated literally) was a closed military site, thus, the traffic over the bridge was controlled round the clock by the militaries. Crossing the bridge to Karosta was only possible with special permits for a few hours a day, the rest of the time the bridge was open to the traffic of Soviet warships. Interestingly, throughout the years of Soviet occupation, the name of the bridge was “The Red Army Bridge” and regained its current name only after Latvia became free. The bridge weighs 300 tons and has been construed in two separate parts (northern and southern) and consists of two identical cantilevers. The bridge carriageway is 7.3 meters wide, and the surface is made of wooden planks. The total length of the bridge is 133 meters. The height of the bridge above the water level is 8.32 meters. In the summer of 2006, the Georgian-flagged tanker “Anna” accidentally collided into the northern abutment of the bridge, and it was only after reconstruction, that Oskars Kalpaks Bridge was officially opened again for traffic in August 2009. text: Invest in Liepaja Port About Port Ferry traffic Cruising Liepaja Marina Oskars Kalpaks bridge Commercial Companies Development projects Job vacancies Map of territories Advantages Strategically advantageous location, non-freezing port Advantages Accessibility – seaport, airport, efficient road, and railway network Advantages Flexible business prerequisites Advantages Available development territories Advantages Efficient support tools for entrepreneurs Next Liepaja Port The Port of Liepāja is one of the most important transportation and transit arteries in the region, ensuring an efficient flow of cargo and connecting the Baltic States with global markets Port Profile Porta area 1 197 ha Maximum draught of ships 13.2 m Maximum breadth of ships 35 m Maximum length of ships 240 m Number of berths 47 Berths for bulk and general cargo 4 800 m Berths for liquid cargo 550 m Berths for fishing vessels, plesure boats and yachts 1 700 m Open cargo storage 545 000 m² Warehouses 160 000 m² Liquid cargo reservoirs 115 000 m 3 Silos 45 000 m 3 Winter Navigation According to the regulations of the Cabinet of Ministers, winter navigation in all Latvian ports begins on December 15 and ends on April 15. Winter navigation means that the shipowners are obliged to prepare their ships for safe navigation in negative air temperatures during such a period of time. Equipment for de-icing the ship's hull must be provided on board. The decision on starting ice navigation in the Port of Liepāja, as well as on the necessity of using icebreakers, is taken by the Liepaja Harbor Master, based on the operational situation in the waters of the port. The icebreaker service in the Port of Liepaja is provided by a commercial company, whereas the Harbor Master is responsible for the operational management of the icebreakers. Regulations for Yachts and small Vessels In order to organize safe navigation, it is recommended that small ships equipped with VHF radio station constantly provide radio communications on VHF channel 11. It should be noted that any vessel traffic participant who can safely navigate outside the main shipping lanes must not obstruct the movement of vessels along them. Movement of yachts and small vessels in the harbor must be done by not disturbing the vessels sailing along the fairway. When sailing in the waters of the Port of Liepaja, one must abide by the “Regulations for the Traffic of Vessels in Internal Waters” and the “Regulations of the Port of Liepaja”. Yacht, cutters or leisure boats are considered a small vessel if unless their length does not exceeds 24 meters. Navigation for yachts and leisure boats is permitted in the City Canal. The speed limit for small vessels in the City Canal is 5 knots (9 km/h). In the rest of the harbor area, there is no speed limit, under the condition, that the speed shall not not endanger other traffic participants, people, moored vessels and other floating or stationary structures, especially considering the influence of the waves created by the particular vessel. text: Governance Corporate governance Procurement and auctions Activity reports Board meeting decisions Activity reports Port statistics The Liepāja Special Economic Zone (Liepāja SEZ) Authority is a derivative public law legal entity established by the state and the municipality, operating under the supervision of the Cabinet of Ministers. The Liepāja SEZ Authority is the successor of the rights and obligations of the Liepāja Port Authority. The Liepāja SEZ Authority has a special budget, its own separate assets, and an official seal. The Liepāja SEZ Authority's structure consists of the Liepāja SEZ Board as the highest decision-making body and an executive apparatus, which is headed by the Liepāja SEZ CEO. The Board 3 Мembers representing the state 3 Members representing the Liepaja City Council 3 Members representing entrepreneurs in Liepaja Board Members Uldis Sesks Chairman of the Board Jānis Vilnītis Deputy Chairman of the Board Gunārs Ansiņš Board Member Edmunds Valantis Board Member Jolanta Plūme Board Member Juris Burņevskis Board Member Āris Ozoliņš Board Member Ilze Skrodele Board Member Functions approves the Development Plan of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone in accordance with the Law “On the Liepaja Special Economic Zone”, and interests of the government, municipality and society; enters into agreements with the Liepaja Special Economic Zone investors on investments and entrepreneurial activities in the territory of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone; enters into agreements with the Liepaja Special Economic Zone commercial companies on their entrepreneurial activities in the territory of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone; issues licenses to the Liepaja Special Economic Zone commercial companies enabling them to exercise tax incentives, as stipulated by the Law “On Application of Taxes in Free Ports and Special Economic Zones”; determines free zones and the borders, thereof, by coordinating conformity of such zones to the implementation of the free zone regime; enters into lease or sales agreements with regard to the land within the territory of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone, excluding sale of the land within the Port, as well as, such cases, where privatization of the land and other real estate within the territory of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone territory is carried out by other institutions; enters into agreements with commercial companies of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone on general transfer of certain executive functions to such companies within the sphere of services of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone, or within certain territory parts of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone; controls fulfilment of concluded agreements; approves prospective budget and the financial expenditure budget for the next year; appoints, manages and controls executive body of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone; title: Auction Announced for Property at Eksporta Street 3 in the Liepaja Industrial Park
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 06. october, 2026 Auction Announced for Property at Eksporta Street 3 in the Liepaja Industrial Park As the development of the Liepaja Industrial Park on the site of the former “Liepājas metalurgs” steelworks continues, the Liepaja Special Economic Zone (Liepaja SEZ) Authority has announced an auction for the property at Eksporta Street 3, located within the Liepaja Industrial Park. This is the next step in involving businesses in the regeneration and transformation of the industrial area, offering an opportunity to acquire existing production buildings together with the land. The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Authority is organizing an electronic ascending-bid auction for the newly created property at Eksporta Street 3, Liepaja. Auction property Address: Eksporta Street 3, Liepaja Land area: 51,521 m² Buildings: the plot contains buildings and structures, including warehouses of various sizes, a production workshop building, a workshop building and other structures Starting price: EUR 680,000.00 Bid increment: EUR 6,800.00 Security deposit: EUR 68,000.00 The following conditions apply to the auction: the building(s) must be renovated and/or reconstructed and the surrounding area improved within 60 (sixty) months from the date of signing the purchase agreement; the buildings must comply with the minimum energy-efficiency requirements established by the laws and regulations of the Republic of Latvia; minimum investment of EUR 733,076.85 (seven hundred and thirty-three thousand seventy-six euros and 85 cents) must be made in the auction property. The auction opens at 13:00 on 6 October 2026 and closes at 13:00 on 5 November 2026. Applicants may register for the auction from 13:00 on 6 October 2026 until 23:59 on 26 October 2026 on the electronic auction platform: izsoles.ta.gov.lv . The auction will be conducted electronically on izsoles.ta.gov.lv . The Liepaja SEZ Authority initially consolidated all the properties located on the site of the former steelworks, worked together with the municipality to develop a detailed local planning document for the area, and constructed the first roads with the necessary utility infrastructure. The disposal of properties through auctions is the next step in involving businesses in the regeneration and transformation of the industrial area, offering them the opportunity to acquire existing production buildings together with land and renovate and redevelop them in line with the requirements of a modern green economy business environment. The Liepaja Industrial Park is located within the territory of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone. It is a location for modern manufacturing facilities, science and research, logistics centers and the development of energy-intensive projects. The approximately 120-hectare development area has been divided into individual plots offering development opportunities and access to utility infrastructure. The Liepaja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepaja SEZ Authority and the Liepaja Municipality. The park borders Lake Liepaja, a specially protected nature area included in the NATURA 2000 network. According to the approved development strategy, the aim is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 new jobs. Sustainability is embedded in the “genetic code” of the Liepaja Industrial Park, with education, innovation and circular economy principles clearly established as its foundations. title: Decisions of the Liepaja SEZ Board of 25 September
text: Contact person Inese Matisone Head of the CEO’s Office Tālr: E-pasts: inese.matisone@lsez.lv 28. september, 2026 Decisions of the Liepaja SEZ Board of 25 September The regular meeting of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone (Liepaja SEZ) Board was held on 25 September, during which decisions were adopted at the conclusion of an investment agreement, the non-exercise of pre-emption rights, and the organization of an auction, as well as amendments to previously adopted decisions. The Liepaja SEZ Board also approved the updated Development Plan of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone for 2018-2035 and the Development Program of the Port of Liepaja for 2023-2027. Liepaja SEZ Development Plan updated The Liepaja SEZ Board has approved the updated Development Plan of the Liepaja Special Economic Zone for 2018–2035 and the Development Program of the Port of Liepaja for 2023-2027, adapting them to market changes, the geopolitical situation and new development priorities. As part of the update, the two planning documents have been consolidated into a single document. Previous development results have been assessed, the statistical database and regulatory framework have been updated, and new development priorities have been incorporated, including renewable and alternative energy projects. The Plan aims to strengthen Liepaja’s position as an industrial, logistics and energy hub by developing the Fore port area, offshore wind energy projects, NATO naval infrastructure and the Liepaja Industrial Park. The development of green economy projects has also been identified as a priority, including sustainable aviation fuel, hydrogen and CO₂ infrastructure solutions. The Liepaja SEZ Authority emphasizes that the updated Development Plan is an important prerequisite for the sustainable development of the port, industry and business environment, contributing to attracting investment and creating new jobs in the region. Liepaja SEZ companies investing in development The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board plans to conclude an investment agreement with Liepaja SEZ company Brimer for an investment of EUR 3.36 million in the construction of a new production and administrative building. The project is scheduled to be implemented from 1 October 2026 to 31 December 2028. The company qualifies as a medium-sized enterprise. The maximum applicable aid intensity for the planned project is 50%. Brimer Liepaja is a manufacturing company and part of the Norwegian Brimer Group, specializing in the development and manufacture of large-scale fiberglass composite products. The company provides a full range of services, from design and engineering solutions to product manufacturing, transportation and installation. The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board also decided to conclude an investment agreement with the company Jensen Metal for the investment project “Purchase of New Production Equipment.” The company plans to invest EUR 133,000 and implement the project from 30 September 2026 to 31 May 2027. The maximum applicable aid intensity for eligible costs is 40%. Paid services provided by the Port of Liepaja The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board has approved a price list for paid services, expanding the range of services available to port companies and other customers. The decision was taken in response to demand from port operators and other market participants, as well as the need to make more efficient use of the infrastructure and technical resources available to the Liepaja SEZ Authority. Going forward, the Liepaja SEZ Authority will provide multiple paid services that do not constitute the core functions of the port and are not financed through port charges. Customers will have access to hydrographic surveys, post-processing of hydrographic data, the use of specialized boats, treatment of oil-contaminated water and equipment rental. Service prices have been established based on detailed cost calculations and market analysis, ensuring full cost recovery while maintaining a competitive offering. The new price list will enter into force following its publication on the Liepaja SEZ Authority’s website. Electricity supply agreement The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board has approved the conclusion of an agreement with Enefit Ltd. for the supply of electricity from 1 November 2026 to 30 April 2027. Two bids were received in the procurement procedure, and the bid submitted by Enefit Ltd., with a tariff of EUR 155.73/MWh, was recognized as the most economically advantageous offer. The agreement will ensure the supply of electricity for the needs of the Liepaja SEZ Administration, as well as for the business activities of tenants operating in the Port of Liepaja and the Liepaja Industrial Park. The availability of electricity is an essential prerequisite for the uninterrupted operation and continued development of the port and industrial park. Repeated auction of the property at 6 Dūmu Street The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board has approved the terms of a repeated electronic auction for the property at 6 Dūmu Street, following the previous auction being declared unsuccessful due to an insufficient number of participants. The property is in the Liepaja Industrial Park and consists of a 46,766 m² land plot and a scrap metal processing complex with a total floor area of 25,181.7 m². The starting price for the repeated auction remains EUR 480,000, based on the valuation of the property carried out by LATIO Ltd. The disposal of the property is part of the development strategy for Liepaja Industrial Park, which aims to attract investment and promote the development of the area. The proceeds from the auction are planned to be used for the further development of the industrial park and to cover liabilities related to the disposal process. Pre-emption rights The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Board has decided not to exercise its pre-emption rights in respect of a 1.5-hectare land plot at 31A Cukura Street, Liepaja, located within the SEZ territory, as well as in respect of the properties at 6/9 Vecā Ostmala, 1 Fēniksa Street and 23 Jaunā Street, Liepaja. Having assessed the need for these properties, the Liepaja SEZ Authority concluded that they are not required for the performance of the Authority’s functions. Following completion of the transactions, the new owners plan to use the properties for the implementation of their respective business development projects. Was this information useful? title: Grain season gets off to a slower start at the Port of Liepaja this year
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 09. september, 2026 Grain season gets off to a slower start at the Port of Liepaja this year Stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepaja handled 341,830 tons of cargo in August 2026. Dry bulk cargo traditionally accounts for the largest share, with agricultural products, construction materials and wood chips totaling 188,160 tons. General cargo was the second-largest cargo group, accounting for 153,240 tons, of which 129,200 tons were transported on the regular Liepaja–Travemünde ferry service to Germany. Overall, the volume of cargo handled in August 2026 was below the average recorded for the same month in previous years. Year Grain handled in August, thousand tons 2026 84.1 2025 161.7 2024 184.7 2023 212.6 2022 217.2 *Grain volumes handled in August, thousand tons Liepaja remains an important hub for Latvian grain exports The Port of Liepaja has a long-standing focus on agricultural cargoes. Since the resumption of port operations in the 1990s, the port has deliberately developed its grain-handling infrastructure, with particular emphasis on locally sourced cargo. Approximately half of the cargo handled at the port is of Latvian origin, while the remainder is transit cargo. A key part of this activity is the export of grain grown by Latvian farmers to international markets. In early August 2026, grain terminals at the Port of Liepaja began accepting Latvian barley and wheat under previously concluded contracts. The terminals have a combined simultaneous grain storage capacity of approximately 730,000 tons. Liepaja Bulk Terminal, the port's largest dry bulk terminal, has signed one-year agreements with leading Latvian grain exporters, including Baltic Agro, Latraps and Linas Agro, covering the period from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. The terminal also works with international agricultural commodity companies, including Archer Daniels Midland (ADM). According to Juris Matvejevs, Chairman of the Board of Liepaja Bulk Terminal, the intake of Latvian grain is progressing more slowly this year than in previous seasons. The first shipment of Latvian wheat for export left the Port of Liepaja only on 6 September, when the Panamax-class vessel Tuo Fu 8, carrying 65,486.39 tons of grain, departed for Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. The terminal also handles cargo flows involving Central Asian markets, both for the export of agricultural products to the European Union and for the import of commodities such as Argentine soybeans and Brazilian sugar. Liepaja Bulk Terminal works with leading global agricultural commodity and logistics companies, including ADM (USA), one of the world's largest agricultural commodity traders and processors. ADM sources, stores and transports and agricultural commodities, connecting farmers with food, feed and industrial markets around the world. The Port of Liepaja's second-largest grain terminal, DanStore, was established in 1999 as a joint venture between the Danish companies Svane Shipping and Scanmills. In 2003, international agricultural commodity trader and processor Bunge became the company's strategic partner, supporting the development of the specialized dry bulk terminal. DanStore is also operating under contracts with several customers, including Latvian grain companies Baltic Agro and Agerona. At present, wheat grown by Latvian farmers is being loaded onto the Handysize-class vessel Jera, which will transport the cargo to Nigeria. Handling local cargo has always been a priority for stevedoring companies at the Port of Liepaja. At the same time, long-term cooperation with major international logistics and commodity companies helps ensure stable utilization of the port's cargo-handling capacity throughout the year. Approximately half of the cargo handled at the Port of Liepaja is Latvian cargo, while the other half consists of transit cargo. In recent years, considerable work has been carried out to develop transit cargo corridors connecting Liepaja with Central Asian markets. The development of these trade routes is particularly important for maintaining diversified cargo flows and making effective use of the port's infrastructure and handling capacity. Any restrictions on grain transit to third countries could have broader implications for global commodity markets. A reduction in the supply of grain to international markets could put upward pressure on global grain and food prices, potentially contributing to higher inflation in Europe, including Latvia, as well as globally. title: Liepaja Industrial Park Development Continues with Site Remediation
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 29. september, 2026 Liepaja Industrial Park Development Continues with Site Remediation The Liepaja Special Economic Zone Authority continues the transformation of the former steelworks “Liepajas metalurgs” industrial site by implementing the project “Development of the Liepaja Industrial Park Area – Phase 2.” The project involves redevelopment and remediation of a historically contaminated industrial site and construction of modern infrastructure required for business operations. The project is being implemented under the European Union Cohesion Policy Program 2021–2027, supporting the transition towards a climate-neutral economy and mitigating the socio-economic impacts associated with this transition in the Kurzeme region. Uldis Hmieļevskis, the Liepaja SEZ Authority CEO, explains that the development objective is to transform the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site into a modern industrial park, creating space for new business initiatives. Liepaja-based companies are growing and expanding, creating a need for new sites where manufacturing and logistics projects can be developed. The industrial park will provide space for business growth and help attract new investment to Liepaja. Uldis Hmieļevskis emphasizes that it is particularly encouraging to see companies with local capital identifying the Liepaja Industrial Park as a potential location for their manufacturing facilities. As part of the project, nine heavy fuel oil storage tanks with a total capacity of 60,000 cubic meters will be dismantled, while soil and groundwater remediation will be carried out in the area designated for the construction of one of the newly constructed streets of the Liepaja Industrial Park. Once the site has been remediated, modern utility infrastructure will be installed, including district heating, water supply, wastewater and stormwater drainage networks, two more streets will also be connected into a single integrated road network. The construction works are being carried out by SIA “A-Land”, under a contract signed on 28 August 2026 with a value of EUR 3.88 million excluding VAT. According to Dainis Kopštāls, Construction Manager at SIA “A-Land”, the project presents a particular challenge for the company, as site remediation must be carried out before the utility infrastructure and road section can be constructed. “Efficient project planning on the client’s side, combined with the professionalism of our partners, is enabling us to move forward according to schedule.” Construction supervision is provided by SIA “Firma L4”, design supervision by SIA “BM-Projekts”, while environmental consultancy services are provided by SIA “Ameco”. One of the most visible elements of the project will be the new roundabout at the intersection of two newly constructed streets. In recognition of the site’s industrial heritage, historic slag trolleys will be placed in the center of the roundabout, symbolically connecting the history of “Liepajas metalurgs” with the site’s new phase of development. The Liepaja Industrial Park has sustainable thinking embedded in its “genetic code”, with education, innovation and the circular economy clearly defined as its core principles. The site of the former “Liepajas metalurgs” plant is gradually being reintegrated into the city, making it accessible to the public and attractive to investors. The Liepaja Industrial Park is being developed by the Liepaja SEZ Authority and the Liepaja City Municipality, together with cooperation partners SIA “Liepajas ūdens” and SIA “Liepajas enerģija”, on the site of the former “Liepajas metalurgs” plant. The site borders Lake Liepaja, which is part of the specially protected natural area NATURA 2000. According to the approved development strategy, the aim is to attract more than EUR 275 million in private investment and create at least 1,500 new jobs. Real FDI magazine has highlighted 10 of the world’s most promising industrial and logistics investment projects, with the Liepaja Industrial Park included among them. In today’s competitive investment environment, locations that can offer more than land alone are increasingly attractive to investors – including modern infrastructure, energy security, logistics connectivity and an ecosystem suited to advanced manufacturing. The projects are in different countries and demonstrate a variety of development models, ranging from large industrial centers in Germany and Spain to emerging logistics hubs in Iceland, Romania, Latvia, the United Kingdom and Mexico. Background In 2018, a Memorandum of Understanding was signed between the Ministry of Economics, the Investment and Development Agency of Latvia (LIAA), SIA “FeLM”, the Liepaja City Council and the LSEZ Authority concerning the development of the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site. In 2019, the consolidation of real estate properties within the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site was initiated. In 2021, the development program for the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site was approved, and an inter-institutional agreement was concluded with the Liepaja City Council on its implementation. In 2022, the local plan for the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site was approved. In 2022, the program for the remediation of the former “Liepajas metalurgs” site was developed. In 2023, the Liepaja Industrial Park (LIP) Development Strategy 2023-2028 was approved. In 2023, several construction designs were developed for infrastructure development works at the site. In 2023, a project application was prepared and submitted for the first road construction works within the LIP area, and the Central Finance and Contracting Agency (CFLA) issued a decision approving funding for the works. In 2023, a lease agreement was concluded with SIA “Liepajas Steel”, valid until 31 December 2025, for the dismantling and removal of an electric steelmaking furnace. In autumn 2024, construction of the first road sections and utility infrastructure was launched, together with the electrification of the entire site. In 2025, the disposal of existing industrial buildings was initiated. At the end of 2025, road sections of three newly constructed streets were completed, commissioned and opened to public access, together with utility infrastructure, including water supply, wastewater and stormwater drainage, and district heating networks. As part of the project, 3,865 meters of electricity distribution networks and eight new transformer substations were also constructed across extensive sites. In September 2026, the CFLA-approved project “Development of the Liepaja Industrial Park Area – Phase 2” was launched. The project includes dismantling of the heavy fuel oil storage facilities, site remediation, and the construction of road into a single integrated road network. Was this information useful? text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 21. september, 2026 Liepaja Industrial Park Named Among the World’s Top 10 Most Attractive Industrial and Logistics Investment Projects The latest edition of Real FDI ongoing publication series highlighting the most attractive investment projects across regions and sectors has revealed its 2026 Top 10. In today’s increasingly competitive investment landscape, locations that can offer not only land, but also modern infrastructure, energy security, logistics connectivity and an ecosystem suited to advanced manufacturing are becoming increasingly attractive to investors. The Liepaja Industrial Park has been recognized as one of the most promising projects in Europe and included in the Top 10. The projects selected by Real FDI reflect the diversity and scale of today’s investment opportunities. They range from major ports and established industrial districts to brownfield regeneration projects and airport-linked logistics hubs. As noted by Real FDI, these projects demonstrate how connectivity, infrastructure, available land and increasingly sophisticated industrial ecosystems are shaping the next generation of investment destinations. “Countries are no longer competing solely to attract investment, but also on their ability to provide investors with the industrial infrastructure they need.” Real FDI has highlighted 10 of the world’s most promising industrial and logistics investment projects. Located across a range of countries, the projects showcase different development models – from major industrial centers in Germany and Spain to emerging logistics hubs in Iceland, Romania, Latvia, the United Kingdom and Mexico. Attention is given to the Liepaja Industrial Park, whose “DNA” is built around a sustainable approach, with education, innovation and circular economy principles clearly embedded in its development concept. The former Liepajas Metalurgs (steelworks) industrial site is gradually being reintegrated into the city, opening it up to the public while making it increasingly attractive to investors. title: Port of Liepaja Continues Handling Grain Grown by Latvian Farmers
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 02. september, 2026 Port of Liepaja Continues Handling Grain Grown by Latvian Farmers Liepaja Bulk Terminal - the largest dry bulk terminal at the Port of Liepaja, has signed agreements with the leading Latvian grain exporters, including Baltic Agro, LATRAPS and Linas Agro, for handling grain grown by Latvian farmers from 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027. The terminal is currently loading locally grown wheat onto a Panamax-class vessel TUO FU 8, which is set to take on more than 60,000 tons of grain. The vessel’s destination is Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. DanStore, the second largest grain terminal at the Port of Liepaja, is also operating in accordance with its agreements. According to the terminal’s management, storage capacity is currently available, as deliveries of the new harvest are progressing relatively slowly. Unlike previous years, when long queues of trucks would form outside the terminal during this period, no such situation has been observed this year. The company suggests that some Latvian grain growers may be holding back their produce in anticipation of more favorable sales conditions and higher prices. Grain prices currently range between EUR 250 and EUR 260 per ton, representing one of the highest levels seen in recent years. In the coming days, DanStore expects a vessel that is scheduled to load approximately 27,000 tons of Latvian grain supplied by Baltic Agro. The cargo will be shipped to Nigeria. Latvian grain arrives at the Port of Liepaja not only by road but also by rail. On 2 September, the Liepaja Bulk Terminal received a train consisting of 26 wagons carrying 1,820 tons of grain supplied by Baltic Agro. Another 26-wagon train from the LATRAPS cooperative is expected to arrive shortly. Throughout its history, and particularly since operations resumed in the 1990s, the Port of Liepaja has focused on developing the handling of agricultural cargo, with particular emphasis on grain terminals and the handling of locally sourced cargo. The export of Latvian-grown grain to global markets plays an important role in the port’s overall cargo flows. Several agricultural cargo terminals currently operate at the Port of Liepaja, with a combined annual handling capacity of approximately 5 million tons. Their total storage capacity for grain at any one time is approximately 730,000 tons. The grain terminals at the Port of Liepaja cooperate with Latvian and international companies involved in the procurement, storage and distribution of grain to global food supply chains. All cargo operations at the Port of Liepaja, including the handling of grain in transit, are carried out in accordance with the applicable regulatory requirements of the European Union and the European Commission. title: Port Services in the Port of Liepaja Become More Accessible
text: 04. september, 2026 Port Services in the Port of Liepaja Become More Accessible The Liepaja SEZ Authority, in cooperation with the Freeport of Riga Authority and the Freeport of Ventspils Authority, has completed the most ambitious Latvian port cooperation project to date in the field of digitalization. The newly developed Port and Multimodal Logistics Services Platform brings together information on vessel visits, berths, port services, permits, passes, contracts and payments in one place. It also enables users to track vessel movements in real time and use digital maps containing port infrastructure data. For customers and services at the Port of Liepaja, this means: faster exchange of information and data; fewer manual tasks and less duplicate data entry; more convenient communication and process coordination. The platform is integrated with the State Joint Stock Company “Latvian Railways”, SKLOIS and other national and port information systems, laying the foundation for a unified digital ecosystem for Latvian ports. The project was implemented from December 2024 to August 2026. It was funded with EUR 3.24 million from the European Union Recovery Fund. Was this information useful? Yes No 16.10.2026. title: Seven Cruise Ships, 4,276 Visitors and Growing Demand: Liepaja Strengthens Its Position on the Baltic Cruise Map
text: Contact person Līga Ratniece-Kadeģe Communications and Corporate Management Specialist Tālr: (+371) 29233446 E-pasts: liga.ratniece-kadege@lsez.lv 04. september, 2026 Seven Cruise Ships, 4,276 Visitors and Growing Demand: Liepaja Strengthens Its Position on the Baltic Cruise Map Liepaja is steadily strengthening its position as a Baltic Sea cruise destination, with the 2026 season marking a new milestone for the city. A record seven cruise ships called at the Port of Liepaja this year, bringing 4,276 passengers to the city. With 11 cruise ship calls already scheduled for 2027, Liepaja is continuing to build momentum as an attractive destination on the Baltic cruise itineraries. During the 2026 season, 86 organized excursions were arranged for cruise passengers, attracting 2,244 visitors, or 52.5% of all cruise passengers arriving in Liepaja. The excursions offered visitors the opportunity to discover the city’s rich cultural and historical heritage, as well as its distinctive tourism attractions. Other passengers explored Liepaja independently, with shuttle buses running every 30 minutes between the port and the city center. From Returning Cruise Calls to Long-Term Growth Cruise ship calls to the Port of Liepaja resumed in 2018 after a longer break, following targeted efforts by the Liepaja Special Economic Zone (SEZ) Authority and the municipality to establish Liepaja on international cruise itineraries. “Liepaja has already secured its place on the Baltic cruise map. Our next priority is to consolidate this achievement and continue growing,” says Uldis Hmieļevskis, Liepaja SEZ CEO . “Our long-term ambition is to welcome more than 20 cruise ships during a single season. This would open new opportunities for local businesses to develop a broader range of services and experiences for international visitors, while further strengthening Liepaja’s role as a cruise destination in the Baltic Sea region.” Cruise Tourism Delivering for the Local Economy Cruise passengers and crew contribute to the local economy by using transport, hospitality, tourism, cultural and entertainment services, while also visiting shops, museums and other attractions. Based on estimates commonly used across the international cruise industry, an average cruise passenger spends approximately €70–€100 at a destination. On this basis, the direct economic contribution generated by cruise passengers visiting Liepaja during the 2026 season could exceed €400,000. However, the value of cruise tourism extends well beyond direct visitor spending. “A cruise ship in the port is much more than just a ship at the quay. It is an opportunity for thousands of people to discover Liepaja - its culture, history, business environment and hospitality,” says Hmieļevskis. “Every visitor who leaves Liepaja with a positive impression becomes an ambassador for our city around the world. At the same time, cruise tourism creates real economic opportunities for local businesses, drives demand for services and helps strengthen Liepaja’s competitiveness across the Baltic Sea region.” A Compact Port, a Diverse Destination One of Liepaja’s key advantages as a cruise destination is the proximity of the port to the city center. Within minutes of stepping ashore, visitors can explore Liepaja’s historic centre, the Great Amber Concert Hall, the unique Karosta district, Seaside Park, the beach, museums, cafés and a wide range of other attractions. This compact geography allows cruise passengers to make the most of even a relatively short port call — whether by joining an organised excursion or discovering the city at their own pace. Cruise visits also play an important role in strengthening Liepaja’s international visibility. Every ship brings hundreds or even thousands of potential new ambassadors to the city, helping to showcase Liepaja as a modern, welcoming and distinctive destination on the Baltic Sea coast. The attraction and reception of cruise ships is supported through close cooperation between the Liepaja SEZ Authority, the Liepaja Region Tourism Information Office, and the ship agencies RCA and ESTMA. With seven cruise ships welcomed in 2026 and 11 visits already scheduled for 2027, Liepaja’s cruise sector is entering its next stage of development - turning growing international interest into long-term opportunities for the city, its businesses and its visitors.
